News.title: The bizarre Arctic town where dying is BANNED, mums pack shotguns for the school run & cats are strictly outlawed
News.content:
GRAVE MISTAKE The bizarre Arctic town where dying is BANNED, mums pack shotguns for the school run & cats are strictly outlawed







Next

A REMOTE Arctic town has gained a bizarre reputation as one of the few places on Earth where dying is banned – despite bloodthirsty polar bears roaming on people’s doorsteps.

For the hardy residents of Longyearbyen, life comes with an unusual rulebook, where cats are outlawed, mums carry shotguns on walks with their children and the sun disappears for months on end.



Perched on the frozen fringes of Norway’s Svalbard archipelago, Longyearbyen is a place which has kept ahold of its Arctic roots.

Around 2,500 people call this icy outpost home, having traded the comforts of conventional living for a life dictated by the icy wilderness.



Stranded some 800 miles from the North Pole, the settlement is among the northernmost permanent communities on Earth.

Its brightly coloured wooden houses huddle beneath towering mountains, bringing a splash of colour to a landscape otherwise dominated by snow and ice.

But the cheerful facades offer little protection from the peculiar realities of life in one of the planet’s most unforgiving environments.

For several months each winter, the sun disappears entirely, plunging the settlement into a seemingly endless darkness.



Temperatures can plummet below -20C, while bitter winds tear through the valley.

Yet its residents remain at the mercy of conditions that would make the average British winter seem positively tropical.

Polar bears roam the surrounding wilderness, making encounters with the enormous predators a genuine danger for anyone straying too far from safety.



Residents travelling outside the settlement are advised to carry suitable protection, with firearms a familiar sight among those heading into the Arctic wilderness.

Even parents taking their children outdoors can find themselves armed against an animal capable of turning an ordinary stroll into a fight for survival.

But while polar bears are free to roam, the humble house cat has been given a considerably frostier reception.

Cats are generally prohibited in Longyearbyen over concerns about the threat they pose to the islands’ vulnerable wildlife.

Dogs, however, have managed to secure themselves a much more friendly welcome.



Huskies and other hardy breeds remain a familiar sight, with dog sledding continuing to play an important role in Svalbard’s culture and tourism industry.

Teams of powerful dogs haul sleds across the frozen terrain, preserving a centuries-old means of travelling through a landscape where conventional transport can prove useless.

Reindeer also wander through the settlement, apparently unfazed by the unusual human neighbours who have made their home in the wilderness.

Founded in 1906 by American businessman John Munro Longyear, the town began life as a coal-mining settlement.

Workers were drawn to the remote outpost by the promise of decent wages, despite having to endure some of the harshest conditions imaginable.



More than a century later, the former mining town has reinvented itself as an unlikely holiday hotspot.

Restaurants, hotels and a university centre now sit among the colourful buildings, offering a surprisingly modern existence at the edge of civilisation.

But despite its icy atmosphere and isolation, Longyearbyen has not escaped the increasingly heated ambitions of Vladimir Putin.



The Russian tyrant has been accused of eyeing the Norwegian archipelago for a potential land grab, with fears his polar objectives could trigger a wider conflict with Nato.

European security expert Anthony Glees previously told The Sun: “Putin is looking like Hitler did a hundred years ago, all the time looking for areas of Europe.”

Yet for all the dangers lurking beyond its borders, Longyearbyen’s most famous peculiarity concerns what happens when life comes to an end.

For decades, Longyearbyen has been described as the town where dying is forbidden.

It is a claim that has travelled far beyond Svalbard, turning the remote settlement into the subject of one of the world’s strangest urban legends.



But the truth is more complicated – and arguably more unsettling.

Death itself is strictly legal but authorities have restricted burying the dead.

The problem is the permafrost beneath Longyearbyen, which keeps the ground frozen for prolonged periods, dramatically slows down decomposition.

In ordinary cemeteries, the earth gradually reclaims what has been buried.

Here, bodies can remain preserved for decades, while changes in the frozen ground can cause coffins to shift towards the surface.



The result is a rather macabre predicament for a town that already has enough trouble dealing with the living.

Traditional coffin burials have been prohibited since 1950, meaning anyone hoping for a conventional final resting place must look beyond the settlement.

Cremated remains can still be buried in the local cemetery under certain conditions.



But the Arctic’s ability to preserve the dead has attracted interest from scientists as well as curious tourists who arrive in their flocks of thousands each year.

In the late 1990s, researchers travelled to Svalbard to examine the remains of victims of the devastating 1918 influenza pandemic.

They hoped the frozen ground might have preserved traces of the virus that killed millions of people worldwide.

And while Longyearbyen’s dead have proved a source of scientific fascination, its living residents have plenty of unusual challenges of their own.

During the depths of winter, residents can go for months without seeing the sun rise above the horizon.



Morning commutes take place in darkness, while the town’s brightly lit buildings provide welcome patches of colour against the frozen landscape.

Even lunchtime offers no guarantee of daylight, with the sun remaining stubbornly out of sight.

But the prolonged darkness does come with one spectacular advantage.

The Northern Lights can appear overhead at almost any hour, sending shimmering curtains of green across the Arctic sky.



It is a breathtaking spectacle that draws visitors from around the world, many prepared to brave the bitter cold for a glimpse of nature’s finest light show.

And just as residents grow accustomed to living without sunshine, the Arctic swings to the opposite extreme.

From roughly April until August, Longyearbyen experiences the midnight sun, when daylight continues around the clock.

The sun refuses to dip below the horizon, leaving residents with the problem of trying to sleep while the world outside remains brilliantly lit.



And while the rest of Europe settles down for the night, Longyearbyen’s residents can enjoy outdoor activities beneath a sun that appears to have forgotten when to clock off.

For modern residents, however, the practical implications of living in such an isolated place extend well beyond funerals.

Longyearbyen has a hospital, but patients requiring specialist treatment must be transferred to mainland Norway.

Pregnant women generally make the journey south before giving birth because the town lacks a fully equipped maternity service.

And if residents fancy a drink after navigating the peculiarities of Arctic life, even that comes with a rulebook.



The settlement maintains an unusual alcohol quota system dating back to its days as a remote coal-mining community.

Residents have traditionally been issued alcohol cards restricting how much beer and certain spirits they can purchase each month.

The system was introduced to regulate drinking among miners living in isolation, with elements of the restrictions surviving long after the industry began to decline.

News.title: Teen girl left with serious brain damage after being flung out of car sunroof as driver made sharp turn in parking lot
News.content:
HORROR STUNT Teen girl left with serious brain damage after being flung out of car sunroof as driver made sharp turn in parking lot







Next

A SCHOOLGIRL has suffered a severe brain injury after she was flung from a car’s sunroof during a high-octane stunt.

Elexis Robinson, 17, was hanging out of the roof of the vehicle as it drove around a car park in Vancouver, Washington.



When the car’s teen driver made a sharp turn, Elexis was thrown head-first onto the pavement and suffered an instant skull fracture.

She has also had three near-fatal brain bleeds that have left her with difficulty remembering her own name.



Elexis is now in hospital recovering from a severe traumatic brain injury after the November 3 incident.

Her heartbroken mum, Alicha Linares, said has turned the family’s world “upside down”.



She told KGW8 that her daughter sleeps most of the day, and wakes up confused, emotional and disoriented.

Elexis, an honours student who was close to graduating high school, now struggles to remember basic information.

“As a mother, there are no words to describe the fear, heartbreak, and helplessness of watching your child endure something so devastating,” Alicha wrote on a GoFundMe page.

“In a matter of moments, our entire world was turned upside down.



“The daughter we love so dearly is now facing an unimaginable medical battle, and our family is desperately hoping, praying, and holding onto every bit of hope for her recovery.”

Elexis’ family now face an anxious wait, with doctors saying it could be up to a year until they get a clearer picture of her recovery.

Alicha said: “We’re kind of left in the dark of what’s going to happen.”

Thrill seekers frequent the car park where the tragedy occurred, with skid marks seen all over the lot.

Alicha said: “She is the one out of my six that I would trust her with my life. I would trust every decision she would make.



“I was shocked. I would have never expected anything like this of her, ever.”

Alicha believed her daughter was influenced by a new friendship that led her to behave out of character.

She said she had told Elexis not to spend time with the girl, whom she had only known since last year.

However, the distraught mum felt conflicted about whether the driver should be punished.

She said: “This girl also made a mistake, too. This is her choice, just as much as it was my daughter’s choice to make a mistake.



“I want her to learn the consequences of this, but she is a 17-year-old girl as well, and to have her life completely ruined and destroyed, I don’t need two lives like that.”

Charges have not been filed against the girl driving the car, according to local media.

Alicha said the incident was a reminder that things can go around very quickly if people aren’t careful.

“It’s upsetting. I know what it’s like to be a kid,” she said.

“I know what it’s like to want to have fun, to enjoy life, but as a mom, older now, learning from the experiences, I would never, ever wish this on a parent.”



“I would never wish kids think that they’re invincible and can do whatever they want because life can change in an instant. Life was almost over for her.”

A GoFundMe page has been set up to ease the “overwhelming financial burdens” of Elexis’ medical care and rehabilitation.

Alicha wrote: “Elexis is so much more than this tragedy.

“She is an incredibly intelligent, beautiful, and kindhearted young woman who has worked so hard throughout high school and is on track to graduate with honors.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“She has an entire future ahead of her, dreams waiting to be fulfilled, and so much life left to live.



“She is deeply loved, and we are determined to stand beside her through every step of this journey.”

News.title: Inside Ukraine’s new underground battlefield as troops dodge ‘kill zones’ & fight in labyrinth of Soviet-era pipelines
News.content:
Next

UKRAINE’S frontline has become an underground battlefield – with soldiers networking through a labyrinth of tunnels to avoid being spotted by drones.

Kyiv‘s forces have also employed guerrilla warfare tactics to fend off Russian troops in a “Vietnam-style” forest, an expert said.



With deadly drone “kill zones” wiping out anything moving above ground, soldiers on both sides are taking the war deep into a dormant Soviet-era gas pipeline network.

Troops are zipping through more than 50 subterranean steel pipes – some barely wide enough to crawl through – on electric buggies to ambush each other with machine guns and RPGs.



War reporter Caolan Robertson told The Sun: “There is an entire subterranean, underground network system that’s been forming in the last few months.

“It looks like the London Tube if you see some of these videos coming out.

“And that’s because the entire war is almost moving underground everywhere you go closer to the frontline.”

In the spring of 2025, Russian troops used them to sneak behind Ukrainian lines and stage a series of surprise attacks.



A Ukrainian commander told The Atlantic of the terrifying subterranean raids: “They kept climbing out of the earth like devils.”

He also told how troops were forced to play a deadly game of whack-a-mole as Russian forces kept popping up during the assault.

Robertson said the tunnel phenomenon is bound to be replicated in other conflicts because of the prominence of drones.



“Everything that moves, everything that moves in Kramatorsk and on the Russian side is being seen and watched,” Robertson said.

“If you go towards Kupyansk, there’s an entire underground operation that’s just taken place.”

“You see these soldiers going through tunnels at very, very high speeds, very high speed, using these underground systems, digging underground systems to hide from the drones or to fortify from the enemy.



“It’s a really rapidly developing thing, and that’s because these drones are taking over everything.”

Russia, which today was reported to have lost 450,000 troops so far in the war according to a Kremlin data leak, has also been facing Ukraine’s guerrilla warfare tactics in a “Vietnam-like” forest, Robertson said.

Following Russia‘s destruction of the Nova Kakhovka Dam in Zaporizhia in 2023, a new ecosystem has sprung up across one area in the frontline.

Trees and bushes have grown from where a huge body of water was left completely drained by a blast three years ago.



“Something entirely new has just sprung up almost out of nowhere on the frontlines of Ukraine here and it looks almost like a tropical rainforest, Vietnam-style, and it’s happening right down here in Zaporizhia.”

Putin’s troops saw it as an opportunity to sneak in and take hardened positions within the natural fortress.

But Ukrainian soldiers were lying in wait, already prepared to take out invading forces using guerrilla warfare-style tactics.

He explained: “The Ukrainian soldiers were ready and waiting for this infiltration, waiting for the Russians in this forest.



“And they took them all out or they took them as prisoners of war.”

The expert laid out how the now drained reservoir was once a pivotal line between both sides in the war – but has now taken on a new form.

He added: “It’s kind of a fascinating concept, really…

“The idea that when something like a mountain or a river or a moat would form a front line.”

It comes as Putin continues to suffer huge losses as his war machine staggers on towards the fifth year of fighting.



Russia is reportedly signing up between 1,000 and 1,200 new recruits every day in a desperate bid to keep its invasion running.

On Saturday Putin’s forces struck a kindergarten and a key bridge in Kyiv in the tyrant’s latest evil night of strikes on war-ravaged Ukraine.

A 14-year-old girl was among at least nine injured as a wave of hypersonic and ballistic rockets rained down on the capital.

Just days earlier the tyrant bombed a school which had turned into a humanitarian centre in one of the worst horrors of the war.

At least 55 people were killed in the sickening attack including two rescue workers and four police officers.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Peace talks have been scheduled for this week between Ukrainian, Russian and US officials – the first of their kind in nearly one year.

They are being held in the United Arab Emirates and are set to last for two days.

News.title: Evil husband, 79, who stabbed his wife, 84, of 50 years to death in bed at their home is jailed for life
News.content:
BEHIND BARS Evil husband, 79, who stabbed his wife, 84, of 50 years to death in bed at their home is jailed for life







Next

AN EVIL husband who stabbed his wife of 50 years to death in bed after subjecting her to years of violence has been jailed for life.

Michael Pyke, 79, murdered Beryl Puke at their home in Aldwick, West Sussex, in May last year.



The former hairdresser was sentenced to life imprisonment, with a minimum of 15 years, on Friday at Hove Crown Court.

Pyke was described as a “happy family man” with no previous convictions until he turned 60 and began offending.



Sentencing him, Judge Jeremy Gold KC detailed the “terrifying and sustained attack” on his “defenceless wife”.

He added that the last decades of his marriage had been tarnished with regular incidents of domestic abuse and violence.

“I have no doubt from the number of times you stabbed Beryl it was your intention to kill her and you did so showing no mercy,” the judge said.

The father-of-two served several stints behind bars prior to his final conviction, many relating to domestic violence towards Beryl.

The court heard how he had confessed to his cousin that he’d murdered his wife after she told him to “f*** off” when he asked for a cuddle.

Pyke then grabbed a kitchen knife and stabbed her multiple times as she lay helpless in bed.



They had previously spent the evening at a friend’s house together on the night of May 30 and he horrifying murder took place between 10.30pm and 2pm on May 31.

Pyke, who was said to drink a litre of vodka and cider a day, called his cousin Roger Taylor and told him about the horror that had unfolded.

After Roger dialled 999, police found Pyke sitting calmly by the TV downstairs, as they discovered Beryl in her nightgown, covered in blood.

Prosecuting, Pippa McAtasney KC outlined Pyke’s 47 convictions for 80 offences which occured between 2008 and 2022.

These included 13 incidents of vioelnce, five counts of assault on emergency workers and 26 for breaching restraining orders against Beryl.



He had served time for stabbing a friend and neighbour who walked past Beryl’s home in July 2007, after she had gone inside to escape Pyke’s drinking.

The victim, who survived the vicious attack, told cops Pyke’s violence towards his wife appeared to “coincide” with his retirement and drinking.

Ms McAtasney said his offending reveals an “extensive history of domestic violence against his wife”.

“A pattern emerges that often the defendant would drink, become aggressive and or violent towards Beryl,” the barrister said.

“She would call the police and he would be in breach of his restraining order.



“On many occasions Beryl did not support the allegations. She would feel sorry for him and didn’t want him to be homeless.”

Following his arrest, bodycam footage shows him saying “F*** this life, I want to die.”

And, “Dead forever, dead forever, thank f****** god for that”.

Forensic teams found Pyke had showered and attempted to clean up after the murder.

Cops found a polo shirt ditched in the laundry basket and a blood-stained knife by the bed, believed to be the main murder weapon.



A post-mortem revealed Beryl had been subjected to 11 stab wounds, inflicted by an 8cm blade, with defensive injuries also visible, suggesting she had anticipated the blow.

The couple’s son sat in the court with his wife but did not share a victim statement.

Instead, it was heard that “they cannot put into words the impact this had on the family” and that anything they wanted to say would be said in private.

Defending Pyke, Martin Rutherford KC said a “really bizarre” feature is that throughout his adult life until turning 60 he was a “happy family man with no previous convictions recorded against him”.

“Matters turned post-60, largely chronicled in the criminal record.



“Woven within that, a tale of homelessness interspersed with destructive and self-destructive periods of time living with his wife.”

Pyke, who had been a long-term “teetotaler” had become drawn and “perhaps addicted” to alcohol.

Following the sentencing, Sussex Police Detective Sergeant Elliott Lander said Pyke “cruelly” took Beryl’s life in the home they shared.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“While in police custody, he made a number of comments which indicated his responsibility for what had happened, showing no remorse and a nonchalant attitude towards the devastating consequences of his actions,” he said.

“Nothing can undo the devastation caused by Beryl’s death, but now sentencing has taken place, we hope her family, friends and all those who knew and loved her can take some comfort in knowing the man responsible will likely spend the rest of his life behind bars.”

News.title: Elite technical colleges must return to tackle Britain’s youth unemployment crisis, Suella Braverman demands
News.content:
Next

SUELLA Braverman has called for the return of top technical colleges to get Britain’s jobless youngsters off the dole and into skilled work.

The former Home Secretary urged Labour grandee Alan Milburn to overhaul Britain’s education system in an open letter ahead of his review into youth unemployment next week.



The Reform UK’s education spokeswoman warned schools were failing teenagers who would rather fix cars or cut hair than go to university.

She wrote: “If you are very academic, the school system is failing you and dumbing you down. If you are good with your hands, school is failing you. If you want to go into a technical or vocational career, school is not built for you.”



She called for a “radical change to the system” that works for “not just those who went to Oxbridge to study PPE”.

Her ten-point plan would create a new elite network of technical colleges to equip youngsters with practical skills and prepare them for jobs protected from AI.

She also demanded a major expansion of apprenticeships, with taxpayers covering 30 per cent of wages for trainees aged 16 to 18.

Mrs Braverman told Mr Milburn: “We at Reform UK are ready to support you and to consign the academic snobbery and elitism of the establishment to the dustbin of history.”

News.title: Shock moment forklift is engulfed by flames and explodes in fireball at Russian plant – as driver suffers horror burns
News.content:
Next

THIS is the dramatic moment a forklift explodes into a fireball at a remote Russian aluminium plant, leaving its driver with horror burns.

Shocking CCTV footage shows the huge blast with factory appearing completely engulfed in flames.



The heavy machinery can be seen moving slowly across the factory floor before a bright fire ignites behind it.

Heavy smoke then starts to plume from the forklift.





At first the fire appears to be small.

But the forklift suddenly bursts into flames and explodes, sending bright sparks across the factory floor.

Smoke is sent in all directions, before a second fiery blast fills the screen and the camera cuts out.

The terrifying explosion blew up production workshops at the Bratsk Aluminium Plant in Irkutsk, Siberia on Wednesday.



The forklift driver suffered burns to 17 per cent of his body, a statement from the plant said.

He was rushed to hospital for treatment after miraculously surviving the explosion.

Conflicting reports had claimed he suffered burns to 85 per cent of his body, but officials said the worker had managed to escape the forklift before the blast.



Preliminary reports suggest the fire was caused by an electrical fault.

Firefighters battled the blaze at the factory for around an hour.

It comes after a monstrous explosion ripped through a factory in Brazil, leaving at least 12 people injured.

Terrifying footage showed a massive fireball engulfing the chemical plant, sparking urgent evacuations of nearby homes.

The fiery blast went off at the Pyrozzar factory in Salto, São Paulo, on Friday morning.



Several people can be seen walking away from the inferno in astonishing video.

Moments later, it erupts into an apocalyptic fireball, sending plumes of thick smoke billowing into the sky at breakneck pace.

Gobsmacked bystanders are seen running for their lives as the flames continue to grow larger by the second.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Other staggering clips showed the vicious flames shooting up from the site of the horror.

The 12 injured victims included one of the company owners, military police officers, firefighters and civilians.

News.title: Dangerous children’s toy sold on Amazon urgently recalled over ‘serious’ asphyxiation fears
News.content:
Next

A POPULAR children’s toy has been urgently recalled due to fears it presents a serious risk of asphyxiation.

The product was sold on Amazon and could be used for sensory play or arts and crafts.

Jacisk 200Pcs Giant Water Beads have been recalled over fears the product presents a “serious risk of asphyxiation”.



An update from the Office for Product Safety and Standards, said: “The product presents a serious risk of asphyxiation because if the product is swallowed in its hydrated form, it can block a young child’s airway.”



The product has been withdrawn from the market and recalled by Amazon.

Owners of this product are being advised to “stop using it immediately”.

You can reach out to Amazon for a replacement or refund.

It comes just days after Baxters recalled their Chef Selections Cullen Skink soup due to a fault which could cause “spoilage of the product” and risk of cans “to swell and potentially rupture”.

The affected product has the batch code L07XC and best before date of April 2029.

Decathlon has also recalled HAMAX Buddy Baby Seat as the label attached to it presents a “risk of choking”.

Plus, the SMILE III, SMILE 4 and SMILE 5Z pushchairs have all been recalled by Britax Römer.

News.title: Inside Jonathan Ross’ ‘very close’ friendship with Brand & Walliams as star ‘horrified’ by revelations
News.content:
Next

DAVID Walliams threw his head back and laughed. On stage at the 2004 British Comedy Awards, Jonathan Ross had just pointed out that the show was 15 years old.

Like most 15-year-olds, he joked, it was drunk, unpredictable and “probably going home with David Walliams”.



A girl the Guardian calls Alex remembers watching from her bedroom. She’d met Walliams at a Little Britain fan event when she was 15. By the time the awards went out, she says, he had already called her and sent her a postcard wishing her luck in her exams.

Alex told ITV News and the Guardian that Walliams later asked her for sexualised photographs and that they first had sex when she was 17.



She said the sex was consensual but she felt he had used his fame to take advantage of her. Another woman, called Jade in the investigation, said Walliams kissed and sexually touched her when she was 15. Walliams denies wrongdoing.

The allegations were published a day after Russell Brand was jailed for ten and a half years for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others.

Read more on Brand HOME LOAN Jonathan Ross let Brand stay in holiday home unaware of attack accusations

For years, the three men turned up in the same places. They were all on Channel 4’s Big Fat Quiz of the Year in 2006. Two years later, when Morrissey cut short a gig at London’s Roundhouse, Ross, Brand and Walliams went on stage together to break the news to the crowd.

They saw each other off screen, too. Ross went to Walliams’s wedding to Lara Stone at Claridge’s in 2010. Later that year, Ross and Walliams were guests when Brand married Katy Perry in India.



When Brand’s divorce from Katy was finalised, in 2012, Ross let the comedian hide out his holiday home in Swanage, Dorset. It is understood that Ross was not present.

It later emerged that in July of that year Brand was accused of raping a woman against a wall in his Los Angeles home, an allegation Ross was unaware of at the time.

Ross was also a guest when Brand married Laura Gallacher in 2017.

Ross said this week he was “horrified” by the allegations against Walliams and by Brand’s crimes. He said he had once been on friendly terms with both men and was “genuinely unaware of their conduct”. He was photographed out on Wednesday, a day after issuing his statement.

Referring to the “tasteless joke” at the Comedy Awards, Ross said the scriptwriters gave him the line and he understood it as a joke about Walliams publicly dating younger women.



He called it “a tasteless joke that I would not dream of making today” and said he would have refused to tell it if he’d had any reason to think it referred to real events.

‘Go home with her dress still on’

Ross had joked about Brand on television, too. This time the woman at the centre of the gag was sitting right next to him.



Lily Allen was the only woman on the panel of Channel 4’s Big Fat Quiz of the Year in 2007. She was on Ross’s team, sitting near Brand and Noel Fielding.

Ross called the pair two of the best-known “cocksmen” in the business and insisted on swapping seats with Allen. That way, he joked, she might “go home with her dress still on”.

Brand and Fielding made jokes about rape. Allen later called the exchange “really horrendous”.

The charity dinner photo

While the three moved in the same showbiz circles and were often pictured in each others’ company, one picture tells a haunting story in the wake of the allegations against Walliams.



In a photograph shown in ITV’s David Walliams: Power and Silence, Walliams has his arm around Lilly Creightmore. Ross and Ricky Gervais are seated at the table at the charity event.

Creightmore was trying to make it as a photographer when she met Walliams. She was 18 when she first agreed to have dinner with him and now claims she was “groomed” and “manipulated” by the comic.

She told the Guardian she remembered feeling young and out of place at the celebrity parties he took her to.

Walliams has insisted he did not act inappropriately and did not “target” her because she was “vulnerable” or “young”.

The calls to Andrew Sachs



Andrew Sachs was due to be interviewed on Brand’s Radio 2 show in 2008. When the Fawlty Towers actor didn’t pick up, Brand started leaving him a message.

Ross interrupted, shouting that Brand had slept with Sachs’s granddaughter, Georgina Baillie. She was 23 when the calls went out.

They kept ringing. In one message, Brand asked if he could marry Baillie. Ross said he’d like to be a page boy. Brand tried singing an apology, bringing up the relationship again.

In his memoir, Brand said Ross suggested cutting the calls, then phoned him on the way home to ask again. Radio 2 aired them. Brand quit the show and the BBC suspended Ross for 12 weeks.



Back on Ross’s sofa

Two years after the calls, Ross interviewed Brand on stage at the Hackney Empire to launch his memoir, Booky Wook 2. The pair apologised for the calls, describing them as “not deliberately malicious but deliberately stupid”.

Brand went on Ross’s ITV chat show in 2013. It was the first time they’d spoken about the row together on television.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Let’s deal with this, because we’re both keen to put this behind us,” Ross said. He said they regretted the fuss they’d caused and the hurt it may have caused Sachs and his family.



There was one thing Ross said he was glad had come out of it. “We became very close.”

News.title: Andy Burnham declares 'fightback' starts now after Labour's election nightmare in Wales
News.content:
Andy Burnham declares 'fightback' starts now after Labour's election nightmare in Wales

Addressing the Welsh Labour conference in Llandudno, the Prime Minister urged the party to 'take stock' after losing power in May’s bruising Senedd elections

View 2 Images Andy Burnham speaking during the Welsh Labour conference in Llandudno (Image: Getty Images)

Andy Burnham has declared the fightback starts now in Wales after Labour’s historic election defeat earlier this year.

‌



‌



Addressing the party’s conference in Llandudno, the Prime Minister urged the party to “take stock” after losing power in May’s bruising Senedd elections. Mr Burnham told delegates: “It’s been a hard year, of course, hard year in terms of the elections that you fought, but we’ve got one job to do today, isn’t it? And make sure the fightback starts in earnest here, listening, learning, coming back stronger, and that’s what we will do.”

‌



He added that Welsh Labour was sending out a clear message: “We’re rebuilding, we’re coming back in the right way, having, having listened. But we will be stronger with Welsh Labour and UK Labour working together. That’s the partnership that always will underpin us.”

‌

Alan Milburn says Andy Burnham must make job or training offers for young people legal guarantee READ MORE :

Andy Burnham tears into David Cameron over Brexit intervention READ MORE :

View 2 Images Andy Burnham urged Welsh Labour to 'take stock' after losing power in May’s bruising Senedd elections (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association)

The Prime Minister said Labour would take “spirit in this fight” from the people of Aberfan. Last month he visited the mining village on the 60th anniversary of the Aberfan disaster, which killed 144 children and adults.

‌



He told the Welsh Labour conference: “What did they do? They stood together as a proud working class community, and they fought for what is right. A country where working class people are treated properly and fairly. And they were right to lead that fight, and I salute them in the way that they carried it forward all of those years.”

His intervention came as Welsh Labour prepared to publish its review into May’s election nightmare where the party lost its century-long dominance over Welsh politics. During his speech on Saturday, the Prime Minister also said the Brexit deal negotiated by the Tories was not good enough for Britain.

‌



Ahead of Friday’s major UK-EU summit, he said: “We’ve got the Conservatives who are standing out against it, saying no change. Well, I don’t believe Brexit and the deal that they got has been good enough for Britain.

“I think we’ve lost more than we’ve gained over the last 10 years, and, actually, I think the Conservatives gave Britain a harsher and harder Brexit than people thought they were getting when they voted in 2016.

Article continues below

“They burned all of our bridges in the aftermath, with the EU, and so I’m going to lead as Prime Minister on this issue, and I’m going to go and try and get the best deal I can for Wales, for those here who could benefit, Welsh farmers, exporters of Welsh shellfish and Welsh lamb.”

The Prime Minister also joked during his speech that he achieved his young political dream of a “kinnock around the Cabinet table” as he introduced the Welsh Secretary, Stephen Kinnock, the son of Neil Kinnock, who led Labour between 1983 and 1992.

News.title: Horror footage shows BMW speeding through Coventry before boy, 12, hit and killed
News.content:
Horror footage shows BMW speeding through Coventry before boy, 12, hit and killed

Aleksanders Dolars - also known as Dolars Aleksanders - ploughed into Keaton Slater in Coventry as he walked home from school

Driver jailed over fatal Keaton Slater collision in Coventry

Shocking footage shows the moment a reckless BMW driver reached 70mph in a 30mph zone moments before he killed a 12-year-old boy in a hit-and-run.

‌



‌



Keaton Slater was walking home from school on June 14, 2024, when Aleksanders Dolars, also known as Dolars Aleksanders, hit him on Radford Road in Coventry. Dolars sped off and abandoned the BMW around six miles away.

‌



Paramedics were called, but Keaton’s injuries were fatal. Dolars fled to Latvia, where police tracked him down before he was extradited to the UK. He was arrested at Gatwick Airport in August and later admitted causing death by dangerous driving.

‌



He was jailed for nine years and four months and banned from driving for more than 16 years at Warwick Crown Court on Friday.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images Keaton Slater (Image: West Midlands Police/PA Wire)

‌



Mum's urgent warning to parents after her baby son gets trapped in bath seat READ MORE :

David Cameron says Alzheimer's made his mother beg sister to kill her in NHS drugs plea READ MORE :

Keaton’s mum Louise has spoken out about sitting outside the suspect’s home to urge his family to hand him in. She was given the details of Aleksanders Dolars after the horrific ordeal. She was told by a neighbour that the family, originally from Latvia, had packed and left just a day or two earlier.

‌



She told the BBC: "All I was going to say was, 'how can you live with yourselves’? I'd tell them to hold their hands up. Do the right thing. Tell him to face what he's done."

Louise later was advised that Dolars was in Lativa as police tracked him through phone records. She created a petition calling for his petition. However there was no extradition treaty in place between the UK and the EU after Brexit causing a lengthy legal battle taking two years.

‌



After the case, Keaton's family paid moving tributes to their 'beautiful boy'. His mum Louise said: "Keaton was our world. He was funny, caring, loving and full of life. He had the biggest smile and a heart full of kindness. He brought happiness into our home simply by being himself.

"The day Keaton was killed was the day our family stopped being whole. There are no words that can properly describe the pain of losing a child. It is heartbreak that never leaves you. When Keaton walked out of our door that day, we expected him to come home. We never imagined that we were watching him leave for the last time.

‌



"It is not only Keaton who died that day. A part of all of us as a family died with him. Our lives changed forever, and nothing will ever be the same again. The circumstances of Keaton's death have made our grief even harder to bear. Knowing that the person responsible did not stop to help our son is something we will never understand. Keaton was left behind.

"I cannot understand how anyone could leave a child who had just been struck and not stop to help him. That knowledge has added another layer of pain to an already unbearable loss.

‌



"He should have had the chance to grow up, fall in love, have a career, make mistakes, achieve his dreams, watch football, play football, grow old and have a family of his own. All of those possibilities were taken away from him.

"I want Keaton to be remembered for the beautiful boy he was - for his smile, his kindness, his love of football, his laughter and the love he gavd to everyone around him."

‌



View 2 Images Aleksanders Dolars abandoned the BMW more than six miles from where he struck Keaton (Image: West Midlands Police)

Keaton's father Clint said: "The bond I had with Keaton is something that is impossible to put fully into words. He was a huge part of my life, my heart and my world. He was someone I loved beyond measure, and I always believed that I would have a lifetime ahead of me to watch him grow, to guide him, to laugh with him, and to make more memories with him.

‌



"Keaton was a passionate Coventry City supporter. He loved his football and followed his team with real passion. His untimely death has taken away the joy he would have had seeing his beloved team reach the Premier League.

"It is another future moment that he should have been here to experience, another thing that he will never get chance to celebrate. Keaton was loved. He mattered. He was more than what happened to him. He was my son, my best friend, my little mini me.

‌



"I will miss him for the rest of my life."

Detective Chief Inspector Sam Lewis, of West Midlands Police, said: “Keaton was a 12-year-old boy, making his way home from school, and he should have been able to arrive back safely. The driver was travelling at excessive speed and rather than stop and help Keaton he just left and tried to avoid capture.

‌



“This was an extremely complex case given it spanned across borders and involved different legislation. We worked with a range of partners, including the CPS, to ensure we could get him back from Latvia to face justice.

"We kept fighting for Keaton and through plenty of persistence, hard work and patience we finally got there. We’re grateful for all the support we received during this investigation, from members of the Coventry community who provided information to the other agencies who also worked tirelessly to ensure Aleksanders could be charged with his awful crime.

‌



“We’re especially grateful to Louise and Clint, Keaton’s brothers, and the wider family for their support during what has been a long and difficult process. This was always about getting justice for Keaton and together we’ve managed to do that.

Tamina Greaves from the Crown Prosecution Service said: “This case presented challenges from the start with a suspect at large with no legal framework to get access to him. However, throughout this case there has been one constant, which has been the resilience and determination of Keaton’s parents, Louise and Clint, to see justice done for their son, who was taken from them is such tragic circumstances.

Article continues below

"Their determination has inspired us to give everything we could to get to today’s outcome."

News.title: Met Office maps show wall of snow hitting England and Wales in 18 areas - full list
News.content:
Met Office maps show wall of snow hitting England and Wales in 18 areas - full list

Weather maps show parts of the UK which will be hit by a 200-mile wall of snow on Tuesday as an Arctic blast causes a deep freeze

UK weather map forecasts wintry conditions as snow expected

Brits are facing a fresh Artic blast within days as a 200-mile band of snow is forecast to hit a huge swathe of England and Wales.

‌



‌



The UK is in the midst of a icy snap with temperatures dropping to -6.4C in Cumbria and Brecon last Thursday - and more wintry conditions predicted.

‌



After another bitterly cold Saturday, the weather is expected to be slightly milder on Sunday with fronts bringing rain from the Atlantic before northern cold air, arriving from the Arctic, once again takes control.

‌



At the same time, there is a band of wet weather moving northwards and the snow is predicted when this hits cold air.

View 3 Images A band of snow across the UK at midnight going into Tuesday

Met Office maps show snow running horizontally across the UK, through northern Wales and England from midnight on Monday and in the early hours of Tuesday. This band then moves northwards and eastwards through the night before breaking up.

‌



Around 3am it begins in southern Scotland, below Glasgow, crosses northern England and goes as low as Nottinghamshire and Lincolnshire.

There could be more than 5cm of snow falling in these areas as well as nearer to 15cm in hilly areas of central Scotland.

‌



BBC weather forecaster Helen Willetts says: "We can see that northerly wind coming back in later in the day pushing those weather fronts out of the way by the start of Monday and we are back into that sparkling Arctic air.

View 3 Images The band of snow is set to head northwards and eastwards during the early hours of Tuesday

‌



"So even at lower levels in the north we could see some snow showers and they will certainly be gathering in force across the northern part of Scotland.

"Tuesday looks quite an interesting day as we've got this next weather system running to the south of the UK, as it comes and bumps into the cold air we could have a spell of snow.

‌



"It is a long way off at the moment but we will firm up, don't take this as read because it could be a little bit further north or south but wherever that weather front grinds to a halt we could see a spell of snow primarily on the hills but not necessarily exclusively - we could see something at lower levels as well. "

And she adds: "We are staying in the colder air for much of next week"

‌



View 3 Images The wall of snow by 6am on Tuesday

While a forecast from the Met Office states: "Into next week, unsettled and cold conditions remain with rain, sleet and (mainly hill) snow key features."

‌



Its outlook for Monday to Wednesday reads: "Colder, but sunnier on Monday. Wintry showers in the far north, with rain, and hill snow moving north across the UK into Tuesday. Brighter, but colder again for most midweek."

News.title: Experts name 'strongest' lifestyle habit that may slash blood pressure without medication
News.content:
Experts name 'strongest' lifestyle habit that may slash blood pressure without medication

Most people know about cutting salt, but experts say waist size and broken sleep are just as critical for your heart - here's 10 things to consider

View 3 Images If you have poor sleep quality, ongoing fatigue, and are worried about your health, it’s a good idea to consult your GP or a specialist (Image: alvaro gonzalez via Getty Images)

Some people are health-conscious and want to prevent issues like heart attacks and high cholesterol. But before you jump straight to medication and supplements to lower or manage your blood pressure, there are a few things you can try first.

‌



‌



In a July 2026 update, experts from the Mayo Clinic have urged people to consider "lifestyle changes". This is because they "play a big role in treating the condition". If you do need medication, you should follow your doctor’s advice and take it as prescribed. But if you don’t have blood pressure problems and simply want to keep it in check and prevent it from creeping into 'high blood pressure' territory - aka Hypertension - a healthy lifestyle could help prevent issues from developing - and may reduce the likelihood of needing medication.

‌



Can I lower blood pressure without medication?

View 3 Images Always seek help from your GP if you are worried (Image: Getty)

‌



Depending on your circumstances, you could prevent hypertension without taking medication . High blood pressure is when your overall blood pressure is always high - even when you are resting.

The British Heart Foundation (BHF) explains that, for most people, this occurs when your blood pressure is over 140/95 mmHg. This is a "serious condition", and experts warn that if you do not manage to get it under control, it could cause a number of issues, including loss of vision, kidney failure, heart failure and vascular dementia.

Arteries are usually flexible, so they can handle changes in blood pressure. But if your blood pressure stays high, they can become stiff or narrow - this makes it easier for fatty deposits to build up, which can also increase the risk of a heart attack or stroke.

‌



10 ways to manage high blood pressure without medicine

Before jumping to ask the doctor for medication, the Mayo Clinic has advised people to try a few changes to how they live, drink and eat, listing "10 ways to manage high blood pressure without medicine".

This includes:

‌



Weight and waist - We all know that avoiding alcohol and eating fruit and veg is key, but experts remind people that "weight loss in people who are overweight is the strongest lifestyle factor that can lower blood pressure." On top of this, it stresses that "the greater the waist measurement, the greater the health risk, including high blood pressure." Do this at home -You can buy a home blood pressure monitor without a prescription at many stores. But remember that regular visits with a healthcare professional are an important part of blood pressure management. Exercise regularly and stay active - Exercise can lower high blood pressure. And no, you don't have to do a marathon. Get active in whatever way you can - if that means walking, then do it. Some is better than nothing. You should aim to get 75 minutes of vigorous aerobic activity or 150 minutes of moderate physical activity per week. Don't panic if you're not able to do this; do what you can. Lower sodium in your diet - Limit sodium to 2,300 milligrams (mg) a day or less. But for most adults, limiting sodium to 1,500 mg a day or less is better. Doing that may lower high blood pressure by about 5 to 6 mm Hg. Ease stress - Long-term stress may contribute to high blood pressure. While easier said than done, you could try meditation, breathing exercises, or any activity that helps you feel calm and unwind. Eat healthy foods - When trying to lose weight, focus on foods that provide sustained energy and the vitamins and minerals your body needs. Aim for whole grains, fruit, vegetables and low-fat dairy. Cut back on saturated and trans fats, as well as cholesterol, and prioritise nutrients such as potassium, calcium, magnesium and fibre. Don't smoke or vape - One of the best things you can do for your heart health is to stay away from tobacco or nicotine products - this includes electronic cigarettes and vaping devices. Tobacco and nicotine raise blood pressure. If you need help quitting, talk with your GP about programs or treatments that can help. Manage your cholesterol and blood sugar - High blood sugar and high levels of "bad" non-HDL cholesterol do not affect blood pressure directly, but they do raise the risk of heart disease. Non-HDL cholesterol is your total cholesterol minus your "good" HDL cholesterol. Limit alcohol - Do not drink every day. The less you drink, the better. One drink equals 12 fluid ounces of beer, 5 ounces of wine or 1.5 ounces of 80-proof liquor. You can find out more about limits via DrinkAware. Get a good night's sleep - Adults should aim for 7 to 9 hours of sleep each night. Talk to your doctor if you struggle to sleep, as getting fewer than 7 hours every night for weeks can affect blood pressure.

View 3 Images The NHS says that "too much cholesterol can block your blood vessels. It makes you more likely to have heart problems or a stroke" (Image: Halfpoint Images via Getty Images)

‌



The Mayo Clinic reassures anyone worried: "Making lifestyle changes takes time. Some days it might feel challenging. So ask your family or friends for support when you need it. Support can come in many ways. Friends or family may drive you to healthcare checkups or exercise with you to keep your blood pressure low."

Unhealthy habits

It’s easy to slip into unhealthy habits. It can start with not getting enough sleep, then stress - at work or at home - keeps you awake even more. When you’re exhausted, cooking feels like a struggle, so you eat food that isn't so good for you.

‌



You forget to make lunch and end up grabbing processed food; you skip fruit and veg because a quicker dinner feels easier. Over time, it all adds up. This is a really common cycle that many people struggle with - so you’re not alone.

If you’re worried about your blood pressure, or think it may be high, don’t ignore it - speak to your GP or another qualified healthcare professional. Lifestyle changes can help, but they don’t work for everyone, and some people will still need medication.

Article continues below

Only a clinician can assess what’s right for you and recommend a treatment plan tailored to your individual health needs.

News.title: Tesco shoppers warned 'do not eat' popular pies after labelling mistake
News.content:
Tesco shoppers warned 'do not eat' popular pies after labelling mistake

Tesco has recalled two products and customers who have bought them have been told to return to the store for a full refund

View 3 Images Tesco has issued a recall (Image: Elaine Blackburne)

Tesco has issued an urgent warning after a mistake made some of its popular pies potentially unsafe to eat. The supermarket chain has told anyone who has bought either of the products to return them to the store for a full refund.

‌



‌



An alert by the Food Standards Agency advised both the Tesco Steak and Guinness Pie and Tesco Steak and Guinness Mini Pies were being recalled because they contain milk which is not declared on the label. It added: "These products contain milk making them a possible health risk for anyone with an allergy to milk or intolerance to milk or milk constituents."

‌



The FSA said Tesco was recalling the products from customers. It added the chain "has been advised to contact the relevant allergy support organisations, which will tell their members about the recall."

‌



It advised: "The company has also issued a recall notice to its customers. These notices explain to customers why the products are being recalled and tell them what to do if they have bought the products."

The affected products

In its recall notice, Tesco said: "We are recalling specific date codes of two Tesco Steak & Guiness Pie products, due to undeclared milk in these products. If eaten, they could pose a risk to those with an allergy or intolerance to milk or milk constituents."

View 3 Images The product recall notice (Image: Tesco)

‌



There are two products that are affected by the mistake. These are:

Tesco 6 Steak & Guinness Mini Pies 198g - All 'use by' dates up to and including 23 November 2026

Tesco Steak and Guinness Pie 200g - All 'use by' dates up to and including 23 November 2026

‌



Tesco advised: "If you've bought one of the affected products and are intolerant or have an allergy to milk or milk constituents, please don't eat it. Instead, return the product to any Tesco store where a full refund will be given. No receipt is required."

It added: "No other Tesco products are affected by this recall. We're sorry for any inconvenience caused." It said if shoppers needed more information they could contact Tesco Customer Services via its contact us page.

‌



View 3 Images Tesco has issued a recall of some popular pies (Image: Getty)

Ensure our latest lifestyle news always appears at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings

Article continues below

What is a product recall?

The FSA regularly issues product recalls when there is a potential problem. It explains: "Sometimes there will be a problem with a food product that means it should not be sold. Then it might be 'withdrawn' (taken off the shelves) or 'recalled' (when customers are asked to return the product).

"Sometimes foods have to be withdrawn or recalled if there is a risk to consumers because the allergy labelling is missing or incorrect or if there is any other food allergy risk. When there is a food allergy risk, the FSA will issue an Allergy Alert."

News.title: Noel Fielding says he and Russell Brand were never friends and haven't been in contact in years
News.content:
Noel Fielding says he and Russell Brand were never friends and haven't been in contact in years

Speaking out for the first time, Noel Fielding said that he was 'horrified and deeply disturbed' to learn of Brand's crimes and said that he was 'completely unaware' of them until they became public knowledge

View 3 Images Russell Brand (L) and Noel Fielding pose after performing at the Royal Albert Hall on March 28, 2007

Noel Fielding declared that he and Russell Brand were never friends and haven't been in contact in years in a scathing statement.

Former comedian Brand, 51, was sentenced to 10 years and six months on Monday after being convicted of rape and sexual assault. Throughout the noughties and the 2010s, Brand and Noel frequently worked together on panel shows, including The Big Fat Quiz of the Year.

Speaking out for the first time last night, Noel said that he was "horrified and deeply disturbed" to learn of Brand's crimes and said that he was "completely unaware" of them until they became public knowledge.

He acknowledged working with Brand on many occassions, but said he never considered him a friend and that he has not spoken to him in years. Noel also said that he regrets some of the jokes he made while alongside him, describing them as "horrible and inappropriate".

"I was horrified and deeply disturbed to learn of Russell Brand’s crimes, which I was completely unaware of until they became public knowledge. My thoughts are with the women whose courage brought him to justice," he said.

Noel Fielding breaks silence on Russell Brand with scathing statement READ MORE :

View 3 Images Noel Fielding and Russell Brand's last known TV appearance together was Celebrity Bake Off in 2019 (Image: Channel 4)

"I appeared on TV, radio and live charity shows with him, and whilst we played it up for the cameras and in the media, I considered it a professional relationship, rather than a personal one. I have had no contact with him for many years. Looking back at some of the jokes I made alongside him I was appalled. They were horrible and inappropriate, and I very much regret them," he told The Sun.

Their last known appearance together was recorded in 2018 on 2019's The Great Celebrity Bake Off for Stand Up to Cancer. Noel had been hosting the show at the time and Brand made a 3D biscuit showstopper depicting the birth of his second daughter.

View 3 Images The pair frequently appeared on panel shows together (Image: Channel 4)

The pair met at the NME Awards in the 2000s but their careers took different paths for some time. Whilst Brand was hitting the big time with his hosting duties on Big Brother's Big Mouth, Noel had success in comedy shows like The Mighty Boosh.

Since then, Noel has been team captain on Never Mind The Buzzcocks and has been co-presenting Bake Off since 2017. As well as his comedy career, he has also acted as the lead role in Apple TV+ comedy series The Completely Made-Up Adventures of Dick Turpin.

It comes after Jo Whiley spoke about the creepy message Brand once left her.

The radio legend, 61, had been speaking to Zoe Ball, 55, on the latest episode of the Dig It podcast and said that she had "cried" for Brand's victims when the verdict was read out.

Jo explained that she has a "show book" that she has guests sign when they appear on her show. In the book, Brand wrote that Jo was a MILF (Mum I'd Like to F**k).

"I've got a show book that people sign my book when they come on the show and I've got a signature from Russell," Jo said. She went on to add: "It's got the word; he just refers to me as a MILF, and I feel like I keep looking at the bookshelf. It's like it's burning a hole in my bookshelf at the moment.

"I'm sitting in the living room like those words are there. I'm going to have to tear the page out and burn it. I really am because it just makes me shudder but that was what you expected I think when you met him."
