Sports.title: Man Utd ‘missed out on top SEVEN summer transfer targets’ before signing £35million Youri Tielemans
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED missed out on their top seven midfield transfer targets before signing Youri Tielemans for £35million.

The Red Devils endured a frustrating summer in the transfer market, with their recruitment struggles now emerging following Michael Carrick‘s sacking.



According to The Athletic, United had Nottingham Forest star Elliot Anderson at the top of their wishlist.

West Ham midfielder Mateus Fernandes was their second choice, followed by Newcastle’s Sandro Tonali and Real Madrid star Aurelien Tchouameni.



Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, Atalanta’s Ederson and Lille youngster Ayyoub Bouaddi, who has now joined Manchester City, was also ahead of Tielemans in the club’s plans.

But United failed to land any of their preferred targets before eventually turning to the Belgian midfielder in a £35m deal.

The club also considered signing Leon Goretzka on a free transfer after his departure from Bayern Munich, but his wage demands proved a stumbling block.

The German instead joined Aston Villa and even scored against United in Carrick’s final game in charge.

Tielemans has been the most regular of United’s three midfield additions, playing 988 minutes in all competitions.

Andrey Santos, signed from Chelsea for £50m, has managed just 556 minutes, while £70m arrival Carlos Baleba has played only 397 minutes.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The recruitment struggles have raised further questions about United’s transfer strategy under Sir Jim Ratcliffe, with Carrick understood to have wanted more reinforcements.

The former United midfielder was particularly keen to sign a backup striker and left-back but was left disappointed by the club’s summer business.

Carrick paid the price for a disastrous start to the season, with United slipping into the Premier League relegation zone.

He was finally sacked on Thursday after just one win in 11 games, despite having guided the club into the Champions League last season.



His dismissal came after United chiefs had already begun working on a deal to bring Mauricio Pochettino to Old Trafford.

Pochettino was appointed as Carrick’s replacement yesterday, with the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss tasked with rescuing United’s season.

The Argentine inherits a squad struggling for confidence, with injuries and poor performances adding to the club’s problems.

United sporting director Jason Wilcox has defended the club’s recruitment, insisting the squad is stronger than it was last season.

But injuries to key players, including Baleba and Benjamin Sesko, have made life difficult for the Red Devils.

And Pochettino now faces the huge challenge of turning things around after another turbulent few months at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Why Man Utd could face rocky start under Pochettino – but there is a GOOD omen for Liverpool clash
Sports.content:
Next

MAURICIO POCHETTINO could be in for a rocky start at Manchester United if his previous Premier League appointments are anything to go by.

But the Argentine has one remarkable record that could give fans hope ahead of his debut against bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield.



Pochettino, 54, has been confirmed for the Old Trafford hotseat after Michael Carrick was sacked on Thursday following a disastrous start to the season.

United have won just one of their opening ten Premier League matches, collecting eight points and slipping into the relegation zone.



The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss takes charge after he’s overseen the USA’s upcoming games with Haiti, with a daunting trip to Liverpool on November 22 set to be his first assignment.

And while United supporters will be desperate for an immediate turnaround, Pochettino’s previous record suggests patience could be required.

Across his first ten Premier League matches at Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, the Argentine managed just 11 wins from a possible 30.

That represents a win percentage of only 36.7 per cent, with eight draws and 11 defeats across those three spells.

His best start came at Southampton, where he collected 15 points from his opening ten league matches after replacing Nigel Adkins in January 2013.

But even that was far from straightforward.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Pochettino won just one of his first seven games, a stunning 3-1 victory over Manchester City, before finally finding some consistency.

Three consecutive wins against Liverpool, Chelsea and Reading followed as Southampton began to pull away from relegation trouble.

He eventually guided the Saints to safety before leading them to an impressive eighth-place finish the following season.

His arrival at Tottenham in 2014 initially promised a much quicker transformation.

Spurs won their opening two league matches under Pochettino, beating West Ham 1-0 and thrashing QPR 4-0.



But the early momentum quickly disappeared.

Tottenham won just two of their next eight Premier League games, suffering defeats against Liverpool, West Brom, Manchester City and Newcastle.

They collected 14 points from their opening ten matches, with four wins, two draws and four defeats.

Things were even more difficult when Pochettino returned to London to take charge of Chelsea in 2023.



The Blues won just one of their first six Premier League games, with their only victory coming against newly promoted Luton Town.

Successive wins over Fulham and Burnley offered some encouragement, but Chelsea finished their opening ten league matches with just three victories, three draws and four defeats.

That left Pochettino with 12 points from a possible 30 and a win percentage of only 30 per cent.

It is hardly the sort of immediate impact United supporters will be hoping for as their side battles to climb out of the bottom three.



Sunshine ahead of Liverpool game

However, Pochettino has never lost his first competitive match in charge of a new team.

The Argentine began his managerial career with a goalless draw against Barcelona in the Copa del Rey after taking over at Espanyol in January 2009.

He followed that with another 0-0 draw against Everton on his Southampton debut four years later.

His first Tottenham match ended in a 1-0 victory at West Ham, while he drew 1-1 with Saint-Etienne after taking charge of Paris Saint-Germain in 2021.



Pochettino also held Liverpool to a 1-1 draw in his first game as Chelsea manager in August 2023.

And his first match in charge of the United States ended in a 2-0 victory over Panama in October 2024.

That gives him two wins and four draws from six managerial debuts, a record he will be desperate to protect at Anfield.

There is another curious connection to United’s next opponents.



Pochettino has won just once in eight previous visits to Anfield as a manager, with that solitary victory coming during his time at Southampton.

The Saints stunned Brendan Rodgers‘ Liverpool 1-0 in September 2013 thanks to a second-half header from Dejan Lovren.

And among the Southampton players celebrating that afternoon was a certain Luke Shaw.



The defender, then just 18, started at left-back under Pochettino and helped keep a clean sheet against a Liverpool attack featuring Daniel Sturridge.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Shaw would join Manchester United the following summer, with Pochettino heading to Tottenham.

The Argentine has failed to win on any of his seven subsequent visits to Anfield, including his most recent trip with Chelsea in January 2024, which ended in a 4-1 defeat.

Sports.title: Michael Olise nearing agreement for first-ever boot deal as reason he has never signed one is revealed
Sports.content:
Next

MICHAEL OLISE is reportedly closing in on a lucrative sponsorship agreement with Nike – despite having worn the company’s boots for years without earning a penny.

The Bayern Munich superstar, 24, has remarkably gone his entire professional career without signing an official footwear endorsement deal.



But that could finally change, with the American sportswear giants now leading the chase for the former Crystal Palace favourite.

According to French newspaper L’Equipe, negotiations between Olise and Nike are at an advanced stage, although an agreement has yet to be officially announced.



The France international has long favoured Nike’s Hypervenom boots, even continuing to wear older models rather than cashing in on a sponsorship contract.

His unusual approach has allowed him to choose his own footwear without being tied down to the commercial demands that come with representing a major brand.

But Nike are now keen to make the dazzling winger one of their biggest footballing faces following the departure of his French teammate and Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe.

Mbappe ended his near-20-year relationship with the company in September to join Swiss sportswear brand On in a ten-year agreement, leaving Nike searching for another global superstar.

And the battle for Olise’s signature is not without competition, with Adidas and On also understood to have expressed interest in securing his services.

Yet those close to the former Eagles ace insist money is not his main motivation.

Olise is reluctant to pursue commercial opportunities unless they fit his personal preferences.

His growing profile has attracted approaches from businesses beyond football – including fashion and memorabilia companies, but his priority has remained delivering on the pitch.

The London-born attacker joined Bayern from Palace in 2024 and has established himself as one of the best players in Europe.

And his remarkable rise could now earn him his first major boot payday.

Sports.title: 'Sir Bobby Robson was a genius - his achievements are criminally underrated'
Sports.content:
Terry Butcher believes Sir Bobby Robson should be remembered as the greatest English manager of all time.

England legend Butcher played under the late great Robson for both club and country and believes his former manager deserves more credit. Robson managed England for eight years, led them to the World Cup semi-final at Italia 90 and also won the FA Cup and UEFA Cup during a glorious spell at Ipswich Town.

Butcher has now put together a book 'Almost Immortal' along with the likes of Peter Shilton, Paul Parker, Stuart Pearce, Des Walker, Bryan Robson, Paul Gascoigne, Chris Waddle, Peter Beardsley, Gary Lineker and John Barnes.

It reflects upon Robson’s style and man-management and Butcher believes those qualities set him apart from the rest. Butcher said: “I think he's the best. I know it's a bold statement, but it's not just based on England being England manager in those eight years.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“It's about setting the club up, setting Ipswich up to become a real force, and not only in England but in Europe as well. When he went to England, he transformed the squad. He made it better. He improved it, and if it got worse, then he made changes.

“And he was tremendous at building teams. He really was, and very, very strong at dismantling those teams. But not just with England, but also when his career abroad, he was very successful.

‌



"He created great atmospheres there and great teams. You look at Ronaldo when he got Ronaldo at Barcelona. Wow, that's one of the greatest signings of all time. He was an absolute genius and Bobby got the best out of him.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 5 Images The cover of Almost Immortal

Meanwhile, Butcher played a starring role in a game which will go down as one of England’s greatest victories on foreign soil.

‌



The night when Gary Lineker scored all four in a 4-2 win, England smashed Spain, Emilio Butragueño and Co in the Bernabéu. Incredibly, February 18, 1987, was also the night that former England captain Tony Adams made his international debut.

It was also a taste of Sir Bobby Robson’s England team at their best and provides a glorious, wonderful reminder for the current generation.

England boss Thomas Tuchel goes to Madrid again on Saturday with a dream of overhauling the current world champions in the Metropolitano Stadium.

“I remember it so well, “ said Butcher. “It was in Madrid, the Bernabeu, the pitch was rubbish, the most horrible pitch in the world because it was soaking wet and I think it helped us because we were used to pitches like that in the First Division.

‌



View 5 Images Terry Butcher, Gary Lineker and Bryan Robson celebrate after a 4-2 win over Spain (Image: David Cannon/Getty Images)

“Wembley was the best pitch in the world at that time. But we were in Madrid, it was Tony Adams' debut and I played alongside Tony Adams. I think it sort of came out of nowhere in many respects. It was Gary Lineker’s night because he scored four and it helped us enormously.

“I also think it helped Gary enormously because he’s a Barcelona player, scores four against Spain in the Bernabeu! That sort of made him at Barcelona with the Catalans. He was off and running. He was top man.

“I had a friend in Ipswich, I got him a ticket and he came out and we had lunch in a tapas restaurant - I didn’t even know what tapas was!

‌



“Afterwards, we went to a Spanish Lladro shop, bought a piece of China, and I spent the rest of the trip carrying it round. It took pride of place, we couldn’t put it on the hold in case it got smashed! It was a brilliant trip.

“Those sort of trips and results really pull a squad together and it definitely did that for us. It was great times with Bobby.”

View 5 Images Ezri Konsa and Marc Guehi are England's first-choice centre-back pairing (Image: JON OLAV NESVOLD/BILDBYRÅN/Shutterstock)

Butcher is one of England’s greatest centre-halves and believes the current first choice pair - Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa - are the rock upon which the team is built.

‌



“I like Konsa a lot,” said Butcher. “I like Guehi as well. He would have learned from the World Cup and also knows there’s other centre halves so that competition brings pressure. That sort of threat is a good thing. Competition and battle for places was always good for me because it drove me harder.”

Butcher has helped put together the book on Robson titled 'Almost Immortal' and clearly his generation did not lift a trophy.

Ex-England captain Butcher believes Thomas Tuchel’s men have that within their grasp - and one trophy will help others follow. They were so close under Sir Gareth Southgate - and went to the semi finals again in the summer.

Butcher added: “The thing about the players now—they've got to realise they're on the cusp of greatness, and the book's almost immortal. This team can become immortals. They've got it well within their power to become immortals.

‌



View 5 Images England legend Terry Butcher (Image: MatchWornShirt)

“Spain have got a real belief about them. Argentina always got a belief about them. We don't seem to have that belief. It was much of a belief as the other countries. I think that's the difference between winning and losing. It has to be a strong team that's got the ability.

“We've certainly got the ability, but it's got to be a team. Winners have a really strong mind and a really strong belief. It's not arrogance. They just know they can win. They know they can beat anybody.

“You've got to believe you're going to win the game. There's that slight mentality difference. You're talking small margins. But enough to be immortal. Not just also immortals all the time. That's our sort of title really. Also immortals. I think that's the next book coming up!

‌



“It's the hope that kills you as an England fan. You get that emotion. But it's one. It's the one trophy. It's like when you're climbing Everest. Climb that mountain, make the final steps and once you get over the top, you will carry on winning.”

Full details of Almost Immortal can be found here: https://www.almostimmortal.co.uk/

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino's dream Man Utd XI as Bruno Fernandes replaced and Chelsea star signs
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino's dream Man Utd XI as Bruno Fernandes replaced and Chelsea star signs

Mauricio Pochettino faces a huge rebuilding job at Manchester United

View 6 Images Mauricio Pochettino could lure some exciting signings to Old Trafford (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Mauricio Pochettino has his hands full after being sworn in as the next Manchester United manager. The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has penned a two-and-a-half-year contract after agreeing to replace the sacked Michael Carrick.

‌



‌



Pochettino's first task is steering a squad of misfits clear of the relegation zone, given United entered the international break in 18th with just one win from 10 games. Beyond that lies a sweeping rebuild that could attract some big names to Old Trafford, with other high-profile figures heading for the exit door.

‌



Given his extensive knowledge of the English, European and world game, Pochettino's pulling power should be significant, provided the club can back him financially. Here's how a dream Pochettino XI could look and how he could reconstruct the team…

‌



Mauricio Pochettino bursts into tears in first interview after getting Man Utd job READ MORE :

When will Mauricio Pochettino first take charge of Man Utd and his likely starting XI? READ MORE :

Defensive clearout

A ruthless clear-out is overdue. Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, and Diogo Dalot all need to go, and unless Lisandro Martinez undergoes a major attitude shift under his compatriot, he should be shown the door when his contract expires this summer.

Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt aren't long-term solutions either. At right-back, Atletico Madrid's Marcos Llorente would be an astute addition, especially as he is out of contract in the summer.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



He's 31 but has retired from international football, which should prolong his club career. The fact that he could operate in midfield too would be a valuable asset. If Pochettino wants a younger option - and a player he knows - he could turn to United States star Alex Freeman, 22. Or why not go for both for a bit of youth and experience?

United are also crying out for a quality left-back. Step forward, Fulham's Antonee Robinson. He ranks among the Premier League's top full-backs in tackles and interceptions and, crucially, rarely misses games through injury, unlike Shaw. He would need no introduction to Pochettino, having played under him for the US.

‌



View 6 Images Antonee Robinson could be an option for United (Image: Getty Images)

In the centre of defence, the likes of Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Nathan Collins (Brentford) and Calvin Bassey (Fulham) have all been linked with United and all three would be welcome, forward-thinking additions. Youngsters like Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven need to stick around but as back-up options rather than regular first-teamers.

‌



In goal, Senne Lammens hasn't been convincing recently - perhaps unsurprising given the players in front of him - but he deserves more time to prove himself.

Midfield tinkering

While he's had a mixed time at Spurs, Conor Gallagher was superb under Pochettino at Chelsea, arguably playing the best football of his career. A reunion could kickstart his career.

‌



During the 2023/24 season, he enjoyed spells across the midfield, playing as a six, eight and a 10. Pochettino regularly spoke highly of the midfielder, once saying: "I think he is a player with a great commitment to the team. It's priceless to have a player like him."

Gallagher could form a handy partnership with Kobbie Mainoo. Youri Tielemans could still have a role to play but Andrey Santos already looks like an expensive mistake.

‌



View 6 Images Conor Gallagher could be available (Image: Robbie Stephenson/PA Wire)

Wing wizard needed

United were linked with Crysencio Summerville in the summer before he eventually signed for Al-Hilal. At 25, a player of his dynamism and quality is wasted in Saudi Arabia.

‌



But once he's sufficiently topped up his bank balance, he'll probably crave a move back to a big league. The Dutchman could be ideal for the Poch revolution.

View 6 Images Crysencio Summerville was on United's radar in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Pounce for Palmer

Bringing in Palmer would be a pricey statement of intent, but the foundations are already laid. He played some of his best football under Pochettino, calling him a "top manager and a top person" and is a childhood United supporter.

Given Chelsea's track record of cashing in on talent, a deal cannot be ruled out. Palmer could replace Bruno Fernandes as playmaker in chief. For all his quality, Fernandes is in danger of becoming more trouble than he's worth. A move could be best for all parties.

‌



View 6 Images Mauricio Pochettino has previously worked with Cole Palmer at Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Reuniting with Kane

While the England captain recently penned a new deal with Bayern Munich, Pochettino is the one manager outside of Tottenham who could tempt him back to the Premier League, following their successful five-year partnership in north London.

‌



Should Kane lift the Champions League this season, there would be little left for him to conquer in Germany. Firing United back to the summit would be the ultimate crowning achievement to a storied career.

Another, more realistic option would be US striker Folarin Balogun of Monaco, who remains on the radar of Premier League clubs after almost joining Everton in the summer.

‌



View 6 Images Could Pochettino tempt Harry Kane to United (Image: PA)

As for existing players, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha are talents who should stick around, while Amad can't be written off just yet. But it's getting increasingly difficult to see a United future for Benjamin Sesko. And it's surely time for Marcus Rashford to sever ties with the club once and for all.

‌



United dream XI under Pochettino: Lemmens; Llorente, Branthwaite, Collins, Robinson; Mainoo, Gallagher; Cunha, Palmer, Summerville; Kane.

Sports.title: 5 biggest issues Mauricio Pochettino will immediately face after arriving at Man Utd
Sports.content:
"We are trying to make our dreams come true."

Mauricio Pochettino burst into tears in his first interview since it was confirmed he would be swapping the United States for Manchester United.

"I never said I wanted to go back but they know there aren't too many opportunities that happen in your career like Manchester United," he said while explaining his decision. "When it arrives, it's difficult to turn down."

Pochettino has always wanted the United job. He'd been interviewed three times for it previously. Now he's finally got his wish, but the mess the club finds itself in following the sacking of Michael Carrick means it will be anything but straightforward.

‌



Here Mirror Football assesses the most pressing concerns facing the Argentine before he arrives in Manchester next week, with just a few days to prepare for a trip to Anfield.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

1. His new bosses

Pochettino likely still has that new job glow. He presumably has a high opinion of the people who believe he's the man for the job. But that perception will soon change because Manchester United are a shambles behind the scenes.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada have come under intense scrutiny from supporters recently, having presided over some shambolic decision-making. But they are not the only culprits.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 5 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are responsible for much of the mess (Image: Jacob King/Press Association)

Sir Jim Ratcliffe is the minority shareholder, but it is he who has the final say on decisions after the Glazer family ceded control of sporting operations to INEOS when they took over two and a half years ago. That has created a muddied picture behind the scenes, with reports of friction surfacing amid their dreadful start to the season.

Pochettino is currently viewed in a very good light by his employers, but in order to be a long-term success at Old Trafford, he will need more than that: a football manager, a politician and a diplomat all rolled into one.

‌



2. Fractured dressing room

As is often the case towards the end of a manager's tenure, the dressing room becomes leakier. But we didn't even need discreet briefings to learn the feelings of some key players, with Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez letting us know in public interviews.

Ex-United boss Erik ten Hag recently said there was a "toxic culture" inside the dressing room during his spell in charge due to players like Cristiano Ronaldo, Casemiro and Raphael Varane having too much influence. It is easy to see comparisons with the current crop.

Another issue is that, despite their miserable results, Carrick left with plenty of lingering goodwill from the players. His "casual" approach - as Roy Keane put is last weekend - may have been problematic, but it also made him popular among the players. Pochettino now has to win them over.

View 5 Images Manchester United's players will need picking up (Image: Ed Sykes/Getty Images)

‌



3. Leaky defence

United are 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 games, so there are obviously multiple issues on the pitch. But the most glaring is undoubtedly in defence, where they have been embarrassing at times.

One clean sheet all season, which came against Sabah. Thirty goals conceded in all competitions - the joint most of any side in Europe's top five leagues along with Crystal Palace and Sassuolo.

Pochettino has to start from the back. He is known for stressing the need for top-level fitness in order to implement his high-intensity pressing game. But he needs to sort out the basics first and foremost.

View 5 Images Manchester United's defence has been their biggest issue this season

‌



For a team boasting experienced players like Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw, there has been a distinct lack of leadership. Senne Lammens isn't a vocal presence in goal. The expensively-assembled new-look midfield isn't protecting the back four. And, as the inexplicable errors by Leny Yoro and Diogo Dalot against Aston Villa showed, confidence is at rock-bottom.

4. 'Lack of effort'

United have consistently been out-run by their opponents this season, with the issue coming into focus around their 1-1 draw with Fulham in September. Gary Neville branded the players an "absolute disgrace" for walking around. "I've never seen such a lack of effort," he raged on Sky Sports post-match.

Effort is the cornerstone of most teams - and is particularly important to Pochettino. Carrick, Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Jose Mourinho and Ruben Amorim all had to fight back against a perception of players coasting. And Pochettino will be no different.

Only Liverpool average less than United's average total of 102.4km per match in the Premier League this season. You suspect Pochettino will have something to say about that.

‌



View 5 Images Mauricio Pochettino will get to work on the training pitch next week (Image: Omar Vega/Getty Images)

5. Paper-thin squad

Pochettino will be fully aware of the task facing him - and the players at his disposal. United's failure to sign a left-back or striker in the summer transfer window - in which they focused instead on midfield - has left them short of depth.

Benjamin Sesko's injury has forced Bryan Mbeumo to play up front, while Shaw's absence has seen Dalot fill in badly at left-back. Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Maguire are all also currently listed as injured.

The January transfer window can't come soon enough, but even then Pochettino is very unlikely to be backed with millions. The loan market is expected to be targeted, meaning expectations have already been tempered.

‌

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino's first job must be getting rid of Bruno Fernandes - he's trouble at Man Utd
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino's first job must be getting rid of Bruno Fernandes - he's trouble at Man Utd

If Mauricio Pochettino wants to succeed at Manchester United, he needs to be bold and kick troublemaker Bruno Fernandes to the curb

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino has a big Bruno Fernandes problem (Image: Adam Davy/Press Association)

When Mauricio Pochettino walks through the doors at Manchester United, his to-do list will stretch from Stretford all the way to Buenos Aires. But his first, most urgent task shouldn't require much deliberation.

‌



‌



He needs to call Bruno Fernandes into his office, shake his hand, and tell him to pack his bags for January.

‌



News that Fernandes has turned his nose up at United's latest contract offer this week has sparked an understandable flutter of anxiety within Old Trafford's leaking corridors. With his current deal expiring at the end of the season, albeit with a one-year extension option sitting in United's back pocket, the conventional wisdom says Pochettino must move heaven and earth to keep his captain sweet.

‌



But conventional wisdom at Manchester United has been dead wrong for over a decade. Fernandes isn't the solution to the club's malaise - he's one of its primary carriers.

Mauricio Pochettino's wife had brutal four word reaction after press conference READ MORE :

When will Mauricio Pochettino first take charge of Man Utd and his likely starting XI? READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Of course, the standard defence of the 32-year-old is always the same: Look at his goals and assists. This is the great Fernandes illusion - the soothing myth that because the numbers on his Wikipedia page look healthy, he must be some sort of lone genius propping up a crumbling empire. Take five minutes to actually watch him, though, and the whole thing unravels like a cheap suit.

‌



Strip away the penalty kicks - harvested with that little theatrical hop once the hard work has already been done - and the corners dutifully aimed at Casemiro's forehead, and what are you actually left with? A midfielder who pads his stats when the pressure is off, when the points are already in the bag, or when the stakes couldn't flatter him more.

For nearly seven years, Fernandes' gaudy chance-creation statistics have served as a convenient smokescreen, disguising a fair-weather talisman in a midfield that cannot keep the ball, control the tempo, or hold its shape against halfway-competent opposition.

‌



Worse still, when the roof is caving in, and United desperately need someone to grab a massive fixture by the scruff of the neck and twist it to his will, Fernandes simply evaporates. He doesn't boss big games - he merely attends them as an outraged spectator, hovering on the peripheries like a man furiously disputing an erroneous restaurant bill.

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes behaviour on and off the pitch has sparked plenty of debate (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Another giant fly in the ointment is how wildly unsuited he is to the tactical regime about to arrive. Pochettino's entire managerial philosophy is built on relentless, lungs-on-fire pressing, synchronised sprinting, and ego-free collective graft. Asking Bruno Fernandes to function inside that kind of disciplined, high-velocity machine is like asking a grumpy cat to enjoy a bubble bath. He can't do it, and - most exhausting of all - he will spend 90 minutes moaning about being asked to try.

And that, really, is the rotting core of the whole enterprise. For all his padded goal contributions, Fernandes is a roaring net negative because of the thick atmospheric poison he pumps into the club. The signature arm-flapping, the theatrical scowls, the slumped shoulders of a wounded martyr. It isn't passion. It's performative con-artistry of the highest order.

‌



Every time Fernandes throws his hands to the heavens after a misplaced pass, he is cynically beaming a coded message to the Stretford End: Look at me. I'm the only one trying. These clowns around me are letting us all down. It's sneaky, deeply self-serving, and faintly villainous. While his team-mates absorb the brickbats raining down from the stands, the skipper stages a one-man pantomime of aggrieved perfection to keep his own halo polished.

We saw the mask slip entirely during his shabby little meltdown with Michael Carrick. Hooked off against Como after a poor performance, Fernandes didn't swallow his pride and take his seat on the bench like a grown-up. He threw his manager straight under the bus, openly slating Carrick's tactics in public with all the petulance of a toddler spitting out lukewarm broccoli.

‌



There was a nauseating whiff of late-stage Cristiano Ronaldo about the whole episode: Look at how I have suffered. I am the most important person in this building, so to hell with the manager, the squad, and the badge.

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes could cause Mauricio Pochettino a big headache (Image: Omar Vega, Getty Images)

‌



And this, remember, is the man wearing the captain's armband at Manchester United. A club that has spent over a decade drowning in an excuse-making, accountability-free dressing room culture is being led by a chief whinger who actively models the exact behaviour that has ruined them. Instead of whipping slackers into shape, Fernandes legitimises sulking as a leadership style.

Pochettino's greatest trick as a manager has always been alchemy - welding a group of fresh, hungry players into a tight-knit unit where everyone pulls in the exact same direction. Keeping Fernandes around makes that impossible. You cannot build a church while the bell-ringer is setting fire to the pews.

‌



Fortunately, this contract standoff hands United and Pochettino a gift-wrapped escape hatch. With his current deal expiring in June, the temptation among the bean-counters might be to trigger that one-year extension option just to protect his transfer value.

But United must resist the urge. Extending his deal only drags out the soap opera, keeps his gargantuan wages on the books, and chains Pochettino to a mutinous skipper for another 18 months. It would be a triumph of accountancy over common sense.

‌



Instead, they must be ruthless. Stick him in the shop window and sell him in January while someone, perhaps in Saudi Arabia, is still willing to pay good money for him. Rip the armband off, hand it to someone whose first instinct in a crisis isn't to throw a strop, and let Pochettino stamp his authority on the place from day one.

United won't miss Fernandes half as much as the G/A fetishists and YouTube highlight-reel fans will claim. Football isn't played on paper or in Excel columns, and matches aren't won with hollow individual statistics.

Manchester United have spent far too long mistaking a noisy soloist for an orchestra. If Pochettino is to get this broken ensemble playing in harmony, his very first act must be to politely, but firmly, escort the soloist off stage.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick breaks silence on Man Utd sacking with emotional open letter
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick breaks silence on Man Utd sacking with emotional open letter

Michael Carrick has issued a public statement after being sacked by Manchester United

View 3 Images Michael Carrick was sacked by Manchester United on Thursday morning (Image: Martin Rickett/Press Association)

Michael Carrick has broken his silence after being sacked by Manchester United. He was finally dismissed by the club on Thursday afternoon after a meeting with United chief executive Omar Berrada.

‌



‌



Carrick was handed the United job on a permanent basis after guiding the club to a third-placed finish having taken over from the sacked Ruben Amorim. The ex-United midfielder could not transfer the momentum he accrued from the previous campaign into this season, as the Reds are now struggling in 18th place.

‌



He only picked up one Premier League victory in ten games this season, a run which has cost him his job. After Mauricio Pochettino's appointment by United was confirmed, Carrick uploaded a letter to his former players and the fan base.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

In a statement uploaded to Instagram, he said: "I've had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love. There are very few who get to live and feel it, and for that I'm incredibly grateful. With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means.

"It's different to anywhere else. Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.

‌



"It's a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day. I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick's final game in charge of Manchester United was a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. (Image: Michael Regan, Getty Images)

‌



"We've had some great times this year and moments we'll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.

"I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies. I know we've not had the results lately, but you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way. That means more than a win or two. That's what makes you who you are. That's why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.

‌



"A special thank you to my coaching staff. You gave me everything you had, every single day, and I couldn't have asked for any more. I'm incredibly grateful for your loyalty, hard work and support throughout.

View 3 Images The Man Utd board believe Michael Carrick has better players than the current league position suggests (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

‌



"To all the staff behind the scenes, thank you for everything you do for this football club. So much of your work goes unseen, but it never goes unappreciated.

"And to the players, thank you for your efforts and the moments we've shared. I wish you all the very best for what's ahead. I want nothing but success for Manchester United.

Article continues below

"This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I'll always be proud to have played my part and I'll always want the very best for it. I'll be right there with you from now on, watching from the side-lines, cheering the lads on. Michael."

Sports.title: McGinn double seals win for ragged Scotland
Sports.content:
Match report as John McGinn scores twice in Scotland's win over North Macedonia at Hampden; Aston Villa midfielder gives hosts lead after McTominay and Gilmour go close; Rastoder's header levels scoring; McGinn penalty seals win after Gannon-Doak fouled; Scotland face Switzerland next

John McGinn's double rescued Scotland as they toiled to a 2-1 win over North Macedonia to keep their Nations League promotion hopes alive.

The hosts were booed off at half-time with the game goalless but there was a sense of relief - rather than joy - at the final whistle after McGinn's penalty secured the three points after Elmin Rastoder's header cancelled out the Aston Villa midfielder's opener.

The win means Scotland can still finish second in Group B1 after Slovenia were held by Switzerland, but will have to win in St Gallen on Monday and hope North Macedonia do them a favour in their final game.

Image: Andy Robertson equalled Sir Kenny Dalglish's appearance record

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli secured his first win at Hampden on a night when skipper Andy Robertson earned his 102nd cap to equal the appearance record held by Sir Kenny Dalglish.

The returning Scott McTominay nearly grabbed an opener after 16 minutes but he was denied by Stole Dimitrievski in the North Macedonia goal after turning and shooting sharply. The keeper then denied Che Adams and McTominay again before the Napoli midfielder attempted to recreate his famous Denmark overhead kick to no avail.

Boos rang around Hampden as the players trudged off at the interval and Billy Gilmour did little to lift the collective mood straight after the break when he fired over with the goal gaping following good work by Adams.

Image: Scotland's Scott McTominay goes close

Scotland did take the lead soon after, however, Adams outmuscling his North Macedonian counterpart to set the onrushing McGinn away into the box before he curled his effort into the net.

Rastoder stunned Hampden less than three minutes later, leaping highest to glance his header past Angus Gunn from a corner, but Dimitrievski went from hero to villain with a little over 15 minutes remaining, bringing down Ben Gannon-Doak when the winger seemed to be running the ball out of play.

Image: North Macedonia's Elmin Rastoder scored to make it 1-1 against Scotland

A VAR review followed, allowing McGinn to step up and deliver a first win in Glasgow for Pocognoli, but it is a performance that will raise more questions than answers.

The key moments from Hampden Park

16: BIG SAVE! Scott McTominay controls the ball with his back to the goal, then turns sharply and shoots but Stole Dimitrievski gets down well to his left and keeps it out.

22: OVER! Andy Robertson delivers a free-kick into the box but Kieran Tierney's header loops over the bar.

27: SAVE! John McGinn's corner is met by Che Adams at the front post before his header takes a big deflection. It looks like it's heading in but Dimitrievski is equal to it again.

35: OVER! McTominay tries an acrobatic effort with an overhead kick but it sails over the bar and out of play.

39: MCTOMINAY DENIED! The ball is threaded into the feet of McTominay and he shoots from a tight angle but the goalkeeper makes another save to keep it level!

46: HOW HAS HE MISSED?! Adams capitalises on a loose back pass and squares the ball to Billy Gilmour. All he has to do is guide it on target and it is a goal but he skies it over the bar!

54: GOAL! Adams outmuscles the defender before poking the ball forward allowing McGinn to race onto it before curling the opener into the back of the net.

57: GOAL! North Macedonia shock Scotland with a quickfire equaliser. The corner is whipped into the box and Rastoder is there to glance it into the bottom corner.

75: GOAL! McGinn scores from the spot to restore Scotland's lead

Pocognoli 'satisfied' with first home win

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sebastien Pocognoli was pleased after his first home win with Scotland against North Macedonia in the Nations League, hoping that it will 'helps build a winning culture'.

Scotland head coach Sebastian Pocognoli:

"I'm happy to get the first win at home. It's important and we knew before the game that it will help to build a winning culture.

"In terms of what we produced on the pitch, I know exactly what we worked on this week. I'm quite satisfied about what I saw in some moments of the game, the work on the ball and off the ball.

"It was not always perfect, but I know that what we worked on in the last two days happened many times on the pitch. And for me that's very important. On top of that, we created a lot of chances that we should score.

"Off the ball, I think we were quite aggressive. We recovered a number of balls that we managed well in some moments of transition. We created a big chance for Billy (Gilmour) from this also. So that's a new approach of the game. Not everything was perfect, but there was a lot to take to move forward.

Image: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli was satisfied with the win over North Macedonia

"After the first goal, I think we need to learn to not drop the intensity. Because after the first goal, for five minutes, I really feel like we dropped the intensity and the focus. And we conceded a goal from a set-piece. And I had the same feeling after the second goal. So, it's something that we need to fix."

Robertson: We have to be patient with new style

Scotland captain Andy Robertson speaking to BBC Sport:

"I thought we showed glimpses of good stuff. We tried to be patient on the ball, tried to keep the ball, I think we did that well at times, but also at times it broke down because the quality wasn't there at times so we're still trying to piece it all together.

Image: Andy Robertson says Scotland are adapting to a new style

"It's a different way of playing and that's what we are working on in the training ground. It wasn't always perfect, but no international game is easy and we're all delighted in the changing room to get that win and hopefully other people have a smile on their face too.

"Every formation can be played differently, there are so many different variations of this formation. We're trying to implement what the manager and coaches want us to do on the training ground and we're working really hard.

"Yes, it's not going to be perfect right away but everything is working towards us going into the qualifiers for the Euros. We're still trying to learn it and we believe in what the manager is trying to teach us to do and we have to be patient with that.

"I know people don't see us train and see the work we're doing in the background, so I can get why people are frustrated but there is an idea behind what we are doing and like you say at times we lacked that quality.

Image: Andy Robertson applauds the fans after Scotland's win over North Macedonia

"Obviously the Slovenia at home game made it unrealistic, or tougher [to qualify]. We'll go over to Monday and we'll give everything we can to win that game. We're in a position where we have to rely on other results."

On equaling Dalglish's appearance record: "It feels amazing for me and my family, it's an amazing achievement. I've been around here for a long time. I've had highs, I've had lows, I've sometimes had praise and had criticism."

McGinn praises 'amazing' Robertson

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player John McGinn hails Andy Robertson after he matched Kenny Dalglish’s caps record against North Macedonia.

John McGinn to Sky Sports on Andy Robertson's record-equalling night:

"Amazing - he deserves everything that is coming his way. The biggest credit I can give him is that he is always available, always willing to help his country. Whether he is at 60, 70, 80 per cent, or 100.

"I'm sure Monday will be a special occasion for him but he'll give the boring answer that it will only be special if we get three points."

Analysis: McGinn takes centre stage on record-equalling night for Robertson

It will be a night that Andy Robertson never forgets but a game most Scotland fans will blank from their collective memories fairly quickly.

Image: Andy Robertson and John McGinn celebrate after Scotland's win

The skipper equalled Sir Kenny Dalglish's record of 102 caps but it was fellow Scotland stalwart John McGinn who spared the home side's blushes on a drab evening in Glasgow.

Scotland looked slow in their build-up, even if there were first-half chances, but when the goal finally did come the floodgates did not open. Instead, North Macedonia, who hadn't scored since November 18, 2025, equalised and could have gone in front.

The natives were understandably restless but were ultimately relieved when Stole Dimitrievski clumsily brought down Gannon-Doak, allowing McGinn to be the hero again.

Image: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli celebrates

The Aston Villa captain was quick to remind everyone that a new style takes time to bed in and that is true. Scotland are moving away from the comforts and success of the Steve Clarke era, but questions will be asked of Pocognoli's insistence on using wing-backs and one upfront at home with a comfortable win expected.

Scotland have something to play for when they travel to Switzerland for their final Group B1 game, with promotion still up for grabs. Robertson should play on Monday to become Scotland's most-capped player outright. How sweet it would be if his 103rd appearance for his country was a winning one.

Sports.title: France put injuries behind them to stun Springboks
Sports.content:
Nations Championship - France 21-19 South Africa: Les Bleus put injuries behind them to hold on and stun Springboks in Paris

Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang was among the try-scorers as France pulled off an epic victory over South Africa

France put a raft of injuries behind them to withstand huge pressure and defeat South Africa 21-19 in a stunning Nations Championship victory in Paris.

The win is only the second for Les Bleus over the Springboks in the last 11 contests, with the hosts playing sensationally in the first half and digging in to survive and get over the line in the second.

Back-three Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Théo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey each scored tries in the opening half, with France belying the fact they had to play Antoine Dupont at 10 due to four fly-halves being out injured (Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack, Thomas Ramos, Antoine Hastoy).

All three tries were converted by Maxime Lucu, with France 21-7 ahead at the half-time break, but the second half proved entirely different.

France 21-19 South Africa - Score summary France - Tries: Grandidier-Nkanang (15), Attissogbe (24), Bielle-Biarrey (32). Cons: Lucu (16,24,33). South Africa - Tries: Wessels (30), Reinach (51), Marx (72). Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu (31,52).

Though South Africa were shown a 20-minute red card to back-row Cobus Wiese for an illegal ruck clear-out, France coughed up sin-bins to Lucu, Grandidier-Nkanang and Régis Montagne - the latter as a result of scrum penalties which kept flowing the visitors' way.

Scrum-half Cobus Reinach and hooker Malcom Marx scored tries in the second half for South Africa - adding to a first-half Jan-Hendrik Wessels effort - but Manie Libbok crucially missed the third conversion and the chance to draw level.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

South Africa's wholesale front-row changes less than an hour before kick-off - swapping their starting front-row for their replacements - had ​little impact on France's fast start, with Dupont floating between fly-half and scrum-half from the off in a marvellous individual performance.

The match was considered a potential preview of the final at Twickenham in two weeks, but while France are closing in on representing the northern hemisphere - England and Ireland are now six points behind with two games to play - South Africa may not make it.

The Springboks will be overtaken atop the southern hemisphere standings and lose their No 1 world ranking if undefeated New Zealand beat Wales on Saturday in Cardiff, as expected.

On Friday, the Springboks closed to 21-14 with 30 minutes to go, revving up their power game for a grandstand finish.

France were bleeding penalties - nine in the scrum alone - but desperate scramble defence roused a packed Stade de France.

South Africa's Pieter-Steph du Toit was held up over the try-line late on, while Lucu - France's goalkicker with an 85 per cent success rate - ramped up the tension when he missed a straightforward penalty attempt that would have given France a 10-point lead.

Springboks hooker Marx inevitably scored from a rolling maul but Libbok, on for Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, botched the conversion attempt that would have levelled the score with eight minutes left.

The Boks had one last chance in the final minute, but Bielle-Biarrey stopped the charge and Dupont jumped on the loose ball, earning Lucu the chance to kick out and end a gripping Test match.

Dupont: We kept intensity up the whole match - 'That's huge for us'

France fly-half Antoine Dupont told ITV:

"I feel tired! They [South Africa] are really intense during the 80 minutes.

"It was so hard today with the yellow cards. We kept the intensity the whole game, and that's a huge thing for us today.

"We tried to adapt [Dupont at fly-half], we just had one day of training this week.

"I tried with Max [Lucu] to have the best combination possible. In attack and defence.

"With the energy of the entire team, it worked."

What's next?

For France, they next face Argentina in their third Nations Championship Test of the autumn at the Stade de France in Paris on Saturday, November 21 (8.10pm kick-off).

South Africa travel to face Ireland at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin for their next Test, also on Saturday November 21 (4.40pm kick-off).

Sports.title: Adames fights Warburton as Bentley targets 2027 bout with champion
Sports.content:
WBC world champion Carlos Adames fights Wales’ Gerome Warburton on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Mix from 4pm.

Adames is the reigning WBC middleweight world champion but is tuning up for major title fights next year with a non-title bout against Warburton at a 165lb catchweight.

Adames has an impressive track record. Undefeated at middleweight he's taken top-class wins over Sergiy Derevyanchenko, Julian Williams, Terrell Gausha and Austin Williams. He was unfortunate to be held to a draw against Hamzah Sheeraz, too.

Warburton, a former Welsh champion, has not operated at that level, but this fight with Adames offers him a route to the elite end of the division, if he can score an upset.

The Welshman though is coming off back-to-back wins over Nathan Heaney, the former British champion who defeated Denzel Bentley, who went on afterwards to win a world championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Denzel Bentley landed a big right hand to floor Shane Mosley Jr in the second round before boxing to an impressive points victory

Bentley, stripped of his WBO title before his recent victory over Shane Mosley Jr, is gunning to become a world champion once again. He will be a close observer of Adames vs Warburton. Bentley is targeting 2027 fights with Adames and IBF titlist Aaron McKenna.

"Early next year, I'm ready to go again," Bentley told Sky Sports. "I'd love another world title shot. McKenna or Adames, seeing as those are the two middleweights who are at this [Zuffa Boxing] stable with us and they are world champions. Those two are my priority."

He does think Adames will win and be in position to fight for his world title in 2027.

"Congrats to Warburton for getting such a massive fight. I know it's not for the title but he's fighting a champion," Bentley said.

"I expect Adames to come through that," he continued. "Warburton's a good boxer, a nice slick boxer but doesn't carry the power to give Adames any respect or stop him in his tracks.

"Adames is going to walk him down and probably get him out of there. I'd rather see Warburton go the distance. He's done well in his career."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Aaron McKenna's IBF middleweight world title fight against Etinosa Oliha

But he added: "Adames gets him out of there, pretty early if I'm being honest."

He will be waiting for Adames. "If he's well enough to go into his mandatory early next year, we can fight maybe summer, a little bit after the summer," Bentley said.

"I'll be happy to wait till after the summer, if it's guaranteed [to be] Adames. If it's not, then I'd like to get out early next year. But if it could be him I'd be happy to wait for that."

Watch Carlos Adames fight Gerome Warburton this Saturday live on Sky Sports Mix from 4pm.

Sports.title: Warner claims sandpapergate investigation 'stinks of a cover-up'
Sports.content:
David Warner has claimed Cricket Australia’s investigation into the 2018 ball tampering scandal “stinks of a cover-up”.

Usman Khawaja's claims in his new autobiography reignited the controversy that rocked Australian cricket eight years ago, with the former opening batter stating that the entire Australian team knew sandpaper was being used to alter the ball before their Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018.

Instagram Instagram , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enable Instagram cookies or to allow those cookies just once. You can change your settings at any time via the This content is provided by, which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enablecookies or to allow those cookies just once. You can change your settings at any time via the Privacy Options Unfortunately we have been unable to verify if you have consented to Instagram cookies. To view this content you can use the button below to allow Instagram cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

Warner has now doubled down on his criticisms of Cricket Australia's probe into the saga, claiming they had not interviewed three of the bowlers - Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon - who featured in that Test, as part of what he called a "shoddy investigation".

"As far as I am aware, CA [Cricket Australia] did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation," Warner wrote in a post on Instagram.

"If that's correct, then how can CA push the idea that their bowlers didn't know?

"It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning, ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea.

"That stinks of a cover-up."

Sky Sports News have contacted Cricket Australia for comment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Warner previously backed Usman Khawaja's claims that the entire team knew about 2018 ball-tampering plan against South Africa / Credit: @davidwarner31

Cricket Australia will not open new investigation

Previously, Warner had said Cricket Australia's investigation into the sandpaper scandal was "rushed and botched", with the former opener issuing his support to Khawaja during a statement issued on Monday.

In his autobiography 'Sabr: Finding my way in cricket and in life', Khawaja said he was not called for an interview by Cricket Australia in the wake of sandpapergate.

Warner and then-captain Steve Smith both received 12-month bans, while Cameron Bancroft was handed a nine-month suspension.

Cummins, Starc, Lyon and Hazlewood were not punished and issued a joint statement in 2021 explaining they had no knowledge that ball-tampering was taking place.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Khawaja said he was not called for an interview following the sandpaper scandal

On Saturday, Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg told Australian radio station SEN that the governing body would not be re-opening the investigation.

"We don't see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again," Greenberg said.

"I don't think there's anything that can be gained from that.

"We have said we're comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we've received. That includes what we've seen from Usman [Khawaja], and our position hasn't changed on that.

"There's absolutely no benefit in going back, that's the clear position of the CA board. I think it's fine, we've got to look ahead, and the matter was dealt with under a previous leadership back in 2018.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Khawaja claimed the entire Australian dressing room knew sandpaper was being used

"Trying to second-guess decisions from a previous time or making an assessment through the prism of hindsight is not something we want to do."

He added: "When you cut to the core of the challenge that we face here, Usman's version of events is inconsistent with what others have had to say.

"I can assure you there are lots of other players who have a very, very different version of events. And they have made that very public from the very start of 2018, they have been very consistent in their position right through until today.

"From my conversations with many over the weekend, I don't think that will change either."

Warner hits out at Cummins

Following Khawaja's revelations, both Cummins and Starc have denied any knowledge of sandpapergate, with the current Australia captain rejecting Khawaja's claims during a press conference on Friday.

"When he [Khawaja] says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, ​he's 100 per cent wrong. I've said that consistently for the last eight years," ‌Cummins told reporters.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Warner claimed Test captain Pat Cummins had thrown Khawaja under a bus, after he denied knowledge of sandpapergate on Friday

Warner, though, hit back at the Australian Test captain's comments, saying he had "thrown Khawaja under a bus".

"Pat Cummins was very well-prepared this morning [Friday]. I still stick by Uzzie, and what he's written in that book," Warner said.

"It is the truth, and I really, really support him. I actually feel for him at the moment; I feel that the captain today threw Uzzie under the bus, and I'm very, very disappointed about that.

"All three of us have paid a big price in this. I hadn't spoken to 'Banger' [Bancroft] in eight years, but at the end of the day, we have to live with these consequences daily. We've got to live with these consequences daily, and we've been served a life punishment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fast bowler Mitchell Starc denied any knowledge of sandpaper being used

"So, when other people talk about how they've been affected by it, there's nothing worse for me, Steve [Smith] and Cameron [Bancroft], who have to walk out there every single day.

"We cop abuse. Yes, we accepted it. But my wife and I paid the greatest price; we lost a baby during that time. That's why it really hurts me the most, until the truth is accepted."

Sports.title: Choi pushing for first LPGA win at The Annika as Korda drops back
Sports.content:
Hye-Jin Choi opened with two bogeys, made up ground with a 15-foot eagle putt late and finished with a three-under 67 on Friday that gave her part of a three-way share of the lead at The Annika.

It was far more effective than the bogey-free round of Nelly Korda, the No. 1 player who could only laugh at her clean card because it was cleaner than she would have preferred - 15 straight pars, one birdie, two closing pars for a 69.

That left Korda four shots behind going into the weekend at Pelican Golf Club, where a victory would make the 28-year-old American eligible for the LPGA Hall of Fame.

"I had a lot of chances," said Korda, competing for the first time in two months. "But you can just tell that from yesterday morning to today afternoon with the wind, that's what the defence of this golf course is. It's as fast as Bermuda as I've putted on throughout my career."

It wasn't a problem for Solheim Cup star Carlota Ciganda, who birdied her last four holes for a 63 to join Choi and Lindy Duncan (66) atop the leaderboard at 12-under 128.

Image: Nelly Korda has dropped further behind the leaders. (AP Photo/Chris O'Meara)

The Japanese duo of Mao Saigo (65) and Minami Katsu (69) were two shots behind.

Choi has been an LPGA member for five years and it has been a curious chase for that first LPGA victory, particularly since she was 17 when she had a late lead in the 2017 US Women's Open and wound up as a runner-up.

She also had two good chances at winning during the recent Asia swing, where she was runner-up in Shanghai and South Korea.

Choi was playing in the group with Korda for the opening two rounds, which she believes has tested her enough to calm her nerves on the weekend. She wasn't rattled by the bogey-bogey start, or the bogey on the par-five 14th, her fifth hole of the round.

She pieced together enough birdies to regain some momentum, then hit an approach that got a nice kick around the green and rolled out to just under 15 feet for eagle on the par-five seventh.

"I have two rounds left, but I have recently played in a champion group on the tournament before, so I have that experience and I'm going just try my best and concentrate on my game," Choi said.

Scoring was low enough in the opening round that one-under 139 made the cut. This is the final regular-season event of the year, and the top 60 in the Race to CME Globe advance to the finale next week in Naples, where the winner gets $2 million.

Julia Lopez Ramirez of Spain, who defeated Yealimi Noh in a crucial singles match in her Solheim Cup debut, was among those at nine-under 131. That was important for the Spaniard, who came into the week at No. 66 in the Race to the CME Globe.

Image: Charley Hull was five shots off the leaders on seven-under. (AP Photo/Chris O'Meara)

Duncan, the 35-year-old Floridian, has yet to win on the LPGA Tour and this was the first time she had at least a share of the lead through 36 holes. She went 2-1 in her Solheim Cup debut.

"The week has gone by really fast, which is sometimes a good thing," Duncan said. "Because if you're playing a lot and you get some momentum going, that's kind of a nice way to play. So it's just been kind of rolling with it."

Charley Hull was five shots off the leaders on seven-under after shooting 67 on Friday. England's Lottie Woad finished the second round level with Hull on seven-under.
