Sports.title: Lawson to stay in F1 as Racing Bulls announces 2027 driver pairing
Sports.content:
Racing Bulls has confirmed Liam Lawson will stay with the team for the 2027 Formula 1 campaign, partnering Arvid Lindblad for a second, straight season.

They have formed a formidable duo this year having propelled Racing Bulls to fifth in the championship, which is set to be the Anglo-Italian team's best-ever result.

Despite sitting on 89 points, however, compared to 38 for rookie Lindblad, Lawson's future was in doubt thanks to junior driver Nikola Tsolov starring in F2 this year.

The 19-year-old Bulgarian is second in the standings and has been handed private testing opportunities and a rookie FP1 session in Mexico as part of his junior driver duties.

So Racing Bulls was weighing up its need for short-term performance against its explicit goal of training young drivers for parent team Red Bull.

But with Lawson rising to the occasion in recent weeks, performing some of his strongest races under constant pressure, the 24-year-old has effectively been too good for the team to ignore.

Nikola Tsolov Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Sources indicated to Autosport in Brazil last weekend that amid a big push for the company's top leadership to back Tsolov, the pendulum swung back towards Lawson's favour with his performances over the Americas triple-header.

Read Also: Formula 1 How the Racing Bulls pendulum is swinging back towards Lawson

So the Kiwi has now signed a fresh deal for 2027 with team boss Alan Permane saying he had "no doubt" that the squad will field the strongest possible line-up next season.

"We’re delighted to be continuing with Liam and Arvid for 2027," he said. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we’ve seen the progress they’ve made, both individually and as a pairing.

“I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition.

“Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027."

Next year is set to be Lawson’s third, full season in F1 having made his debut at Zandvoort towards the back end of the 2023 campaign - having another partial season in 2024.

Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

"I’m very happy to be continuing with Visa Cash App Racing Bulls next year,” he said. “We’ve had a brilliant season together and the team has worked very hard to produce a fast car, which I’ve loved driving.

“It feels great to be part of a historic season for the team as we continue our fight for P5 in the constructors' championship. It's a testament to the hard work of everyone both at track, and back at the factory.

"I’m looking forward to carrying this moment forward with Arvid through to 2027. We’re building something super positive and I’m excited by what we can achieve together.”

Lawson is currently eighth in the drivers’ standings with Lindblad in 11th ahead of the final three rounds: Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

"Looking back on my first season in Formula 1, it's been a truly special year, full of new experiences and learnings since the very first pre-season test," said 19-year-old Lindblad.

"I can't wait to get started next year, building on everything I've learned during my rookie season. It's set to be an exciting year, and I look forward to continuing to drive alongside Liam."

Sports.title: What the Brazilian GP revealed about F1's ability to cope with rain
Sports.content:
The question of what might happen in a wet race has vexed Formula 1's stakeholders since before the beginning of the season. It's also prompted some unnecessarily hysterical commentary throughout the year, peaking in the run-up to last weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos, where rain for qualifying and the race was a virtual certainty for the first time this season.

Although the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was interrupted by rain and the discovery of a software glitch, by the time the race got going the track was drying quickly. This was not the case in Brazil.

Qualifying at Interlagos was red-flagged for 80 minutes after a downpour coincided with the start of the session, and many media outlets alighted on a spicy George Russell quote in the aftermath.

"I love driving in the rain here but, at some point, if that was a race, there was no way we should be driving in that because the chances of seeing a really, really horrific incident are very, very high," he said.

Perfect headline material for a noisy story, but context was lacking. The general consensus within the paddock after that session was that the FIA made the right calls at the right time, immediately suspending Q1 during the initial downpour, then applying great rigour to identify a safe ‘window' to restart it.

"In general, I want to race, but yesterday [Saturday] I think it was the perfect call," said Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur after the race. "When we did the first [Q1] lap before the red flag, we came back with two centimetres of water in the car…"

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Carlos Sainz, Williams, Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Those conditions were too wet to stage any kind of track activity beyond a boat race in the pitlane. The real questions surrounded how the cars and the latest generation of tyres would perform in the kind of wet and/or rapidly changing circumstances in which qualifying and the race could actually be staged.

Historically, Pirelli's heavily treaded ‘extreme' wet tyres are rarely seen, since too much of their operating window sits outside the margin of what is considered to be acceptable racing conditions. They displace massive quantities of water but the tread blocks overheat too quickly as the track dries. By the time the track is wet enough to justify the ‘extreme' tyre, a red flag is usually imminent.

The intermediate tyres have therefore been the wet-weather boots of choice, but this year's are understood to be too ‘hard' and slow to come up to operating temperature. Pirelli just hasn't been able to accomplish like-for-like running with the narrower wheels mandated for this season, given the testing restrictions.

It's long been feared that lack of grip from the new intermediates, combined with the more brutal torque delivery of the latest generation of engines, would make the 2026 F1 cars dangerously undriveable in the wet. Hence the outbreak of hysteria ahead of the Brazil weekend.

What actually transpired was less dramatic, and more nuanced. The nature of the track surface at Interlagos meant driveability was occasionally an issue, but not always. In the background, the FIA has been doing a lot of work since the beginning of the year to manage power delivery in these conditions.

Alexander Albon, Williams, Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

While qualifying – once it got started – offered some hope that the ‘extreme' wets are now more useable, the intermediates were a little more problematic. Kimi Antonelli went off at Turn 12 on his lap to the grid, and several other drivers reported their cars became a handful again when rain in the last 10 laps dictated a return to the intermediates.

"I think what is good is that we can use the 'big wet' much more than in the past," said Vasseur. "And this is good because it's not pushing you to use inter when it's a more 'big wet' situation, or mix between the two, and then you are taking risks.

"I think the quali was pretty good… but also the grip was completely different. You saw in the lap to the grid today that everybody was completely like hell. I think it's a difficult track with these conditions."

Pirelli's target for next year is to bring the performance of the wet-weather compounds closer together, so the intermediate warms up faster and the ‘extreme' is more resistant to wear. But this is a challenge to engineer because the tracks differ so much in terms of the energy going through the tyres.

"It was difficult to fire them up but they also wore quite quickly," said Alex Albon, who finished 15th in Brazil.

"So even when they're cold, they're wearing and it just feels like they never overheat, or they never level up to temperature. And then by the time you're circulating, the tread's already come off the tyre and then you're already struggling, you're sliding around. So, you never feel good at any point in the race; it never feels like it comes alive."

This would explain some of the peculiarities of the opening laps, where those at the front of the grid found themselves having to be super-cautious because they couldn't feel the grip – while some of those towards the rear, who spent less time waiting for lights-out, got strong getaways.

Even among those there was a variance: Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton quickly broke through to the top 10 from 20th and 21st on the grid, only for Hamilton to then go backwards as his car developed massive oversteer snaps. Verstappen, like Antonelli, then found his car less performant on the slicks.

Wet conditions added to the drama of qualifying Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

This mixed spread of performance over the wet and dry tyre compounds will be tricky to unpick, but the consensus remained that the wet-weather rubber needs more development. There were minor gripes but not the disasters that were feared and noisily predicted.

"I think the level of the wet and the inter is not good enough and we need to work with Pirelli on finding a better tyre," said Carlos Sainz, "because in the mixed conditions the inter is still a very weak tyre at the rear. By the time it warms up, the front is gone.

"And the extreme, honestly, yesterday we had so much sliding and a big lack of rear grip, so still missing a bit of development on these two tyres."

While the data gathered through running in many different conditions this weekend will be useful, it's still an isolated example. What worked or didn't work at Interlagos may not translate elsewhere, given variances in surfaces and ambient temperatures.

"Quite tricky I would say," was Liam Lawson's take on racing in the wet in a 2026 F1 car.

"The biggest problem today is the [ambient] temperature was much cooler than yesterday. And so even though there was less water, on the laps of the grid the cars were nearly undriveable, and the temps were just going down.

"So, we survived the start of the race but at points when it rains a lot, the inter becomes... it's not that the standing water's too much, it's that you can't actually keep the temperature in it. So, if we're on a track like Vegas and it rains, honestly, I think we're in trouble.

"But overall, obviously we got through a weekend for the first time with these tyres."

Additional reporting by Roberto Chinchero and Guilherme Longo

Sports.title: F1 2026 calendar update: Imola off the table, no plan B if Iran war escalates
Sports.content:
The Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix which will conclude Formula 1’s 2026 season are set to proceed as planned, provided there is no dramatic escalation of the Iran war.

The Middle Eastern conflict, which started in late February as the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, has destabilised the region. The calendars of many motorsport championships have been impacted – not least F1’s, whose Saudi Arabian race was cancelled while Bahrain’s round was postponed and hosted in Malaysia.

F1 has been monitoring the situation closely, with a chilly Imola as an alternative season finale on the first weekend of December if Qatar and Abu Dhabi were unable to host their respective events.

Lusail did run its MotoGP round without major issues last weekend, though both Yamaha teams withdrew from the competition due to the geopolitical situation.

10 November was F1’s deadline to provide Imola with a final answer as to whether the Italian track would have to prepare for a grand prix in the next three weeks; it will not.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Isack Hadjar, Racing Bulls Photo by: Zak Mauger / Motorsport Images

So the 2026 season will end with the planned Las Vegas-Qatar-Abu Dhabi triple-header, with travel insurance and governments’ travel advice currently allowing it.

However, there’s a caveat: F1 is aware it cannot guarantee the situation won’t change by early December and insists it will prioritise safety if the conflict escalates.

Team bosses have been maintaining a straightforward stance on the matter – they trust F1 and the FIA to make the right calls.

“I trust them to take the best decision for all of us,” Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur commented in Mexico. “Me, personally, I want to race. It doesn't matter where, but I want to race. Now, I will go where they will tell us to go.”

“Stefano and Mohammed have been pretty clear about the situation that Formula 1 follows what the international guidelines are, whether there are travel restrictions, airlines not flying, any warnings in the region, the kind of feedback that local governments are making,” his Mercedes counterpart Toto Wolff added in Friday’s press conference at Interlagos. “So not only the promoters, but what the local governments are making. And this is what you need to rely on, in my opinion, and I'm fully with that.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“I think that if riders stand up, who know nothing geopolitically about what's going on, but have an audience that listens, I think that is something that creates media value. But I would have done the same as MotoGP management has done. You want to ride or drive, go. If you don't want to, don't go. It's as simple as that, and everybody can take their personal decisions on that, and I respect that.

“Of course, you've got to be wary of what's happening in the next few days, a few weeks, and Stefano has his finger on the pulse to monitor that. If things were to get more dangerous and we would get that feedback, then he's going to be the first one, together with Mohammed, to protect the people that were meant to travel. So that's why I'm following their guidance.

“From what I'm hearing internally, it hasn't been raised. It hasn't been a topic. But also there, if someone feels they don't feel comfortable, he or she doesn't feel comfortable travelling, then it's something that I would always respect. And maybe that's an opportunity to give somebody else a chance. It wouldn't change anything for the relationship. I've always respected that some people didn't want to go to certain grands prix, and that's how I see it at the moment.”

Additional reporting by Ronald Vording

Sports.title: Ignore social media echo chamber and trust F1 over Middle East races – Wolff | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff says Formula 1 is right to go ahead with its plans to race in the Middle East.

Many sports including other motor racing series cancelled events in the region due to the US-Iran war. However F1 commercial rights holder Liberty Media held its Moto GP event in Qatar last weekend, despite one manufacturer staying away due to concerns over the safety of travelling to the region.

F1 confirmed this week it has abandoned its back-up plan to relocate the final round of 2026 to Imola in Italy if its planned events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi cannot go ahead.

Wolff said those questioning the wisdom of racing in the Middle East should pay less attention to media coverage and listen to those in charge of the series.

“For me, with our social media feed, we are always at risk of seeing what we want to see,” he told the BBC. “I believe you need to trust what the authorities say. You need to rely on the commercial rights holder, that’s F1, and the FIA as our governing body.”

However Wolff said no staff will be forced to attend the final two rounds and anyone choosing not to could hand an opportunity to a replacement.

“I strongly support that if someone doesn’t want to go to Qatar or Abu Dhabi, personally doesn’t want to, then I’m very fine with that,” he said. “We don’t want to oblige anyone. There’s not going to be any sanctions, or so on, on teams.

“If you don’t feel right about going there, then I have respect for that, and don’t go. It gives an opportunity maybe to someone else to be tested and to see how another person would perform in the future. That’s how I would approach it.”

Sports.content:
The Daily Mail says the FIA has barred its Formula 1 reporter from attending the final three rounds of the world championship as a media representative.

It quotes a letter sent yestreday by FIA general manager Alberto Villareal regarding an article the newspaper published about Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc , whom its F1 correspondent Jonathan McEvoy called a “sneaky little b*****d”.

“The FIA considers that your article falls short of the standards of professionalism expected of media representatives accredited to cover the FIA Formula One World Championship,” said Villareal, quoted by the newspaper.

“Accordingly, the FIA has decided to exercise its discretion under the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship Accreditation Guidelines to withdraw your media accreditation for the remainder of the 2026 season, with immediate effect.”

Three rounds of the season remain in the USA, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Earlier this year Max Verstappen ordered the removal of another journalist, Giles Richards of The Guardian, from a Red Bull press conference. Verstappen was unhappy Richards asked him three months earlier whether he regretted colliding with George Russell during last year’s Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

Sports.title: Grosjean admits his single-seater career is likely over after ending IndyCar season 19th | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Former Formula 1 driver Romain Grosjean, who survived a fireball crash six years ago in Bahrain, is preparing to call time on his single-seater racing career.

Grosjean raced in F1 between 2009 and 2020, then switched to IndyCar. He completed his fifth season in the series this year but the 40-year-old admits he is unlikely to return.

“The reality is, this is probably the end for me with single-seaters,” Grosjean told Racer.

Grosjean finished on the podium three times in his first season in IndyCar with Coyne, earning the attention of top team Andretti, who hired him for the 2022 season. The team replaced him after he finished 13th in the championship for two years running,

After spending one year at Juncos Hollinger, Grosjean lost his drive for 2025, but returned with Coyne this year. The season began promisingly when he reached the final round of qualifying in St Petersburg, but a string of finishes outside the top 10 followed.

The Coyne driver finished on the podium just once all year. He ended the season 19th in the standings ahead of just six other full-time drivers, including RLL’s Mick Schumacher, who replaced him at Haas in 2021.

Grosjean said it had been a “tough” season overall. “I had [a] few amazing moments. I got the chance to lead the Indy 500. I finished in the top 10. I ran [in] the top five most of the last 60 laps. Amazing! I got a podium in Markham, which was incredible with my ‘tractor.’

“But then we go to Milwaukee and Laguna Seca, and [at] Laguna Seca, I qualified dead last, almost. I know it’s one of my fastest tracks, so I’m like, ‘I don’t want that anymore.’ I’ve had enough of those moments where you just don’t have the tools to play.”

Grosjean was supposed to contest his final grand prix at Abu Dhabi in 2020. However the burns he suffered in his Bahrain crash forced him out early. His former team Haas gave him the opportunity to test one of its cars at Mugello last year.

Sports.title: Court of Appeal to hear Audi’s case over Tsunoda decision on November 25th | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The International Court of Appeal has set a date to hear Audi’s appeal over the Italian Grand Prix stewards’ decision regarding Yuki Tsunoda.

Audi is challenging the decision not to penalise Tsunoda, who finished the race in 10th position, for triggering an extra formation lap before the start of the race.

The ICA will hear the case on November 25th at the FIA’s headquarters in Paris.

Tsunoda, who substituted for Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson at Monza, finished seven seconds ahead of Gabriel Bortoleto. Therefore the Audi driver could gain a point if Tsunoda is penalised.

Bortoleto previously said Audi’s case was “straightforward”.

F1’s sporting regulations state any driver who causes an extra formation lap must start the race from the pit lane and will receive a Stop-and-Go penalty if they fail to. As Tsunoda did not start from the pit lane, Audi believes he should receive a penalty.

The stewards ruled Tsunoda “was not the ’cause’ of the extra formation lap” and therefore did not have to start from the pit lane.

This is the second time this year the ICA has been asked to rule on a decision taken by the stewards at a grand prix. In September they reinstated two penalties which were originally issued to Pierre Gasly during the Monaco Grand Prix and later rescinded.

ICA hearing announcement

On 6th September 2026, at the end of the formation lap during the race restart following a red flag, the race director ordered an additional formation lap Following the race, the stewards investigated a potential breach of Article B5.9.4 of the 2026 FIA Formula 1 Sporting Regulations by Mr Yuki Tsunoda (driver of car number 22), which requires any driver who caused an extra formation lap to start from the end of the pit lane. Failure to do so, a Stop-and-Go penalty should be imposed on the driver. In decision number 69, the stewards decided to take no further action against Mr Yuki Tsunoda. On 9th September 2026, Audi Revolut F1 Team lodged an appeal against that decision, arguing that Mr Yuki Tsunoda had caused the extra formation lap and should therefore have received the prescribed Stop-and-Go penalty.

Sports.title: Racing Bulls keep Lawson and Lindblad as Tsolov gets Red Bull reserve role | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Racing Bulls has confirmed an unchanged driver line-up for the 2027 Formula 1 season.

Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad will continue to drive for the team next year.

The news ends speculation Red Bull’s second Formula 1 team would replace either of its drivers with Nikola Tsolov. The Red Bull junior driver lies second in the Formula 2 standings with four races remaining.

Shortly after Racing Bulls confirmed its driver line-up, Red Bull announced Tsolov as its reserve driver for 2027. Red Bull also announced Tsolov will be Racing Bulls’ reserve driver.

Racing Bulls is on course to score its best championship result under any of its identities, including its time competing as Minardi, before it was purchased by Red Bull at the end of 2005.

However Lawson’s future at the team came into doubt as Racing Bulls delayed its decision on its driver line-up for next year. Lawson made his F1 debut in 2023 and gained promotion to Red Bull in 2025 but the team dropped him after just two rounds. Lawson made a temporary return to Red Bull this year as a substitute for the injured Isack Hadjar.

During his time at Racing Bulls, Lawson has scored enough points to single-handedly put Racing Bulls fifth in the constructors’ championship. However he clashed with Red Bull driver Max Verstappen during a practice session in Mexico earlier this month, which his rival said was “not very smart behaviour” for a driver who was “fighting for [his] seat”. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies denied his team would have any say in its junior squad’s driver line-up.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane said Lawson and his rookie team mate Lindblad form “the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition”.

“Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027.”

Tsolov said he hopes to make the step up to F1 after next year. “My ambition is clear: I want to become an F1 driver,” he said. “Having the opportunity to spend next year preparing for that next step is incredibly exciting.

“I’m confident that with the team’s support and experience, I’ll have the best possible preparation to make sure I’m fully ready to take the next step onto the F1 grid when the time comes.”

Mekies said Red Bull has been highly impressed by Tsolov. “Nikola is an exceptionally talented young driver, and we have been hugely impressed by his development and performances over the past few years,” he said.

“To fight for the championship in F3 and now challenge for the F2 title in his first full season says a great deal about his ability and determination. What has impressed us just as much is his maturity, his approach to racing and his willingness to keep learning and improving.

“We have enormous belief in Nikola’s potential and see him as a driver with a very exciting future in F1. This appointment reflects our confidence in him and our commitment to his continued development. Our focus in 2027 will be on giving him the experience, tools and support he needs to be ready to race in F1 next.”

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Can Seek WBA Permit to Fight Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez can ask the WBA to let him fight Ryan Garcia first, which could extend a mandatory wait that began under Rolly Romero. Mike Coppinger reported that the WBA notified the parties of Lopez’s right to apply for a special permit to unify with the WBC welterweight champion.

February 6 is the date under discussion for Lopez and Garcia. The WBA upheld its order for Lopez to defend against Jack Catterall on November 11, and a unification still requires the association’s approval. The timing puts a February fight on the table while Catterall is still waiting for a bout the WBA originally required within 180 days of his May win over Shakhram Giyasov.

Romero took the WBA welterweight title from Garcia on May 2, 2025. The WBA ordered him to defend against Giyasov that October and gave the camps 30 days to negotiate. Romero held the belt for more than 15 months before losing it to Lopez, and the Giyasov defense never happened.

The WBA elevated Romero to Super champion in May 2026 and put its vacant Regular title up for grabs between Catterall and Giyasov. Catterall won on May 23, and the WBA’s terms called for Romero to face the winner within 180 days. Romero was allowed one optional defense in that period. Lopez took the title by majority decision on August 22 and inherited the obligation to fight Catterall. The original 180-day timetable pointed to November 19.

The WBA ordered Lopez to face Catterall on September 22 and gave the camps until October 22 to negotiate. When the association reaffirmed the order on November 11, it opened a fresh 10-calendar-day window for an agreement or an alternative proposal. Either side can request a purse bid if talks fail or one camp declines to negotiate.

Catterall’s promoter, Eddie Hearn, threatened this week to sue the WBA if it lets Lopez keep the belt and fight Garcia ahead of Catterall. “I would sue them immediately,” said Hearn on Inside the Ring.

Hearn had already predicted that Lopez would vacate the belt if the WBA insisted he fight Catterall. The southpaw’s timing and counterpunching make him a tough opponent for Lopez, who would be risking a bigger payday against Garcia by taking the mandatory first.

Fans criticizing the news on social media argued that granting a permit would be unfair to Catterall, who earned his shot in May. Some predicted the WBA would let Lopez keep the belt and fight Garcia first, leaving Catterall waiting again.

The WBA said in its November ruling that Lopez’s team had yet to submit a formal request for a unification permit. Chris Mannix reported that Lopez’s team says it filed one on November 5 and that Sports Illustrated reviewed a copy. Coppinger’s report establishes that the WBA has told the parties Lopez can apply. The association still has to decide whether to grant an exception.

Keeping the WBA belt gives Lopez more leverage when he negotiates his purse. He can offer Garcia a two-belt unification as a fellow champion. Lopez already has a following and has won titles in three divisions, so he can command a sizable purse as a challenger, too. The belt still gives his team another reason to ask for a bigger share.

The WBA belt probably makes less difference to fans. People who already follow Lopez have a reason to tune in either way. Viewers who barely know him are unlikely to buy the fight because he brings a second belt. For Catterall, that same belt is the one the WBA told him he’d get to fight for within 180 days.

The WBA created this mess by dragging its feet since May, and granting a permit now would prove that mandatory orders only apply when bigger money isn’t on the table. Lopez is clearly trying to bypass a risky fight with Catterall to get to Garcia first. If Garcia wins in February, Catterall ends up stuck waiting on a third different WBA champion while Garcia chases bigger spring fights. Without a hard deadline that the WBA actually enforces, Catterall is just holding a paper title shot that never comes due.

Sports.title: Bradley Urges Shakur Stevenson to Take Hearn Fights Without Signing
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley recommends that Shakur Stevenson find out ahead of time what fights he can get, but not sign with his Matchroom company. Stay a free agent and fight twice for Hearn, and then move on.

The pickings are kind of slim for Shakur with Matchroom, though. Even if he doesn’t sign with them, there aren’t superstar fighters that will provide him the kind of money that he was reportedly asking for when he was signed with Zuffa.

He wanted $15 million per fight and reportedly turned down a $7 million offer to fight Raymond Muratalla. If Shakur cares about money, the biggest payday he potentially gets is fighting Jaron ‘Boots’ Ennis, but he might have to go up to junior middleweight to make that fight.

Given the big production Stevenson made about wanting a 144-lb catchweight for a fight with Devin Haney, he probably won’t be excited to move up to 154 to face a puncher like Ennis.

Matchroom fighters

Giorgio Visioli

Charlie Sheehy

Alan Chaves

Note: Andy Cruz is no longer signed with Matchroom.

Dalton Smith

George Kambosos Jr.

Jack Catterall

Lewis Crocker

Paddy Donovan

Shakhram Giyasov

Conah Walker

Jaron “Boots” Ennis

Bradley wants Shakur to try and get a deal with DAZN that would allow him to work with other promoters on their platform. From there, he could fight the opponent he wants that competes on that network. The big question is whether DAZN would support the paydays Shakur wants.

Hearn brought up the idea of Shakur focusing on the undisputed championship at 140, which would put him in fights against Raymond Muratalla, Dalton Smith, Gary Antuanne Russell, and whoever wins the vacant IBF title.

The immediate question is whether Shakur fights Muratalla or gives up his WBO light welterweight belt. That would be the second straight fighter he chose not to face after he failed to make a deal with Devin Haney.

“I don’t want to be, you know, solely tied to you, but let me get these two fights. Once I get done here, I can move on to do work with another promoter,” said Bradley to Fighthub TV, describing how he would have Stevenson approach those talks. “That way it’ll be easier for him to make fights, right? “Okay, Eddie, what do you got for me? Who do you got?”

Matchroom has some good fighters, but not the ones that would lead to the type of purses Shakur was hoping for. He was paid well for his last two fights on Turki Alalshikh’s cards, getting $10 million for Teofimo Lopez and $7 million for William Zepeda, according to Sportster.com and SalarySports.com.

Perhaps the best piece of advice Bradley gave Shakur was for him to fight more often, because the ideal way to increase his popularity to get the kind of paydays that he was hoping for at Zuffa. Fighting once a year isn’t going to get it. In 2026, Shakur has only fought once, beating Teofimo.

Sports.title: Hearn Wants Diego Pacheco on the Turnbuckle Calling Out Canelo
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn wants Diego Pacheco to look so good in victory over Darius Fulghum on Saturday night that he can climb on the turnbuckle in Carson, California, and call out Canelo Álvarez and Jaime Munguia.

Super middleweight contender Pacheco (26-0, 19 KOs) will need to raise his game to look impressive enough against the big-punching Fulghum for Canelo, Munguia, and fans to take him seriously.

In recent fights, Pacheco, 25, hasn’t looked great, struggling to beat Kevin Lee Sadjo and Steven Nelson.

“Forget all this by any means necessary. You want to go and get those big fights. You want to shout out those big names. You come in here, you look sensational in front of the whole country,” said Hearn at the weigh-in on Friday about what he wants from Pacheco. “You got to be doing a job on Darius Fulghum tomorrow night and standing on that turnbuckle calling out Canelo Alvarez, calling out Jaime Munguia. And you got to get people believing in you.”

The problem is that even when the 6’4″ Pacheco is dominating, he still doesn’t look overly impressive. His game is built on jabbing, loading up on hooks, and holding. He looks awkward and gangly. Expecting him to shine against Fulghum is asking a lot, and could be dangerous because he’s going up against a big puncher.

Sadjo had Pacheco hurt several times in their fight last December. He dropped Pacheco in the eighth, forcing him into full safety-first mode for the rest of the 12-round contest. From the eighth round on, Pacheco fought to survive, prompting fans to boo.

Fulghum told Pacheco that he made a mistake by selecting him as his opponent for this fight. He says he plans on knocking him out. “Pressure bust pipes,” said Fulghum.

If Fulghum can get in close and battle him on the inside, Hearn’s hope for an impressive showing from Pacheco could go up in smoke. Fulghum could spoil everything, though there’s little chance he’ll get a fight against Canelo or Munguia next. Canelo has already mentioned Terence Crawford and Willy Hutchinson as the two on his hit list. For Pacheco, he may have to look elsewhere, toward Jacob Bank or Wilkens Mathieu.

Sports.title: Why Muhammad Ali Still Edges Joe Louis
Sports.content:
Joe Louis had the greatest heavyweight title reign. Muhammad Ali had the greater heavyweight career. Louis held the championship for nearly 12 years, and nobody has matched that run. But Ali beat Sonny Liston when few expected him to, took the title back from an unbeaten George Foreman a decade later, and won two of three fights with Joe Frazier. If the question is who proved the most against the best heavyweights of his time, Ali is my pick.

Louis gave up the title when he retired in 1949. Ezzard Charles was already champion when he beat Louis on points the following year, and Rocky Marciano knocked Louis out in 1951, before Marciano had won the title himself. Those losses are part of Louis’s record, but the fight that best explains his greatness took place in 1938. Max Schmeling had knocked him out two years earlier. Louis stopped him in the first round of their rematch.

What Ali proved after Liston

Ali was 29–0 when he was forced out of boxing after refusing military induction in 1967. He came back in 1970 and lost to Frazier the following year. Frazier could get inside, make Ali work at a pace he disliked, and hurt him with the left hook. Ali won the rematch and then the third fight in Manila. He also knocked out Foreman, who had taken the title from Frazier in two rounds. Ali’s third championship came in 1978, when he outpointed Leon Spinks seven months after losing the title to him.

Marciano has the cleanest record of the six at 49–0, with six successful title defenses. His best argument is what he did when he was behind. Jersey Joe Walcott dropped him in the first round of their 1952 title fight and was ahead on all three cards when Marciano knocked him out in the 13th. Larry Holmes makes a stronger case on longevity. He won the WBC belt from Ken Norton in 1978 and reached 48–0 before Michael Spinks beat him. Holmes’s jab was still good enough to help him outpoint an unbeaten Ray Mercer in 1992, at age 42.

Mike Tyson’s best years were spectacular. He took his first belt from Trevor Berbick at 20, collected the other two, and stopped Michael Spinks in 91 seconds. His first reign ended when Buster Douglas knocked him out in Tokyo. Foreman’s case runs in the opposite direction. His two-round demolition of Frazier showed what he could do in his prime. Knocking out Michael Moorer at 45, twenty years after losing to Ali, showed how much he could still do long after it.

Louis is the closest call because a champion has to keep winning after everybody has had years to study him. What puts Ali ahead for me is that the two best heavyweights he faced asked completely different questions of him. Frazier made him fight at close quarters for rounds at a time. Foreman had the power to end the fight if Ali made one bad mistake there. Ali found a way to beat both.

Sports.title: Raymond Ford’s Matchroom Deal Is Up. What Has He Earned?
Sports.content:
Raymond Ford’s contract with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom has expired, and it now remains to be seen whether he’ll be re-signed for another stint. Hearn hasn’t said whether he’ll bring him back.

Ford is coming off a one-sided loss to O’Shaquie Foster last May, and you’ve got to figure out whether Matchroom will offer him less guaranteed money. It would make total sense for Hearn to re-sign Ford at a reduced price in a take-it-or-leave-it offer. Why pay similar money if he’s not producing?

The former WBA featherweight champion Ford, 27, has been with Matchroom his entire career since 2019, but he’s had a rough go since 2024. During that six-fight stretch, he’s been involved in four grueling fights, losing two of them and getting lucky with a questionable stoppage against knockout artist Otabek Kholmatov.

Ford (18-2-1, 8 KOs) took brutal shots from Kholmatov. He got hit with everything in the book, took them, but looked war-torn by the later rounds. He was losing that fight going into the 12th round when the referee suddenly halted the bout after the injured, hobbling Kholmatov briefly lost his balance.

“His contract’s up with us at the moment. We’ll see what happens,” said Hearn to iFL TV when asked about Ford.

The Foster fight was Raymond’s chance to redeem himself, but he failed miserably, getting outboxed, looking overmatched from the word go against the WBC super featherweight champion.

After that performance, Matchroom has to decide whether it’s worth bringing him back at any price. The company can sign other younger fighters with less mileage on the odometer who can handle pure boxers and sluggers better.

Unfortunately, Ford hasn’t shown the ability to deal with either type. His loss to the tiny 5’2″ slugger Nick Ball was another example of Ford’s inability to deal with a guy with power that brings pure heat for 12 rounds. Unlike Kholmatov, Ball wasn’t hampered by a knee injury that slowed him down in the later rounds.

At this point, Hearn might be better off letting Ford walk and finding another promoter willing to match him carefully and subsidize his career. Under the right circumstances, Ford can still win a title, but it would require rebuilding and waiting for the perfect style match-up.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn in Contract Talks With Unnamed World Champion
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is hinting at signing two American fighters, including a world champion. He said he’s talked with WBO light welterweight champion Shakur Stevenson and former lightweight champion Keyshawn Davis. Hearn says he doesn’t have either ready to sign yet.

All told, Hearn says he’s in talks with 7 total fighters. Shakur and Keyshawn, plus 2 unnamed fighters at the contract stage, plus three others.

Signing Keyshawn and Shakur would still create problems for Hearn, since they would want to be paid a boatload of money for their fights. Yeah, it would be great for Hearn to have those two talents, but with the costs, it could be a nightmare if their cards hemorrhage dough repeatedly. Neither of them are PPV draws.

Hearn wants Shakur to focus on becoming undisputed at light welterweight. He’s talked about him fighting champions Gary Antuanne Russell and Dalton Smith in addition to whoever winds up with the vacant IBF title.

He’s also interested in matching him against Raymond Muratalla, who may be the toughest of the bunch because of his size and power. That would be a tougher fight for Shakur than the ones he’d had thus far in the pro ranks. It wouldn’t be a shock to hear him drag his feet at accepting it, which could cost him his WBO title if he refuses.

Hearn wants to get the 2020 Olympic silver medalist Keyshawn fighting often, as he believes he’s wasting his career. Although he has already fought twice this year, they were fights that he used to get his feet wet at 140 against Nahir Albright and Jamaine Ortiz.

The Albright fight seemed totally needless, though, because he’d already beaten him in 2023. Running it back seemed weird and wasteful.

“Get on the horse, man. You’re wasting your career,” said Hearn to iFL TV about Keyshawn.

Well, if Hearn does sign Davis, he should put him back in with his four-time conqueror Andy Cruz. That’s a fight that he should have taken by now, given that he was soundly beaten by the Cuban talent in the 2020 Olympics.

Cruz has been calling him “My son” since he turned pro, trying to instigate a fight. Keyshawn has shown no desire to get back in the ring with him, which looks bad for him. Why fight the likes of Jamaine, Nahir and Miguel Madueno when you’ve got Cruz, a guy that beat you four times? It comes across like Keyshawn has a confidence issue holding him back. If that is the case, Hearn would be signing a problem.

“I don’t have anything at contractual stage with Shakur Stevenson or Keyshawn Davis, but I would love to sign both,” said Hearn in an interview with iFL TV. He confirmed he had spoken to both fighters and said he would like to work with their teams.

With Anthony Joshua getting old and nearing the end, and Andy Cruz’s contract with Matchroom coming to an end, Hearn needs new blood to replace them. Losing Cruz would be a disaster because he’s only now on the cusp of winning a world title, and unlike Joshua, he’s at the top of his game and still young.

Ghana News.title: Mahama, Akufo-Addo, Otumfuo expected at Agogo Manhene’s funeral
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama, former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo and Asantehene Otumfuo Osei Tutu II are among prominent dignitaries expected at the final funeral rites of the late Agogomanhene, Nana Kwame Akuoko Sarpong.

The three-day traditional funeral, known as Dotie Yie, will take place from November 24 to 26, 2026, at the Kyei and Ofori Krobron Stool Palace in Agogo in the Asante Akyem area.

An announcement by the Agogo Traditional Council indicates that the funeral will bring together traditional rulers, political leaders, government officials, religious authorities, diplomats, security personnel and representatives of various institutions to pay their last respects to the late chief.

The announcement was dated November 10, 2026, and signed by Nana Kwame Nti.

The final day, Thursday, November 26, is expected to attract the country's top political and traditional leadership, including the Asantehene, the President, former Presidents and Vice-Presidents, Ministers of State and other senior government officials.

The programme, signed by the Krontihene of the Agogo Traditional Council, Nana Kwame Nti, outlines separate arrangements for groups expected to attend the three days of mourning.

On Tuesday, November 24, the first day of the funeral, religious leaders, the Muslim community, churches, diplomats, members of the Council of State, political parties and officials of the Municipal Assembly are expected to attend.

Heads of government departments, corporate institutions, non-governmental organisations, private unions, associations and members of the general public will also have the opportunity to pay their respects.

Wednesday, November 25, will bring together traditional authorities from the National and Regional Houses of Chiefs, as well as security agencies and other state institutions.

The Ghana Armed Forces, Ghana Police Service, Ghana National Fire Service, Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority and Ghana Immigration Service are among those expected. State-owned enterprises, educational institutions and old students' associations are also scheduled to participate.

The final day's observances will be attended by the Asantehene and other senior members of the Asante Kingdom, alongside the country's political leadership and other invited dignitaries.

The first two days will have morning sessions from 5 a.m. to 11 a.m. and afternoon sessions from 1 p.m. to 6 p.m. On Thursday, the morning session will run from 5 a.m. to 11 a.m., with the afternoon programme ending at 5 p.m.

The Traditional Council said the funeral was an opportunity to celebrate the late chief's years of service to Agogo, Asanteman and Ghana.

It has urged dignitaries and other prospective attendees to make the necessary arrangements ahead of the event and directed that official RSVPs be submitted through designated representatives.

Ghana News.title: Here are some quality product displays at the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 – Don’t miss out
Ghana News.content:
The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 opened at GHUD Park, Accra Mall, bringing together an impressive collection of Ghanaian businesses, established brands, entrepreneurs and service providers for a three-day celebration of enterprise, innovation and commerce.

With an extensive range of products and services on display, patrons have plenty of reasons to make their way to the exhibition grounds before the fair ends on Sunday, November 15.

From delicious local delicacies and refreshing beverages to fashionable clothing, beauty products, technology, household essentials and financial services, the exhibition offers visitors an exciting opportunity to discover quality products, meet business owners and shop directly from participating brands.

A marketplace bursting with flavour and innovation

Food lovers are particularly well catered for, with exhibitors presenting an exciting selection of locally produced and processed products.

Among them are Wilmar Africa, showcasing its Fortune Spread brand; Kivo; Didi Shito; Corki Ventures, with its spices; Adjoor Ventures, specialising in tuna distribution; Manellah Foods, known for cereal production; and Gold Coast Foods, presenting Sankofa Spices.

Other food and beverage exhibitors include Yaapee Royal Foods, NutriSmart Ventures, Golden Parani Company Limited, Golden Pride (Yao Consult), G-Way Investments Africa Limited, Ikam Plus Company Limited, Desco Limited, Golden Parani Company Limited and ESBONY Food Package.

Visitors can also explore natural and refreshing beverage options from Koa Impact Commerce, with its natural cocoa juice; Spring Board (Delsoy Ltd), showcasing soy milk; Spring Board (Orave Juices), with fruit juice; Pinnacle Coco Limited, offering coconut juice; Jussvina Drinks (Global 500); Green Cup, with its beetroot, guava and pawpaw tea; and Myst Natural Water.

The culinary experience extends to Flourish Foods Africa's grilled chicken and poultry products, MamsiJoy Ventures' rice, Ellie's Catering Services' fufu, Martha's Yam Trading, Farm Mate's fresh tomatoes, Orrab Farms' fresh produce, T&C Farms' animal production and Atohfield's crop and animal farming.

Aladdin Bakery, 97 Bakes, Evive Delight Ltd, Bliss Pop, Selis Satisfactory and Golden Coast Foods add even more variety to the food offerings, with products ranging from baked treats and popcorn to kenkey and other processed foods. BB Brothers also brings its canned wine offering to the exhibition.

Fashion, beauty and lifestyle take centre stage

Fashion enthusiasts will find plenty to explore, with a diverse collection of clothing, accessories, footwear and personal-care products.

Haute Xklusive, La Robe Classique, Kims Foods and Clothings, JAT Couture, Kofikyere KloTHING, Utonez Clothier and Regy Couture Ltd are among the brands presenting fashion options.

Asangenta adds dresses, bags and hats to the mix, while Shoes TE3 caters for different footwear needs and sizes. Kinky Love Crochet brings its hair and wig offerings to the exhibition, complementing the wider lifestyle display.

Beauty and personal-care enthusiasts can discover products from Haus of Lush, RNS Beauty, Atlast Prime Merchantile Ltd, Leepoku Ventures and Chocho. Mist and Strands also presents bath and body products, while Reed Diffusers Ghana Ltd adds scented home accessories to the experience.

LIZ Imports showcases perfumes and home appliances, while Kemz Ceramics brings ceramics to the exhibition. Eldem Floral Services adds colour and elegance with fresh-cut flowers.

Technology, business solutions and essential services

Beyond consumer products, the fair provides a valuable opportunity to discover businesses using technology and innovation to address everyday challenges.

Solid Connect is showcasing its application for artisans, while Greenhaul Solutions presents waste-management and scrap-procurement services. We Shop Africa and Ayuda bring e-commerce solutions into focus, while Katon 360 Technologies showcases a digital platform designed for SMEs.

Technology enthusiasts can also visit Galop Sea Limited for laptops and accessories, Xfromo Hypermart for phones and accessories, including Google Pixel phones, and Vital Vendors for car essentials.

Financial and institutional services are equally represented. Ecobank showcases banking services, while GLICO Life presents insurance solutions. MTN brings telecommunications and connectivity services to the exhibition.

DBS showcases housing and roofing solutions, Sintex Tank presents water-storage products, and Vaal Real Estate offers real estate opportunities. GEPA also provides an important export-sector presence, connecting the exhibition to Ghana's wider ambition of promoting locally made products and businesses.

Other exhibitors include Worafam Group of Companies, showcasing safety wear; MGIG Suppliers, with powdered soap; BB Chemist, presenting Relax Liver Salt; Prestige Children's Palace and Roses Enterprise and Mothercare, offering mother-care products; and Central University, representing the education sector.

Travel and hospitality services are also represented by Grandeur Consult Travel and Tour and Astolinks, while Gorgeous Vie Event Hub showcases events and décor services. Afram Publication brings books to the exhibition, and Advantage GH Premium Apparel presents printing services.

An opportunity patrons should not miss

The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair goes beyond the traditional shopping experience. It creates an environment where businesses can interact directly with consumers, build brand awareness, generate sales and establish valuable commercial relationships.

The initiative builds on JoyBusiness's longstanding engagement with Ghanaian small and medium-sized enterprises, particularly the need to improve access to markets, financing, technology and business development opportunities.

For patrons, it is an opportunity to discover emerging Ghanaian brands, compare products, make purchases and support businesses contributing to the country's entrepreneurial landscape.

With Saturday and Sunday still to come, the public is encouraged not to miss the remaining days of the fair.

Whether you are searching for your next favourite food brand, refreshing your wardrobe, exploring beauty products, looking for technology solutions or simply interested in supporting Ghanaian businesses, there is something worth discovering at GHUD Park, Accra Mall.

The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 continues until Sunday, November 15. Make time to visit, explore the impressive displays and experience the products and innovations that Ghanaian businesses have to offer.

Ghana News.title: Disqualified NDC National Youth Organizer aspirant rules out appeal
Ghana News.content:
A disqualified aspirant in the National Democratic Congress (NDC) National Youth Organiser race, Steven Nhyira Odarteifio, has ruled out challenging the party's decision to disqualify him from the contest.

He said he would neither protest the decision nor pursue an appeal, choosing instead to remain neutral as the party prepares to elect a new National Youth Organiser.

In a statement following the conclusion of the party's vetting process, Mr Odarteifio expressed disappointment with the outcome but thanked the NDC for giving him the opportunity to present his vision for the youth wing and young people across the country.

He also congratulated the two candidates who survived the vetting and wished them well in the contest.

Mr Odarteifio said he hoped the candidates would put their differences aside after the election and work together to strengthen the party's youth wing.

“I have decided to remain neutral in this contest, and I stand ready to support whoever wins,” he said.

He reaffirmed his commitment to youth development and agricultural transformation, saying he would continue to advocate policies and initiatives that improve opportunities for young people and help the party fulfil its promises to them.

The former aspirant also expressed gratitude to his sponsors, campaign volunteers and supporters for their contributions throughout his bid for the position.

Ghana News.title: Drug trafficking isn’t a political problem; it’s an institutional one – Senyo Hosi
Ghana News.content:
Convener of the OneGhana Movement and Trustee of the Ghana Coalition Against Galamsey, Senyo Hosi, has described drug trafficking in Ghana as an institutional problem, calling for stronger enforcement systems, greater accountability and adequate resources for the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC).

Speaking on JoyNews' Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, he argued that the country's fight against drugs must move beyond political debates to address weaknesses within institutions responsible for border security and law enforcement.

Mr Hosi acknowledged improvements in NACOC's operations, particularly the expansion of its presence from approximately eight districts to 81, but maintained that the Commission remained significantly under-resourced.

Although he commended efforts to improve the institution's capacity through training and equipment, he insisted that more investment was needed to enable it to effectively tackle drug trafficking.

Mr Hosi also warned against limiting Ghana's drug problem to cocaine, arguing that synthetic substances posed a serious threat to young people.

"The drug problem should not be made a cocaine problem at all. The bigger problem we have is with the synthetics. Serious problem. That's what our youth are getting into," he said.

Beyond NACOC's capacity, Mr Hosi raised concerns about the effectiveness of cargo scanning systems at Ghana's ports, questioning how cocaine consignments could pass through without detection.

He called for investigations into the operations of port scanners, their maintenance and the role of Customs officers responsible for inspecting containers.

He also questioned reports that some scanners frequently broke down, although he said he could not independently verify the information.

For him, such concerns point to deeper institutional weaknesses that must be investigated rather than turned into political blame games.

"It's no more a political problem. It's a whole institutional problem," he stressed.

He also expressed disappointment that the drug menace had not received sufficient attention in the government's budget, urging authorities to prioritise funding for NACOC, just as they had highlighted the fight against illegal small-scale mining, popularly known as galamsey.

He warned that Ghana must treat drug trafficking and substance abuse as major national concerns, particularly given the growing exposure of young people to illicit substances.

He added that strengthening enforcement institutions, improving border surveillance, and holding those responsible for trafficking networks accountable were essential to addressing the problem.

Ghana News.title: 200 police officers deployed to Nalerigu NDC election grounds
Ghana News.content:
About 200 unarmed police officers have arrived at the Nalerigu Senior High School, the venue for the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Regional executive election ahead of the polls.

A total of 231 delegates are expected to participate in the regional election.

The officers assembled at the election grounds on Saturday, November 14, as part of security arrangements to ensure a peaceful electoral process.

The Police explained that the presence of the officers was intended to guarantee a free, fair and orderly election.

He disclosed, however, that armed police personnel had been placed on standby to respond to any eventuality that might threaten security during the exercise.

The commander urged all candidates, their supporters and other party stakeholders to conduct themselves responsibly and avoid actions that could undermine the electoral process.

The security arrangements come amid deepening divisions within the NDC in the Nalerigu-Gambaga Constituency, which have triggered legal disputes and public exchanges between rival party executives.

The disagreements centre partly on the selection and legitimacy of five co-opted constituency executives and their eligibility to participate in the regional election.

The dispute resulted in an application to the Nalerigu High Court, which restrained five individuals from participating in the election.

The internal tensions have also exposed a broader political rivalry between Regional Minister Ibrahim Tia and former Nalerigu-Gambaga MP and former Minister for Climate Change, Alhaji Baba Issifu, over political influence in the constituency.

The deployment of approximately 200 police officers, with armed personnel on standby, highlights security concerns surrounding the closely watched election involving 231 delegates.

Ghana News.title: We can’t rely on NAIMOS alone to fight galamsey – Senyo Hosi
Ghana News.content:
Convener of the OneGhana Movement and finance and economic policy analyst, Senyo Hosi, has called for a major rethink of Ghana's approach to tackling illegal mining, warning that the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) cannot win the fight on its own.

He says the country must adopt a broader strategy that addresses the economic and social conditions sustaining illegal mining, particularly in communities where it has become a major source of livelihood.

Speaking on JoyNews' Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, Mr Hosi criticised what he described as an overreliance on NAIMOS, arguing that local authorities must take greater responsibility for enforcing mining laws and protecting their communities.

He specifically challenged Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) to strengthen enforcement at the local level rather than leave the responsibility largely to the national task force.

“We cannot rely on NAIMOS alone to win a war which has taken seed at the local level. MMDCEs, who control security at the local level, continue to fail to enforce the laws,” he said.

He also questioned the effectiveness of NAIMOS operations that involve moving from one community to another without ensuring that illegal mining activities are permanently halted.

“NAIMOS should just stop roaming people's villages,” he stated.

Citing operations at Osino, he questioned the sustainability of interventions if illegal miners returned immediately after security personnel withdrew.

“You went to Osino. You left the place. The people went back in. What did you achieve?” he asked.

Mr Hosi also raised concerns about allegations of extortion associated with anti-illegal mining operations, recalling similar accusations against previous interventions, including Operation Vanguard.

Economic realities must inform galamsey fight

Mr Hosi argued that the government's approach must recognise the scale of the economic interests and livelihoods tied to illegal mining.

He said it would be unrealistic to expect security operations alone to eliminate an activity involving an estimated one million to three million people without providing alternative sources of income.

“You are dealing with a trade that has about a million to three million people involved, a whole community. You can't just shut them down when that is actually their livelihood,” he said.

He noted that illegal mining had become intertwined with the economic survival and social realities of some communities, making enforcement without alternative livelihood opportunities difficult to sustain.

“The communities have this intertwined with their culture, their economic survival. You can't shoot poverty away. That is the reality of this,” he stated.

He further argued that the continued participation of residents, despite the deaths and dangers associated with illegal mining, demonstrated the depth of the socioeconomic challenges confronting affected communities.

For Mr Hosi, the government must recognise that the fight requires more than arrests, excavator seizures and military deployments.

“We can't keep wanting to do things the same way. There's a need for a total rethinking of this,” he said.

Questions need for state of emergency

Responding to whether Ghana still needed a state of emergency to address illegal mining, Mr Hosi said such a measure could be implemented in severely affected areas if the government was prepared to accept the political consequences.

He maintained that the problem was not necessarily the absence of the legal and security measures required to tackle galamsey, but a lack of political willingness to apply them decisively.

“It's not as though there's no need. Let me be very clear. While I often say the fight can't be won in the context of the political inertia that we have, if you want to win this, you will win it,” he said.

However, he cautioned against relying exclusively on military intervention, citing the disparity between Ghana's estimated military strength of 28,000 to 30,000 personnel and the millions of people he believes are involved in the illegal mining economy.

He also questioned the political and practical sustainability of shutting down livelihoods without addressing the conditions that drive people into the activity.

Cleaner water bodies, forest reserves should define success

Mr Hosi said Ghana must clearly define what success in the fight against illegal mining should look like, arguing that protecting water bodies and forest reserves must be the immediate priorities.

He said the country should focus its resources on achievable objectives rather than pursue an overly broad campaign without clearly identifying measurable outcomes.

“We just have to be clear and select our victories, our winnable tasks. We have to define what victory looks like at first,” he said.

According to him, the most important measure of progress should be cleaner rivers and the protection of forest reserves, rather than the number of enforcement operations conducted.

“What does victory look like for us in Ghana? Galamsey. It must mean cleaner waters. That is what victory should look like for us, number one. Number two, our forest reserves,” he stated.

He suggested that NAIMOS should prioritise stopping mining activities in rivers and their immediate surroundings, arguing that sustained enforcement in these areas would produce more visible environmental benefits.

“If NAIMOS and their work were just committed to our rivers, and nobody was mining on our rivers, at least for now, we wouldn't have this water we are seeing in front of us,” he said.

He also questioned the effectiveness of government expenditure on the anti-galamsey campaign, insisting that the results must be assessed against improvements in water quality and the restoration of degraded forest reserves.

Referring to the government's 2027 budgetary allocations and statements by the Finance Minister, Mr Hosi said the public deserved measurable evidence that the resources committed to the fight were producing results.

“You should be telling us whether our water bodies have improved with all the investments you have made in that particular sector,” he said.

“It hasn't. It has gotten worse,” he added.

He maintained that unless Ghana addresses the economic incentives sustaining illegal mining while protecting its critical environmental resources, the country risks repeating enforcement exercises without achieving lasting results.

Ghana News.title: Miracles Aboagye insists State must account for 6 deaths at Manso Keniago over galamsey
Ghana News.content:
The Director of Communications for the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Miracles Aboagye, has called for a thorough investigation into the killing of six people during a confrontation involving personnel of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and residents of Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region.

He has cautioned against collectively labelling the deceased as illegal miners or members of a mob, insisting that the circumstances surrounding each death must be independently established to ensure justice for the victims and their families.

Speaking on JoyNews' Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, during a discussion on the incident, Mr Aboagye said available accounts suggested that some of the victims might not have participated in the confrontation.

He expressed condolences to the bereaved families, citing reports of a woman who was allegedly shot in her bathroom and others who were shot on the street.

“I express my condolences to the lost ones. The sad and painful reality is that some of the six fallen citizens may not even be part of anything,” he said.

“I have seen a woman who was shot in her bathroom. The cameras were there. They showed where she was in the bathroom and the blood stains. But I've seen two people shot on the street,” he added.

Mr Aboagye said he had listened to accounts from both the community's chief and NAIMOS officials but maintained that the conflicting narratives made an independent investigation necessary.

“Whatever the case is, we have lost six citizens that, as we speak now, we are yet to understand clearly why each of them died,” he said.

He argued that each victim deserved an individual assessment rather than being grouped and presumed to have been involved in the confrontation.

“Remember, you can't bunch human souls together and label all of them with one issue and use that as a basis for their death. Every family deserves justice. We need to understand why each of the six people has died,” he stated.

State must take responsibility for citizens' safety

While urging civilians to avoid confronting armed security personnel, Mr Aboagye said the State had the primary responsibility to protect lives, particularly during enforcement operations.

He argued that residents should exercise restraint when confronted by armed officers, as there was little to gain from engaging security personnel in a potentially dangerous confrontation.

“My view is that there is no glory in confronting armed men, especially those who are backed by the law,” he said.

However, he stressed that this did not absolve security personnel or the State of their responsibility to protect innocent people during operations.

“The number one responsibility of the State is the security, safety and protection of its citizens. That comes before every other thing,” he said.

“When it comes to our safety and security, it's solely in the hands of the State. And so the State must take responsibility,” he added.

Mr Aboagye further argued that the presence of a crowd at the scene did not necessarily mean everyone within it was participating in an attack on security personnel.

He said officers must exercise restraint and distinguish between those actively confronting them and innocent residents who might have gathered out of curiosity.

“You must be mindful. And even if there's one single soul, just one person in that mob that is innocent, you have a duty and responsibility to be moderate to protect that person,” he said.

He maintained that the possibility of innocent people being caught up in the confrontation made it unacceptable to justify all six deaths simply on the grounds that a mob had confronted the task force.

“There is no justification in getting a single innocent person to die in a mob in an attempt or with the justification that it's a mob and your life is under threat. You are trained, they are not,” he stated.

Questions NAIMOS use of drone surveillance

The NPP Communications Director said he would accept the outcome of an investigation establishing that all six deceased persons were illegal miners who actively obstructed the NAIMOS operation.

However, he insisted that such a conclusion must be supported by credible evidence rather than assumptions about the victims' involvement.

“If all six people are identified to be galamseyers who are standing in the way of NAIMOS, we can do this. But we don't know that yet,” he said.

He also questioned why drone footage was not being used to establish the sequence of events and identify the individuals who participated in the confrontation.

“If you have a drone and you encounter such a mob, you don't leave the drone. You let the drone fly,” he said.

Mr Aboagye also alleged that influential individuals benefiting from illegal mining continued to enjoy political protection, declaring that “the kingpins of galamsey are backing government”.

How the Manso Keniago confrontation unfolded

The incident occurred on Wednesday, November 11, at Manso Keniago in the Amansie South District of the Ashanti Region, when NAIMOS personnel were transporting excavators seized during an anti-illegal mining operation to a designated location for safekeeping.

Read also: Manso Keniago clash death toll rises to six, 15 injured

The confrontation reportedly followed disagreements between the task force, some residents and traditional authorities over the transportation of the seized equipment through the community on a tarred road. Residents reportedly preferred that low-bed trailers be used.

NAIMOS maintained that its personnel encountered an armed group attempting to obstruct the operation and said officers fired warning shots to disperse the crowd. The Secretariat subsequently described the shooting as an act of self-defence.

The death toll, initially reported as three, later rose to six, while 15 others were reported injured. Two NAIMOS personnel also sustained gunshot wounds but were subsequently treated and discharged from hospital.

Mr Aboagye's comments add to growing calls for an investigation into the circumstances of the deaths, with questions remaining about the conduct of the operation, the use of firearms and the individual roles, if any, played by those who lost their lives.

Ghana News.title: NDC is the biggest enabler of galamsey – Miracles Aboagye claims
Ghana News.content:
Director of Communications for the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, has accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of enabling illegal small-scale mining, popularly known as galamsey, alleging that some party officials and government functionaries are involved in the practice while authorities appear to be taking action against other miners.

Mr Aboagye argued that the fight against illegal mining was being undermined by what he described as selective enforcement of the law, insisting that the actions of some individuals associated with the governing party were creating resentment among communities affected by the government's anti-galamsey operations.

Responding to the killing of some six persons following a clash between community members and the government's anti-galamey task force, NAIMOS, he maintained that the political leadership of the NDC could not distance itself from the activities of individuals allegedly engaged in illegal mining, particularly when videos had emerged purportedly showing some party officials making statements in support of galamsey activities.

"There is no pretence here. The kingpins of galamsey are back in government. I keep saying it, and I have said it several times. I have always proven it. The NDC is the biggest enabler of galamsey in this country," he stated.

He accused the government of failing to confront the problem consistently, arguing that while security personnel were deployed to clamp down on illegal mining activities in some communities, other operations allegedly continued in areas where individuals linked to the governing party were believed to be involved.

According to him, illegal mining activities were still taking place along major routes and in communities stretching from Osino and Konongo in the Asante Akim area towards Kumasi.

He questioned the apparent inconsistency in the government's approach, claiming that people were being subjected to police operations and other enforcement measures while illegal mining continued in other locations.

"As we speak this morning, Osino, Konongo, Asante Akyem, all the way to Kumasi, people are mining," he alleged.

He warned that selective enforcement could have serious consequences for public confidence in the country's institutions.

"In a society where the people don't feel justice is prevailing, in a society where the people feel there is selective justice, they will revolt," he cautioned.

"These people, before they came to office, gave us a roadmap. It is still in their manifesto, and it is still on their campaign videos. They said, 'Vote for me, and when we come, these are the things we will do.' Which ones have they done?" he questioned.

"Today in Ghana, galamsey is worse than it was in 2024. Everywhere you go," he claimed.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
