Abdullahi Bewene delivered an impressive performance at right-back, justifying Eric Chelle’s decision to hand him a starting opportunity ahead of Bright Osayi-Samuel.

The young defender showed considerable energy and willingness to support Nigeria’s attacking movements while remaining disciplined in his defensive responsibilities. His ability to contribute at both ends of the pitch was particularly encouraging, as he demonstrated confidence going forward without neglecting his primary defensive duties.

For a player looking to establish himself in the Super Eagles setup, such an opportunity was important, as Chelle’s decision to trust him ahead of a more established option suggested the coach was willing to assess his alternatives and reward players who could offer something different to the team.

Bewene responded with a performance that should boost his confidence and strengthen his case for further opportunities. While one impressive outing does not automatically guarantee a regular starting position, the youngster has given the coaching crew another option to consider as Nigeria continue their quest for a place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

Ibrahim Hamad’s injury weakens Tanzania’s defensive resistance

Tanzania also suffered an injury setback during the second half, with defender Ibrahim Hamad unable to continue despite his encouraging performance before the interval.

The 29-year-old had done a commendable job of containing Nigeria’s attacking threat during the opening 45 minutes, particularly in his attempts to limit the influence of Akor Adams, as his defensive organisation and ability to compete physically helped Tanzania remain in the contest before the break.

However, Hamad was forced off after sustaining an injury and was subsequently replaced by Charles M’Mombwa. His departure came at an unfortunate moment for the Taifa Stars, who were already under increasing pressure as Nigeria stepped up their attacking intensity.

Although it would be difficult to attribute Tanzania’s eventual defeat solely to his substitution, his absence deprived the visitors of an experienced defensive option during a crucial period of the encounter.

World.title: ‘This is just the beginning’: Flamingos vow to keep improving after World Cup win
World.content:
Players of Nigeria’s Under-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, say they have shifted focus to personal and career development following their triumph at the 2026 FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco.

The players told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in separate interviews that although winning the competition was a major achievement, it marked only the beginning of their football careers.

The captain of the team, Chidi Harmony, said the players must put the achievement behind them and concentrate on correcting their mistakes and improving their individual performances.

“This is just a starting point. We cannot look at this success and say we have arrived. As young players, we have to put this aside and focus on development.

“It is time to work on our mistakes. We want to go out every day and keep improving ourselves so that we can win more trophies for the country,” Harmony said.

On her personal ambitions, Harmony said she had identified four or five top European clubs she hoped to play for, but declined to disclose their names.

“I have four or five big clubs I want to play for, but I will keep them to myself for now. I will share the names the day I finally sign for any of the clubs,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Similarly, Golden Ball winner, Oluebube Umejiaku, expressed gratitude to God for the team’s success in Morocco, saying she was already looking forward to greater achievements.

She recalled that following their triumph at the WAFU B tournament in Cote d’Ivoire, the team had resolved to replicate the feat at the World Cup.

“After the WAFU B in Cote d’Ivoire, where we won, we told ourselves that we would go and do the same in Morocco, and I am very happy we returned home with the trophy.

“Personally, I feel I have not even started. This is just the beginning of my career, and I pray that God helps me achieve more and win more trophies for the country,” Umejiaku said.

Forward Kemi Adegbuyi also said she remained determined to achieve greater success, adding that she was focused on improving her game and making further impact in football.

She expressed gratitude to God, her family and supporters for their contributions to her success.

“I am very happy and grateful to God, my family and those who have been supporting me.

“But now, I am focusing on not letting my guard down. I am concentrating on improving myself and making more statements in football,” Adegbuyi said.

The FC Robo forward also called for increased investment and support for the Nigerian women’s league to enable more talented players to showcase their abilities.

According to her, the league has many undiscovered talents who require adequate platforms and opportunities to develop their careers.

“There are a lot of hidden talents in the women’s league in Nigeria. We just need the right platforms to showcase our talents.

“We need more investment and support,” she said.

(NAN)

World.title: Governor’s aide flays Amaechi over posture at emir’s palace
World.content:
Controversy has trailed a recent campaign visit by the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to Bauchi State, with the party’s vice-presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, being criticised over his posture during a courtesy call at the Emir of Bauchi’s palace.

Mr Amaechi accompanied the party’s presidential flagbearer, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, and other senior ADC chieftains to the palace as part of the party’s ongoing nationwide campaign for the January 2027 general elections.

However, images and video clips circulating on social media from the visit sparked debate among observers and political commentators. Some described Mr Amaechi’s posture before the traditional ruler as disrespectful to the revered stool and Northern Nigerian cultural norms.

Garba Muhammad, a new media aide to Governor Umar Namadi of Jigawa State posted on Facebook that Mr Amaechi’s sitting pattern disrespected the traditional institution.

“Look at the way the ADC vice-presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, sat today at the Bauchi palace when they went for their campaign. There is absolutely no respect or honour here,” Mr Muhammad wrote, echoing sentiments from others who argued that political leaders seeking the support of traditional institutions must demonstrate decorum.

Traditional palaces in Northern Nigeria are widely regarded as custodians of culture and authority, where strict protocols of deference—including sitting posture and mode of greeting—are closely observed by visiting dignitaries.

Mr Muhammad and several other commentators argued that Mr Amaechi’s demeanor fell short of the standard expected of a high-ranking national figure courting grassroots and traditional backing.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

While the ADC has yet to respond to the viral commentary, party loyalists online dismissed the criticism as a deliberate distraction by political opponents, insisting that the visitors were warmly received by the palace and focused on key national issues such as security, economic recovery, and infrastructure.

Campaign rally

The ADC campaign team led by Atiku arrived in Bauchi State on Friday ahead of the party’s presidential campaign rally scheduled for Saturday.

Atiku arrived at the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa International Airport, Bauchi, with members of his entourage.

The ADC presidential candidate is expected to address party supporters and residents of the state at Saturday’s rally.

World.title: 2027: Atiku, Obi making victory easy for Tinubu – Sule Lamido
World.content:
Former Jigawa State Governor, Sule Lamido, has stated that the inability of opposition figures Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi to form a united front is giving the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) a significant advantage ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Mr Lamido made these remarks on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he discussed the 2027 general election and the ambitions of Nigeria’s leading political figures.

According to the former governor, the ruling party already benefits from a large bloc of serving and former governors, and a divided opposition only makes the path to victory easier for President Bola Tinubu.

“Because of the number of governors—both former and serving governors of the APC—and because Atiku and Obi divided their own forces, it gives them the advantage,” Mr Lamido said.

“So both Peter Obi and Atiku are simply handing over the victory, very easily because they cannot come together.”

He said the major presidential candidates—specifically naming President Tinubu, Atiku Abubakar, and Peter Obi—are driven by personal ambition and a desire for power rather than a commitment to solving the nation’s pressing challenges.

He warned that the country stands to suffer regardless of which of the three emerges victorious.

“I have been saying, look, no one is going to tell you that it is for Nigeria. Whoever wins, Nigeria will lose. That is my problem. Whoever wins, whether Peter Obi or Atiku, in terms of our unity, our economy, our love as a country of brothers and sisters, it is all going down.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Lamido also criticised the current political climate, noting that rivalries have devolved into personal attacks rather than constructive debates.

He lamented the rise of propaganda, hate speech, and incitement in ongoing political activities particularly in northern Nigeria where politicians turn campaign arenas to hate speech, warning that campaigns have abandoned substance in favour of personality clashes.

“It is more about their personalities. They are building each other, attacking each other. Those things become very, very personal,” he said.

“A lot of things have gone wrong with the traditional campaign on issues—about love, about empathy, about unity, about Nigeria, and then what can you offer? What can you offer? So it is not there anymore.”

Mr Lamido also dismissed the claim that he was backing President Tinubu, insisting in the interview that he remains faithful to the Wike-backed PDP faction and its presidential candidate.

World.title: Falana urges Tinubu govt to prosecute sponsors of electoral violence ahead of 2027
World.content:
Human rights lawyer Femi Falana has urged the federal government to prosecute politicians who sponsor electoral violence, warning that attacks on political opponents and intimidation of voters threaten the credibility of the 2027 general elections.

Mr Falana, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), said the government must go beyond arresting suspected political thugs and hold accountable those who recruit, finance and arm them.

He made the call at the sixth Frontier Discourse Annual Public Lecture Series and Awards organised by Pacesetter Frontiers Magazine at Merit House, Maitama, Abuja. The statement was shared with PREMIUM TIMES on Saturday.

In his keynote address, titled “Barrel to Ballot: The Naturalisation of Violence, Nigeria’s Polity and its Democratic Circus,” Mr Falana stated that political violence was rooted in deeper problems of governance, accountability and the failure to protect citizens’ rights.

“As the 2027 elections approach, the State must protect lives, enforce electoral laws and punish those who sponsor or perpetrate political violence, irrespective of status or political connections,” he said.

He accused politicians of recruiting unemployed youths, arming them and supplying them with money and drugs to attack opponents, disrupt political meetings and intimidate voters.

The warning comes amid reports of attacks on political figures and their supporters in different parts of the country.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The African Centre for Security, Governance and Development (CentreSGD) reported 70 physical election-related attacks across 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory between 1 January and 27 October 2026. It said 27 people were killed in 20 of the incidents.

The organisation also cited a Yiaga Africa survey which found that 61 per cent of Nigerians feared violence could prevent them from voting in the 2027 elections.

Mr Falana referred to the 30 October attack on African Action Congress presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore and members of his entourage in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State.

The incident generated conflicting accounts. While Mr Sowore described it as an attack by armed men, the Ekiti State Police Command said it was an altercation with another group at a restaurant.

Mr Sowore disputed the police account and questioned the identity of those arrested.

The lawyer also cited the attack on the convoy of Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, in Calabar, Cross River State.

Police said suspected hoodlums armed with machetes and sticks attacked the convoy around Watt Market Roundabout on 4 November. They later announced the arrest of a 27-year-old suspect, Victor Duke, while investigations continued.

Mr Falana also mentioned attacks on All Progressives Congress leaders in Kebbi, Katsina and Nasarawa states, saying the incidents showed that no political party had a monopoly on political violence.

He noted that political competition should be determined by ideas and persuasion rather than intimidation and the use of force.

He urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to establish a dedicated unit to investigate and prosecute electoral offenders.

Mr Falana advised the commission to obtain reports from the police and other security agencies, investigate alleged violations and take offenders to court.

“I am suggesting that INEC should have a prosecution unit with a view to getting reports from the police and other security agencies about electoral offences and then take them to court,” he said.

He also criticised the National Assembly for failing to implement the recommendation for an Electoral Offences Commission, arguing that the absence of an effective prosecution mechanism had allowed politicians involved in electoral violence to escape accountability.

The lawyer raised concerns about what he described as restrictions on opposition parties’ access to campaign platforms. He alleged that some state governments demanded between N150 million and N200 million for political billboards, depending on the office being contested.

He stated that the charges could make it difficult for opposition parties to campaign and give incumbent politicians an unfair advantage.

Mr Falana said the country already had constitutional and electoral provisions prohibiting the use of violence and armed groups for political purposes.

He cited Section 227 of the Nigerian constitution, which prohibits the establishment and maintenance of private political armies and other organisations equipped to use physical force or coercion to pursue political objectives.

He said the prohibition applied regardless of the names given to such groups, including political vanguards, enforcement teams and campaign protection groups.

He also referred to Section 228(a) of the Constitution and Section 78 of the Electoral Act 2026, which provide for sanctions relating to violations of the constitutional prohibition.

Under the Electoral Act, Section 95 requires the police to provide adequate security for political rallies and processions, while Section 96 prohibits the organisation and use of groups for political force or coercion. Section 97 also prohibits threats of force or violence intended to compel support for or opposition to a political party or candidate.

Mr Falana further cited Sections 120, 129, 130 and 132, which address disorderly conduct at political meetings and elections, possession of offensive weapons intended to intimidate voters, and the use of force or threats to interfere with citizens’ right to vote.

He explained that the failure to enforce these provisions, particularly against those who finance and organise political violence, remained a major problem.

“The problem is the gap between the law in the statute book and the law in operation,” he said.

He criticised the practice of arresting suspected political thugs while their alleged sponsors continued to enjoy political protection.

The concerns are not new. A joint election observation report by the National Democratic Institute and the International Republican Institute documented 586 election-related violence incidents and 348 fatalities during the 2023 election cycle.

The observers also reported attacks on INEC offices, personnel and electoral materials and raised concerns about the limited accountability for political actors involved in electoral violence.

Mr Falana said the government had a constitutional obligation to protect citizens, citing Section 14(2)(b) of the Constitution, which identifies the security and welfare of the people as the primary purpose of government.

He also referred to Sections 33, 34 and 35, which guarantee the rights to life, dignity of the human person and personal liberty.

He urged Nigerians to reject vote-selling, electoral manipulation and incitement, while demanding accountability from political office holders.

He said democracy should not be measured only by the conduct of elections but also by whether citizens could participate freely and hold elected officials accountable.

“We must end political violence, dismantle impunity and restore the ballot to its rightful owners,” he stated.

“The ballot must be more powerful than the barrel. That is the democracy Nigeria deserves and must collectively build.”

World.title: Tinubu, Mbah, APC and the South-East, By Collins Ogbu
World.content:
For 24 years, from 1999 to 2023, Ndi Igbo gave the PDP everything; our votes, our loyalty, our blood and our bloc. In return, what did we get? Neglect dressed as friendship. We were the bride that was never taken to the altar. Five presidential tickets, zero Igbo vice-presidential slots, zero Igbo Senate Presidency after Evan Enwerem and Adolphus Wabara, and a South-East that became the backyard of broken promises.

The PDP used our votes to build power in Abuja while our roads became death traps and our youths became statistics. That era is over. The question before us in 2027 is not about party; it is about destiny.

And here is the moral weight of this story that our children must never forget: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has been benevolent to Ndi Igbo even though a greater percentage of us did not vote for him in 2023. In most of the South-East, he got less than 10% of the votes.

Any bitter politician would have punished us. Any vengeful leader would have said, “you rejected me, so I reject you.” Tinubu did the opposite. He chose statesmanship over revenge, nation-building over bitterness. He looked beyond the ballots and saw a people who deserve development. If a man can love you when you did not vote for him, imagine what he will do when you stand with him in 2027. That is the definition of a father of the nation.

President Tinubu did what no President since 1999 has dared to do: he looked the South-East in the eye and treated us as partners in security and power, not as suspects. In the military, the highest command of this country’s security architecture now bears Igbo fingerprints.

Vice Admiral Emmanuel Ikechukwu Ogalla from Enugu State became Chief of Naval Staff; the first time an Igbo man has held that position in the Fourth Republic. And when Ogalla retired, the President did not take the position away from us. He still appointed another Enugu son, Air Vice Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, as the Chief of Air Staff.

Two service chiefs, back-to-back, from the same state, from the same South-East. These are not token appointments. These are trust appointments. Tinubu gave the Igbo the keys to the nation’s waters and its skies at a time when others said we could not be trusted. That is a political statement that history will remember.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Then came the South-East Development Commission (SEDC); a dream our fathers died for since the end of the Civil War. From 1970 to 2023, every President promised reconstruction, reconciliation and rehabilitation, and every President failed. Tinubu signed the SEDC into law in 2024. For the first time, the South-East has its own development vehicle, with its own budget, its own mandate to rebuild our region like the NDDC rebuilt the South-South. This single act alone is worth more than 24 years of PDP loyalty. It is the institutional foundation for our Marshall Plan.

For the first time in our democratic history, an Igbo son, Dave Umahi, holds the strategic Ministry of Works; the ministry that decides which region lives and which region dies economically. And he has not disappointed.

The Enugu-Port Harcourt Expressway, abandoned for 20 years, is now near completion. The Enugu-Onitsha Expressway, the 2nd Niger Bridge access roads, the Enugu-Abakaliki, the Owerri-Umuahia, the Aba-Ikot Ekpene corridors; all moving at a pace we never saw under the PDP. This is not promise. This is asphalt, concrete, and evidence.

Look home, to Enugu, and see what alignment produces. When Governor Peter Mbah made the courageous decision to align Enugu with the centre by joining the APC, cynics said he sold us out. Today, the results mock the cynics. 268 Smart Green Schools; one in every ward, built in just three years. A feat no Governor in the history of the South-East has achieved.

Enugu Talent City and the AI Institute from the NCC Digital Industrial Park leased for 15 years. Enugu Air, Enugu’s own airline. The International Conference Centre completed. The 300-bed Enugu International Hospital. Water flowing in Enugu metropolis after 20 years of thirst. This is what happens when a performing Governor is no longer fighting Abuja but working with Abuja.

The economics are even more powerful. Under Tinubu, the South-East is being reconnected to the national economy. The $1 trillion economy agenda is not Lagos agenda; it is our agenda. With SEDC, with the new coastal highway feeding into Eastern ports, with the revitalization of the Eastern rail line, with the renewed attention to the Enugu coal, Anambra gas, Ebonyi salt and Abia industrial clusters, the President is positioning Ndi Igbo to be the industrial engine of Africa again, as we were before the war. Continuity means our traders in Onitsha, Nnewi, Aba, and Ogbete will have power, roads, and ports to sell to the world without leaving home.

Let us speak the painful truth: isolation has never fed us. Political discordance has never built one kilometre of road. When we voted 95% against the centre, we got 5% of the budget. Politics is give and take. The Yoruba, our brothers in the South-West, are in power today. They understand reciprocity.

If in 2027, the South-East gives Tinubu a solid bloc vote; not 5%, not 15%, but a decisive, united, brotherly vote, we lay the moral and political foundation for the Presidency of Nigeria to come to the South-East in 2039. That is how power rotates in Nigeria. You do not get power by shouting from the wilderness. You get it by building bridges while your brother is on the throne.

The PDP gave us slogans. The APC under Tinubu and Mbah is giving us schools, roads, commissions, appointments, and respect. To vote otherwise in 2027 is to vote for a return to the wilderness; to vote for anger over wisdom, for memory over future, for isolation over influence. Ndi Igbo are not a people of self-pity. We are a people of enterprise, of strategy, of long vision. Our fathers traded across Africa because they understood alliances.

Therefore, let 2027 be the year Ndi Igbo choose continuity over chaos, stability over sentiment, and future over grudge. Re-elect President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. Re-elect Governor Peter Mbah. Vote APC at all levels; Senate, House of Representatives, State Assembly. Not because APC is perfect, but because for the first time since 1999, the South-East is finally inside the room where Nigeria’s future is decided, even when we did not vote for the man in the room. Let us not walk out of that room. Let us stay, build, and take our rightful place.

Ndi Igbo, the time is now.

*Dr Collins Ogbu, a lawyer, writes from Enugu.

World.title: Nigerian govt issues travel advisory to Addis Ababa
World.content:
The Nigerian government has issued a travel advisory, warning citizens to be cautious when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, due to its high altitude, which could pose health risks.

In a statement issued on Friday, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs warned that the high altitude could pose a serious risk to travellers with pre-existing cardiovascular and respiratory conditions.

The ministry said at least 16 Nigerians have died due to complications linked to the city’s high-altitude terrain but did not provide details.

According to the ministry, Addis Ababa, the Ethiopian capital, sits about 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure reduces oxygen availability and poses a health risk to travellers.

Addis Ababa is a major international aviation hub and the principal operating base of Ethiopian Airlines, Africa’s largest carrier.

The city serves as a connecting point for passengers travelling from Nigeria to several international destinations, making it a regular transit destination for Nigerian air travellers.

According to the ministry, healthy people are likely to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments. However, people with certain underlying medical conditions could face increased health risks.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It specifically identified cardiovascular and respiratory conditions as ailments that could be aggravated by exposure to such environments.

“People with certain pre-existing medical ailments, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory conditions, may experience increased health risks in such conditions.

“The Federal Government of Nigeria advises particularly those with pre-existing medical conditions to exercise caution and seek appropriate medical advice when planning journeys involving transit through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in view of the potential health risks associated with the city’s high-altitude terrain,” the statement read.

The ministry, however, clarified that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to Ethiopia or using Addis Ababa as a transit destination.

Rather, it said the warning was aimed at ensuring that medically vulnerable travellers were adequately informed about the potential effects of high altitude and could take necessary precautions.

“The Federal Government places a high premium on the health, safety and wellbeing of Nigerians and therefore urges all travellers to make informed decisions and take appropriate precautions, particularly where existing medical conditions may increase their vulnerability during travel,” the statement said.

World.title: NAFDAC uncovers unregistered cosmetics, falsified medicines, banned soaps at Trade Fair Complex
World.content:
By Chioma Obinna

The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has uncovered a suspected illegal cosmetics production and packaging operation at the Tools and Hardware section of Trade Fair Complex, Lagos. The raid exposes a network of unregistered products and materials allegedly intended for illicit manufacturing.

Read Also: NAFDAC uncovers another fake herbal factory in Lagos, arrests manager

The discovery followed an enforcement operation at the sprawling market along the Lagos-Badagry Expressway. Officials found unlabelled cosmetics, empty product containers, packaging materials and already-produced creams across different floors of a two-storey building.

In a video of the operation shared on its official X account on Saturday, NAFDAC officials were seen inspecting the building and displaying the recovered materials, raising concerns over the production and circulation of cosmetics of unknown origin and regulatory status.

“This is exactly what we are able to find at this particular location,” one of the officials said while displaying various packaging materials and empty containers.

The inspection revealed packaging materials bearing names such as turmeric vitamin C and other cosmetic product descriptions, alongside empty shampoo tubes, lotion containers and materials suspected to be intended for the packaging of unregistered products.

On the upper floors, officials discovered additional packaging materials, including containers for different cosmetic products, as well as already-produced glutawide cream.

The agency also displayed materials bearing different product names, but could not immediately establish the identity and regulatory status of some of the substances and products found at the premises.

NAFDAC described the operation as part of its ongoing enforcement activities at the Trade Fair Complex, where it has uncovered several suspected illegal manufacturing, storage and distribution activities.

‘Drugs’

In a related discovery at the complex, the agency uncovered a warehouse on the last floor of a building containing packaging materials for suspected falsified medicines, including Augmentin 625mg and Amplicloxa.

Bottle caps bearing the Gordon’s Gin brand were also reportedly found among the materials.

The latest discoveries add to a series of enforcement operations by NAFDAC at the Trade Fair market.

In previous raids, the agency recovered 728 cartons of Crusader soap, 718 cartons of E45 soap and quantities of Extract Gold whitening soap, products it said were banned by the Federal Government.

The repeated discoveries have raised concerns about the scale of illegal product manufacturing and repackaging activities operating within the market, as well as the potential risks to unsuspecting consumers.

Vanguard News

World.title: Nollywood sequel “Issakaba: The Return” hits cinemas after 25 years
World.content:
Nollywood action thriller ‘Issakaba: The Return’ has returned to cinemas nationwide after 25 years of the release of the original movie, ‘Issakaba’.

The director, Lancelot Imasuen, announced the cinema release in a post on his Instagram page on Friday, expressing excitement over the return of the popular movie franchise to the big screen.

In the post, Imasuen described the production as the return of a legend and urged movie lovers to watch the film in cinemas.

The sequel features veteran actor Sam Dede reprising his role as Ebube, leader of the Issakaba Boys, while introducing other actors from different generations of Nollywood.

Other cast members include Chidi Mokeme, Iyabo Ojo, Regina Daniels, Chiwetalu Agu, Alex Osifo, Charles Okafor, Nosa Rex and Mark Angel.

Directed by Imasuen, who also helmed the original production, ‘Issakaba: The Return’ revisits the story of the fictional vigilante group against the backdrop of contemporary Nigerian society.

The original film, released in 2001, drew inspiration from the activities of the Bakassi Boys, a vigilante group that emerged in south-eastern Nigeria to combat criminal activities.

The sequel, distributed by Blue Pictures, brings together returning actors and newer Nollywood performers, marking the revival of one of the industry’s recognised action film franchises. (NAN)

World.title: Rock ‘n Roll Hall of Fame honours Fela Kuti
World.content:
The legendary Fela Anikulapo Kuti

The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame will, today, honour Nigerian music legend Fela Kuti, as music stars and industry figures gather in Los Angeles to celebrate the latest inductees.

The list of inductees include Sade, Oasis, British rocker Billy Idol, rhapsodic hip-hop transformers Wu-Tang Clan, versatile rock star Phil Collins, English heavy metal band Iron Maiden, post-punk and electronic dance music renegades Joy Division/New Order and the velvet-voiced late Luther Vandross in the performer class of 2026.

Five artists will receive an “early influence” honor: Queen Latifah, Celia Cruz, MC Lyte, Fela Kuti and Gram Parsons.

The Cleveland-based Hall of Fame – which surveyed more than 1,000 musicians, historians and industry members to choose the entrants – will honor the acts in a star-studded gala concert at Los Angeles’s Peacock Theater.

But who will show up and who will perform remains iffy.

Often inductees perform themselves – the evening can serve as a way to reunite the long estranged – or fellow musicians take the stage to showcase an act’s legacy.

Several of the 2026 artists have already said they’ll skip.

Sade – the group whose sensual, captivating rhythms have endured as fan favorites for decades with hits including “Smooth Operator” and “No Ordinary Love” – said they were bowing out in a statement on their website.

“Sorry we can’t be there in person to celebrate with the other artists. Please know that our absence takes nothing away from how much this recognition means to us,” said the group, fronted by the singer Sade Adu.

Britpop’s one-time feuding brothers Liam and Noel Gallagher of Oasis – who recently announced a 2027 world tour – also declined to make the trip.

Noel Gallagher is scheduled to perform solo in London. Liam Gallagher had previously voiced disdain for the institution, and earlier this week said in an X reply to a fan: “It’s too far to be going for the night.”

Iron Maiden said they will miss the ceremony as they’re on tour in Australia.

‘Tremendous honour’

The two British rock bands Joy Division and New Order will get a rare joint induction. New Order formed from the ashes of Joy Division after the original group’s lead singer, Ian Curtis, died in 1980.

New Order went on to pioneer the future of alternative dance, with signature tracks including “Blue Monday,” “True Faith” and “Bizarre Love Triangle.”

But it’s unclear which members will attend, or if New Order will perform.

Collins – one of rock’s great drummers, whose signature hits include “In the Air Tonight” and “Sussudio” – has said health problems will keep him from taking the stage.

Staten Island’s own Wu-Tang Clan – the ragtag group of New Yorkers who paired raw production with streetwise rhymes and martial arts influences to create cinematic hip-hop that changed the game – recently wrapped a tour they billed as their last.

The Clan – known for songs like “C.R.E.A.M” and “Protect Ya Neck” – doesn’t always appear at events or even on tour as a full unit, but receiving an honor from the Rock Hall could be an apt moment for a reunion.

Ahead of Idol’s induction, Los Angeles named Friday, November 13 as “Billy Idol Day,” making it seemingly likely the rocker who came up in London’s punk scene and put out radio hits including “Dancing With Myself” will attend Saturday’s ceremony.

When his induction was announced, Idol called it “a tremendous honor.”

Eligible nominees into the Rock Hall must have released their first commercial recording at least 25 years prior to being nominated.

Vanguard News

World.title: Triumphant Democrats descend on COP31 snubbed by Trump
World.content:
Supporters of the climate campaign group Fridays for Future protest with an illuminated globe-shaped lantern during a demonstration in front of the Chancellery (Bundeskanzleramt) in Berlin on November 13, 2026, on the occasion of the UN climate summit COP31 being held in Turkey until November 20. (Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP)

Fresh from their US midterm election triumph, an emboldened group of Democratic lawmakers descended on the COP31 climate talks shunned by President Donald Trump on Saturday to signal their commitment to tackling global warming.

The 18-strong delegation joined the annual UN conference in Turkey after their party regained control of both chambers of Congress in a landslide victory last week cheered by climate campaigners.

“Many of our allies and partners across the world think the United States has not been predictable or dependable. So we have a lot of trust to earn back,” Florida Representative Kathy Castor told AFP.

“We have so much work to do. And yes, I hope the United States gets back on track with urgent climate action,” she said after the group took photos in front of a large COP31 sign in a sprawling expo centre.

The election has been a topic of discussion at COP31 in Antalya, with hopes that Democrats can restore some clean energy policies and that a pro-climate president can be elected in two years.

“What happened in the US is remarkable, and a much needed shift that we all needed, not only from a climate perspective, but overall,” Harjeet Singh, strategic advisor to the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative, told AFP.

Since taking office in January 2025, Trump has rolled back some of the clean energy policies of his predecessors, promoted oil drilling, pulled the United States out of the Paris Agreement and kept his country out of the UN’s climate negotiations.

“It is absolutely shameful that the Trump administration operates this way, that this is an administration that is filled with climate deniers, that is beholden to big oil in the United States,” Yassamin Ansari, an Arizona lawmaker, told AFP.

– ‘Climate action alive in America’ –

Ansari and other members of the delegation spoke at a panel focused on the midterm elections, attracting a crowd that overflowed outside the “America Is All In” pavilion.

The group reminded COP31 delegates that, while Trump has rejected clean energy, US states and local governments have continued to promote renewables and other pro-climate policies.

A group of US mayors and governors visited COP31 earlier this week, along with former US vice president Al Gore and former US climate envoy and secretary of state John Kerry.

“Despite the setbacks that we’re experiencing through this Trump administration, climate action is alive in America,” California Congressman Raul Ruiz told the panel.

The president’s Republican party was handed a resounding defeat last week in large part due to anger over soaring energy prices and Trump’s costly war with Iran.

Democrats have vowed to use their majority in the House and the Senate to launch investigations into the administration’s climate policies and propose clean energy legislation.

But Trump still has two years left in office and has vowed to wield his veto power.

“At a time where Americans from all political backgrounds want to see their energy bills reduced, this administration will be very hard pressed to veto legislation that will bring down costs for the American people,” Ansari said.

World.title: US proposed ceding Ukraine territory in exchange for joining NATO
World.content:
File: Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky . Photo by Handout / UKRAINIAN PRESIDENTIAL PRESS SERVICE / AFP.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said that the United States proposed Ukraine cede land to Russia in exchange for joining NATO and that his government was in talks on “specific” security guarantees from the West.

Read Also: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China – White House

“The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Zelensky told reporters Friday in comments embargoed until Saturday.

He said Ukraine was discussing “specific security guarantees from NATO and the EU” and that if Western countries confirmed them “then I will ask our Ukrainian society what it thinks: do we accept it or not? I have no right to make that decision on my own.”

‘Dangerous’

Ukraine’s Presiudent Volodymyr Zelensky said the EU and NATO are Europe’s only “real security”, warning the Kremlin’s bid to change the continent’s security architecture could lead to more wars.

“This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations,” Zelensky told reporters Friday in comments only releasable on Saturday. “Real security in Europe means the EU and NATO. That’s it. There is no other security in Europe.”

Russia’ winter war

Russia is “betting everything” on this winter’s campaign in its war with Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in comments released Saturday as he called for a US military package that would pressure President Vladimir Putin to end the fighting.

“They are betting everything on this winter,” Zelensky told the media Friday in comments kept under embargo. He said the US Congress adopting “sanctions and weapons” legislation would be “the kind of motivation Putin needs” to de-escalate.

Vanguard News

World.title: I can never insult Peter Obi; we parted ways amicably — Tanko
World.content:
By Henry Umoru, Abuja

The National Coordinator of the Social Democratic Party, SDP Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Yunusa Tanko, has taken a swipe at those behind viral reports circulating online alleging that he spoke ill of and used unprintable words against the candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, ahead of the January 16, 2027 election, Peter Obi, saying he cannot ever insult his former principal.

The National Coordinator of Prince Adewole Adebayo and Dr Usman Bugaje’s Presidential Campaign Council described the fabricated reports as the desperate handiwork of those he described as mischief-makers and political detractors bent on sowing discord and tarnishing his hard-earned reputation.

In a statement signed on Saturday by the Chief Media and Communications Advisor, Adebayo-Bugaje (Ade-Buga) Presidential Campaign Council, Comrade Mark Adebayo, Tanko explained that anyone familiar with his character and political journey knows that he is a principled, decent, and respectful individual who neither engages in blackmail nor trades in insults.

He expressed complete confidence that Peter Obi would immediately dismiss the falsehoods, knowing full well the mutual respect they share.

“I can never insult His Excellency, Mr Peter Obi,” Dr Tanko stated emphatically. “We parted ways peacefully and with absolute mutual understanding. Politics is about vision and service, never about bitterness or personal attacks.”

Reiterating the sentiments he shared during his unveiling as the National Coordinator of the Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Tanko expressed deep appreciation and lasting gratitude to Mr Obi for the relationship they shared during his tenure as an aide and as the National Coordinator of the Obidient Movement Worldwide.

“I remain forever grateful to His Excellency, Mr Peter Obi, for the wonderful opportunities he gave me to serve alongside him and lead the Obidient Movement worldwide. I thank Mr Obi, and I stand proudly by the records of my service with him,” he added.

Dr Tanko, who warned purveyors of fake news that their attempts to manufacture bad blood between him and his former principal have failed before arrival, affirmed that he and the 2023 presidential candidate of the Labour Party (LP) remain the best of friends and pledged that he will continue to accord the former Anambra State Governor the utmost respect at all times.

The Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council urges the general public and members of the press to disregard the malicious publications in their entirety and rely only on verified communications from the council.

World.title: How lifestyle, late detection fuel diabetes crisis in Nigeria
World.content:
As Nigeria joins the rest of the world to commemorate World Diabetes Day(WDD), marked annually on Nov. 14, health experts have warned that changing lifestyles and late detection are fuelling a diabetes crisis in the country.

WDD is commemorated to raise awareness on prevention, early detection and care.

Diabetes Mellitus, a chronic metabolic condition characterised by elevated blood sugar due to inability of the pancreas to produce enough insulin or impaired insulin action, has become a major public health concern, with complications including blindness, kidney failure, heart failure, stroke and limb amputation.

According to the International Diabetes Federation (IDF) Diabetes Atlas, globally no fewer than 589 million adults live with diabetes, with 24.6 million in Africa.

About 11 million adults live with the condition in Nigeria, with many unaware of their status.

Experts said the disease, which could remain undetected for years without symptoms, was now killing more Nigerians than malaria, HIV and tuberculosis combined.

An Endocrinologist, Prof. Michael Olamoyegun, said diabetes killed more Nigerians than malaria, HIV and tuberculosis combined.

Olamoyegun is Professor of Medicine and Endocrinology at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology and also Consultant Physician and Endocrinologist at LAUTECH Teaching Hospital, Ogbomoso, Oyo State.

He said diabetes is a metabolic disorder of carbohydrates, fats and protein.

He added that it is characterised by elevated blood sugar due to inability of pancreas to produce enough insulin.

According to him, diabetes also occurs if insulin action is impaired.

He said there are many variants but three main types existed – Type 1, Type 2 and Gestational Diabetes.

” Type 1 diabetes, which occurs due to absolute deficiency of insulin, is seen mainly in younger age group, usually less than 30 years, although occasionally in adulthood.

“It is found in about five to ten per cent of all individuals with diabetes.

“This group is managed with insulin injections since the body no longer produces insulin.”

The endocrinologist said Type 2 diabetes represented 90 to 95 per cent of individuals with diabetes, stressing it occurred when insulin was not able to function well in the body.

He also noted that it usually occurred in older individuals who had family history in first-degree relatives.

Olamoyegun, also the Secretary General of the Association of Clinical Endocrinologists of Nigeria (ACEN), added that hypertension, overweight or obesity and sedentary lifestyles were contributory risk factors.

He said it is usually managed with oral medications, dietary control and occasionally with insulin.

On gestational diabetes mellitus, he said it was first detected in pregnancy, saying it complicated about 7.5 to 12 per cent of all pregnancies.

He explained that diabetes in pregnancy made it high risk as it could worsen outcomes for mother and foetus.

On prevalence, he said the number of people living with diabetes had increased worldwide and in Nigeria.

“Globally, more than 600 million people are living with diabetes, 25 million in Africa, while seven per cent, that is 11 million adults older than 18 years, in Nigeria have diabetes.

“Most people with diabetes are unaware of their status.

“The number of Nigerians living with diabetes increased by more than 21 per cent in last five to six years.

“In Nigeria, most individuals with diabetes are aged 45 to 59 years (mostly productive years).

“At least 15 to 20 per cent of people admitted into medical wards in most tertiary hospitals in Nigeria have diabetes and they usually have one complication or another,” he said.

“Globally, diabetes kills one person every five to six seconds, every 30 seconds, someone’s leg is amputated due to diabetes.

“Nigeria has one of highest rates of amputation due to diabetes in the world and most amputations are major amputations, below or above the knee,” he said.

Vanguard News

World.title: Tight security as Tinubu visits Jos for APC presidential rally
World.content:
File image

By Golok Nanmwa, Jos

Security has been beefed up in Jos, the Plateau State capital, ahead of the expected arrival of President Bola Tinubu on Saturday for the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-Central presidential campaign rally.

Our correspondent, who visited several parts of the city, observed a heavy deployment of security personnel at strategic locations, including Hill Station Junction, Zaria Road, Polo Roundabout and parts of Yakubu Gowon Way, as security agencies intensified surveillance ahead of the President’s visit.

Tinubu is expected to attend the APC presidential rally scheduled to hold at the Zaria Road Stadium, Jos, where he is also expected to commission three major development projects executed by the Plateau State Government.

The projects are the Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) Centre in Jos, the Plateau Special Activity Centre (P-SAC) and 50 hybrid Jet Mover buses for inter-local government transportation.

Ahead of the President’s visit, Governor Caleb Mutfwang, APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, and former Deputy Governor, Dame Pauline Tallen, inspected the facilities.

Speaking on the BPO Centre, Mutfwang described it as a strategic investment in human capital development, job creation and economic empowerment.

According to a statement signed by his Director of Press and Public Affairs, Gyang Bere, the governor said the facility, established through a partnership between the Plateau State Government, Outsource Global and MTN Nigeria, has an operational capacity of 800 seats and is projected to generate up to 2,400 direct full-time jobs when fully deployed across three shifts.

He said the centre would connect Plateau youths to the global digital economy through customer experience management, technical support and back-office services.

Mutfwang added that young people would be able to work for international organisations from Jos and earn in foreign currencies.

On the Plateau Special Activity Centre, the governor said the facility was established to strengthen intelligence-driven security operations, stressing that security remained fundamental to sustainable development.

The centre comprises a Fusion and Analytical Centre, Geo-Intelligence/GIS Unit, Drone Unit, Training Centre and Profiling Room to enhance intelligence gathering, threat detection, analysis and coordinated security responses.

He also said the 50 hybrid buses would improve public transportation, reduce travel costs and enhance connectivity across the state’s 17 local government areas.

Meanwhile, during an inspection of the Zaria Road Stadium, venue of the rally, Mutfwang expressed confidence that the event would attract massive participation from APC supporters and stakeholders across the North-Central region.

He urged residents to turn out in large numbers to welcome Tinubu, whom he described as a statesman committed to the development and security of Plateau State.

The APC National Chairman, Yilwatda, commended the governor and the Presidential Campaign Council for coordinating preparations for the rally.

He expressed satisfaction with arrangements covering the rally venue, security, airport logistics and traffic management.

“The preparation is top-notch, and I’m impressed with what I’ve seen in terms of the venue preparation, security, airport, street mapping and everything. It is excellent. I expect that tomorrow will be a wow on the Plateau,” he said.

Yilwatda expressed confidence that the APC would mobilise massive support for Tinubu, citing the party’s growing political structure and the involvement of former governors, deputy governors, speakers and other prominent political stakeholders.

World.title: Federal Ministry of Finance’s Draft Nigeria Economic Policy Framework: Can It Deliver More Than Another Document?
World.content:
By Ugo Inyama

A government can improve its accounts while families struggle to balance theirs. Investment announcements can increase while businesses face high operating costs. Economic indicators can strengthen before citizens experience meaningful relief.

The challenge of economic policy is to connect these realities: to turn stability into opportunity, stronger revenue into effective services and reform into better living standards.

That should be the central test of the Federal Ministry of Finance’s draft Nigeria Economic Policy Framework.

The consultation, which opened on October 26 and closes on November 27, proposes enduring principles, decision rules and performance measures for economic policymaking across successive administrations. It remains a draft, open to public comment.

The initiative deserves serious engagement. Businesses benefit from predictable policies. Households need confidence that the costs of reform have been considered. Public institutions need clear responsibilities and consistent standards against which their performance can be assessed.

The question is whether this framework will establish those disciplines in practice.

One of its strongest proposals is a Policy Impact Statement for every major economic intervention. This would examine the evidence, available alternatives, distributional effects, fiscal implications, implementation capacity, performance indicators and exit conditions. The draft also proposes public scorecards and independent reviews.

These provisions could improve government decisions. Their effectiveness, however, depends on when assessments are published, how thoroughly they are scrutinised and what happens when officials disregard them.

Except in clearly defined emergencies, impact statements should appear before implementation. Citizens and businesses need an opportunity to examine assumptions and raise concerns while changes remain possible.

The final framework should also define a major intervention carefully. Budgetary cost is only one consideration. A regulatory restriction may cost government little while substantially increasing expenses for businesses and consumers. The number of people affected and the severity of the consequences should also determine the level of scrutiny.

Oil revenue illustrates why this matters.

Additional receipts can finance investment, reduce debt, settle outstanding obligations or strengthen savings. But temporary gains can also encourage commitments that become difficult to sustain when prices or production decline.

A sound framework should require government to distinguish exceptional receipts from dependable income. It should explain how additional resources will be used, disclose the risks and identify the benefits citizens should expect.

The same approach should apply to tax incentives and industrial protection. Support should have a clear economic purpose, measurable outcomes and a review date. Where benefits fail to materialise, government should be prepared to revise or withdraw it.

Consistency must nevertheless leave room for democratic choice.

Future administrations should retain the authority to change policies in response to evidence, public preferences and economic circumstances. The lasting obligation should be to justify decisions transparently and assess their consequences.

Any legislation arising from the framework should therefore strengthen standards of evidence, consultation, disclosure and evaluation. It should avoid making one administration’s preferred economic choices unnecessarily difficult to reconsider.

Emergency flexibility is also essential. Government may sometimes need to act quickly. In such cases, it should publish the justification, estimated cost, duration and arrangements for subsequent review. Extensions should require fresh evidence.

Digital governance can help make these requirements workable.

Each major intervention should have an accessible public record connecting its assessment, budget, responsible institution, implementation milestones and evaluation findings. Consistent identifiers would make it easier to follow a policy from approval through expenditure to results.

Public dashboards should be supported by downloadable data, clear methodologies and revision histories. Researchers and journalists must be able to examine the evidence behind official conclusions. Personal information, particularly that of vulnerable beneficiaries, should remain protected.

Independent scrutiny is equally important. Statistical measurement, financial audit and policy evaluation perform different functions. Their responsibilities should be explicit, and the institutions involved should have the authority and resources to publish findings without undue interference.

The framework must also specify what follows when an institution fails to comply. Published corrective action plans, responsible officials and deadlines would provide a practical starting point.

Ultimately, household welfare should carry substantial weight in assessing economic performance.

Growth, revenue and investment are important foundations. Progress must also be visible in purchasing power, employment quality, poverty reduction and access to functioning schools, healthcare and other essential services.

Where reliable data permit, national results should be broken down to show differences across regions and population groups. An improving average can conceal persistent hardship.

Implementation will require clear ownership, adequate capacity and realistic milestones. Existing reporting systems should be strengthened, with states and local governments involved within their constitutional responsibilities.

The consultation offers an early opportunity to demonstrate that approach. The Ministry should explain how public submissions influenced the final framework.

Nigeria needs economic rules that improve decisions and make results easier to verify. The framework’s value will become clear when its standards shape everyday government practice and when citizens across the country begin to experience the benefits.

*Ugo Inyama

Executive Director

African Digital Governance Centre

www.africandgc.org⁠

Ugo@africandgc.org⁠

World.title: NMDPRA Seeks Effective Collaboration in Movement of Petroleum Products in S’ South
World.content:
Sylvester Idowu in Warri

The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) has called for effective collaboration in the movement of petroleum products.

NMDPRA also sought for vigilance and adherence to established operational standards in the region.

The South South Regional Coordinator of NMDPRA, Mr Ibrahim Dimowo, made the call on Thursday during the ‘Technical Working Committee (TWC) Trucks-in-Transit 2nd Road Show’ safety sensitisation programme held in Warri.

Dimowo said that the programme would build upon the successes and lessons learned from its maiden edition held in Lagos State.

He added that the road show would further help deepen safety awareness among operators and drivers within the South-south region.

“The programme is designed to provide practical knowledge on defensive driving, hazard recognition, fatigue management, fire prevention, spill containment and journey management planning.

“It will also help to provide tanker integrity standards, emergency response actions and regulatory expectations for petroleum transportation,” he said.

Dimowo said that the programme was aimed at reflecting on the collective commitment to improving safety standards in the transportation of petroleum products across the country.

The coordinator noted that the movement of petroleum products remained a critical component of Nigeria’s energy security and economic development.

He said that the development posed serious concerns that required a collective effort to address.

“I wish to specially acknowledge the dedication and contributions of members of the Technical Working Committee on Trucks-in-Transit.

“Through your tireless efforts, the committee has continued to champion initiatives aimed at reducing road tanker accidents, strengthening preventive measures, enhancing emergency preparedness and response capabilities within the downstream petroleum industry.

“Your contributions have undoubtedly supported the protection of lives, property and the environment while fostering greater stakeholder collaboration in achieving our shared safety objectives,” he said.

Dimowo also commended the tanker drivers and transport operators, noting that their daily responsibilities had placed them at the forefront of product distribution across the country.

“Every safe trip completed is a testament to your commitment to protecting lives and preserving the integrity of the petroleum supply chain,” he said.

Dimowo appealed for effective collaboration to build a safety culture where every journey “begins safely, progresses safely and ends safely”.

He expressed confidence that the knowledge gained from the engagement would further strengthen collective efforts towards preventing incidents and ensuring safer roads for all users.

National President of the Nigerian Association of Road Transport Owners (NARTO), Alhaji Yusuf Othman, said the association was in full support of the Trucks-In-Transit innovative.

Othman, who was represented by the General Manager (Administration) of the association, Mr. Atiku Ahmed, said that safety awareness on the roads was a shared responsibility of the drivers, transport owners, regulators and the communities.

“We are not bystanders in this effort, our members own the tankers, employ the drivers and bear the consequences when things go wrong.

“Every tanker crash is therefore more than a statistic, it is a human tragedy that affects families, businesses and communities,” he said.

Othman quoted the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) to have stated that between January and September 2026, 7,156 road crashes were recorded.

“The FRSC Corps Marshal announced on Monday that a total of 7,156 road crashes was recorded, while 3,445 death and 22,292 injuries recorded nationwide in the period under review,” he said.

The national president of NARTO said that the alarming tragedy was a pointer that the issues of tanker safety must never be treated as optional.

“However, the FRSC reported a 61.29 per cent reduction in tanker and trailer- related fatalities in 2025. This shows that sustained cooperation can save lives and we must keep building on the progress,” he said.

Othman said that NARTO recognised safety as a fundamental responsibility of its members, while focusing on drivers’ training and awareness, compliance before and after loading, speed limit devices, preventive test and public enlightenment.

While urging members to obey speed limit and proper rest, Othman advised the public to keep a safe distance from crash or leaking tanker.

He reaffirmed the association’s commitment to the Truck-in-Transit programme and the shared goal of eliminating tanker accident and explosion on the roads.

In his presentation, the Assistant Corps Marshal Operations of the FRSC, Dr. Omiko Godwin, said that safety was a shared responsibility involving the drivers and regulators.

Godwin, who spoke on the topic: ‘Staying alive on the highway: Defensive driving, fatigue and hazards awareness for tanker drivers,’ said that tanker driving required higher standard of professionalism.

According to him, the product they coveyed had higher risk of rollover, adding: “Any ignition can cause fire outbreak, therefore, professional competence is required.

“You must know your route, be discipline before the wheel and see every other road user as a mad man. Look ahead and be focused, create space between you and the next vehicle because brake can fail.

“The product does not worth the life of anybody, not even a beggar. Tannker drivers should remember that they have families, therefore, they should take every caution to ensure they arrive safely,” he said.

Godwin attributed 90 per cent of crashes involving tanker drivers to over speeding and fatigue.

“A tanker on the road must have two drivers.

A tired driver is an unsafe driver, therefore, operators should provide a relief driver so that when one is tired, the other driver will take over,” Godwin said.

He advised drivers to also check the condition of their vehicle before embarking on a journey.

The National President of Petroleum Owners Association of Nigeria, Dr. Billy Gills-Harry, said that the downstream operators could significantly reduce tankers risk accident through proactive and preventive measures.

Gills-Harry spoke on the topic: ‘From response to prevention: Practical measures to reduce tanker discharge at retail outlets accidents.’

“The transition from response to prevention requires disciplined operation, continuous training, strong supervision, improved infrastructure, modern technology and unwavering commitment to safety at every retail outlets,” he said.

The National Assistant Secretary of the Petroleum Tanker Drivers (NUPENG branch), Mr. Emmanuel Omokero, who spoke on behalf of the participants, thanked the organisers of the event.

“This is the first time we are seeing this type of training in Warri, we are grateful. Before now, we have warned our drivers that no truck should drive at night, if you are tired, rest before you embark on your journey,” he said.

Delta Coordinator of NMDPRA, Mr. Godwin Ikomi, on his part, said that the sensitisation programme would be sustained.

The event was attended by representatives of government agencies, security and emergency response organisations, tanker drivers, petroleum marketers, depot operators, truck owners among others.

World.title: Pharmacy Academy Urges Nigeria to Prioritize Health Security, Local Drug Production
World.content:
Uchechukwu Nnaike

The Nigeria Academy of Pharmacy has called for increased investment in pharmaceutical research, local medicine production and technological innovation to strengthen Nigeria’s health security and reduce vulnerabilities in the supply of essential medicines.

The academy said the country must move beyond dependence on imported medicines and critical pharmaceutical technologies by building a resilient, self-reliant pharmaceutical industry capable of responding to emerging health challenges.

The President and Chairman, Governing Council of the academy, Prof. Lere Baale, stated this ahead of its 2026 annual general meeting and investiture of new fellows, scheduled for November 16 and 17 in Lagos.

Baale said Nigeria’s health security cannot be separated from its economic independence and scientific capabilities, stressing the need for a coordinated national approach to pharmaceutical development.

In a statement signed by the Secretary-General, Lekan Asuni, the president expressed the organisation’s believe that national health security must become a strategic priority amid increasing healthcare demands, emerging infectious diseases, antimicrobial resistance and challenges in medicine supply.

He said the forthcoming gathering would examine how Nigeria could harness pharmaceutical knowledge, research, scientific innovation, technology and regulatory excellence to develop a more equitable and sustainable healthcare system.

Baale added that the academy would continue to promote collaboration among government, academic institutions, pharmaceutical manufacturers, regulatory agencies, healthcare professionals and development partners to translate scientific knowledge into improved health outcomes.

The event, themed, ‘Pharmacy for National Health Security: Advancing Innovation, Medicine Sovereignty and Sustainable Healthcare’, will feature a keynote address by the World Health Organisation Representative and Head of Mission in Nigeria, Dr. Pavel Ursu on November 17.

The two-day programme will also feature the investiture of new fellows into the academy in recognition of their professional achievements, scholarship, leadership, innovation and contributions to pharmacy and society.

Baale described the fellowship as a responsibility that should inspire professionals to contribute meaningfully to national development.

He said, “Fellowship of the Nigeria Academy of Pharmacy is not simply an honour to be received; it is a responsibility to be discharged. Our Fellows must be architects of solutions, champions of innovation, mentors of future generations and courageous voices for policies that improve the health and well-being of Nigerians.”

The academy said the admission of new fellows would strengthen its role in promoting scientific advancement, professional standards and evidence-based policies on national health and development.

The AGM will hold on November 16, at 11am at the Business School Netherlands, GRA, Ikeja, Lagos. Participation is restricted to academy fellows.

The investiture ceremony and keynote address will hold on November 17, at the Old Great Hall, College of Medicine, Lagos University Teaching Hospital.

The ceremony is open to the public, including policymakers, healthcare administrators, pharmaceutical industry executives, researchers, professional associations, development partners and media organisations.

World.title: NGF Partners Grand Challenges Nigeria to Scale up Research, Tackle Maternal, Newborn Mortality
World.content:
* As Tinubu’s aide urges states to adopt, fund health innovations to curb maternal deaths

The Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Public Health in the Office of the Vice-President, Uju-Rochas Anwukah, has called on state governments to prioritise health research by adopting and funding locally developed innovations capable of reducing maternal and newborn mortality.

Anwukah warned that research findings would amount to little if they remained on paper without translating into practical interventions that improve healthcare delivery and save lives, particularly those of women and newborn children.

She made the call on Friday at the Nigerian Governors’ Forum and Grand Challenges Nigeria Annual Meeting and Innovation Exchange, where stakeholders reviewed locally driven healthcare innovations and explored strategies for scaling up successful interventions.

The presidential aide, who is also the Board Chair of Grand Challenges Nigeria, urged federal and state governments to demonstrate stronger commitment to research by providing the institutional support, funding and policy framework required to sustain successful innovations beyond their pilot stages.

“Too many promising ideas end up as reports on a shelf, while the families they were meant to help never feel the difference. This meeting is about closing that gap,” she said.

Anwukah disclosed that 10 Nigerian-led projects had received seed funding of up to N60 million each from Grand Challenges Nigeria since inception, while eight beneficiaries participated in the meeting to showcase their innovations and engage with potential implementation partners.

She recalled that Vice-President Kashim Shettima launched the initiative at the State House two years ago, making Nigeria the seventh African country to join the Grand Challenges network.

According to her, investment in healthcare must begin with mothers and newborn children, stressing that a healthy start remains fundamental to human capital development and national productivity.

“That investment has to begin with the mother and the newborn because a healthy start is the foundation of every productive life,” she said.

She, however, cautioned that healthcare interventions that collapse immediately after the expiration of donor grants should not be regarded as successful.

“A pilot that ends when the grant ends is not a success at all. It is a missed opportunity,” Anwukah said.

She identified credible evidence, institutional ownership, adequately equipped frontline health workers and sustainable financing as critical requirements for scaling up promising healthcare innovations.

The presidential aide urged federal and state governments, alongside development partners, to make concrete commitments on the innovations they intend to adopt, specifying implementation timelines and the officials responsible for delivering them.

“When we gather again next year, the question will not be what we discussed but what we delivered together,” she added.

Also speaking, the Senior Programme Officer, Nutrition at the Gates Foundation, Alem Hadera Abay, described maternal and child health as critical areas requiring urgent intervention.

Abay noted that Nigeria continued to record high maternal and child mortality despite improvements in some child health indicators, urging the country to intensify efforts towards meeting its commitments under the World Health Assembly targets and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Similarly, the Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Mukhtar Yawale Muhammad, called for stronger collaboration among researchers, regulatory agencies, state governments and private-sector organisations to ensure that research outcomes translated into practical solutions.

Muhammad said research initiatives must move beyond pilot stages through institutional backing, sustainable financing and clearly defined implementation strategies.

He emphasised the importance of involving potential users and implementing institutions from the earliest stages of research development, rather than waiting until pilot projects had been completed before seeking adoption.

In his remarks, the Director-General of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum Secretariat, Dr Abdulateef O.T. Shittu, represented by the Head of Health Team, Dr Chinekwu Oreh, acknowledged the challenges confronting state governments in maternal and newborn healthcare, primary healthcare delivery and sustainable health financing.

He said innovations must be designed around the practical realities of Nigeria’s healthcare system to achieve meaningful impact.

“The question before us is therefore not simply what innovations exist, but which ones work, under what conditions, and how we can make them available to more Nigerians,” he said.

Shittu urged stakeholders to identify institutions capable of adopting promising innovations and establish realistic timelines for implementation.

“The true value of innovation lies not in the novelty of an idea, but in its capacity to improve lives,” he added.

Earlier, the Programme Director of Grand Challenges Nigeria, Godwin Bamsa, said the initiative was established to mobilise funding for locally developed innovations addressing Nigeria’s health and development challenges.

He explained that the programme was focused on identifying local healthcare needs, supporting Nigerian researchers and connecting innovators with institutions capable of adopting their solutions.

The President of the Nutrition Society of Nigeria, Professor Salisu Abubakar, also called for stronger partnerships among researchers, government institutions and development partners.

Abubakar recalled that Grand Challenges Nigeria was launched in November 2024 with support from the Gates Foundation and the Office of the Vice-President to promote and fund locally driven innovations.

He urged the Nigeria Governors’ Forum and the Federal Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology to demonstrate concrete commitments towards funding and implementing promising research outcomes.

Meanwhile, Associate Partner at Dalberg, Ms Chimdi D. Owundiegu, challenged Nigerian innovators to strengthen partnerships with relevant institutions to bridge the gap between research and implementation.

She observed that many promising innovations remained unused because of weak connections between research organisations and the institutions responsible for deploying their findings.

Owundiegu also identified the proposed National Research Institute as a potential mechanism for addressing fragmentation in research funding and coordination.

She, however, stressed that the proposed institution must maintain effective partnerships with public- and private-sector organisations to ensure that research outcomes translate into measurable improvements in maternal and child healthcare.

World.title: ADC-PCC Demands Withdrawal of Tinubu’s ‘All Is Fair in Politics’ Remark, Warns Against Political Violence
World.content:
The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has called on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to publicly withdraw his “All Is Fair in Politics” remark, warning that the statement could fuel political violence, embolden thugs and threaten the nation’s peace and stability ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Council also urged the President to embrace peaceful coexistence by condemning inflammatory statements and alleged acts of violence by some governors and chieftains of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

The ADC-PCC made the demands in a statement signed by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, in which it expressed concern over what it described as the President’s silence on alleged political violence involving members of his party.

It accused the Presidency of adopting a selective approach to condemning political violence by cautioning opposition parties while allegedly shielding those accused of perpetrating violence within the APC.

“President Tinubu cannot claim to desire peace when his own words provide cover for violence.

“‘All Is Fair in Politics’ is not the language of a Head of State. It is the language of political desperation and an open licence for thuggery, ballot snatching, intimidation and bloodshed,” the statement said.

The Council alleged that opposition supporters had been subjected to attacks in different parts of the country, including Edo, Cross River, Gombe, Lagos, Kebbi and Kaduna.

“From Edo to Cross River, Gombe to Lagos, and Kebbi to Kaduna, Nigerians have witnessed attacks on opposition gatherings, destruction of campaign materials and the brutalisation of innocent supporters, allegedly by APC-sponsored thugs.

“Yet, Mr. President has not considered it necessary to call his governors and party members to order,” it added.

The ADC-PCC further faulted the Presidency for what it described as diversionary tactics, alleging that it blamed victims and preached restraint to opposition parties while members of the ruling party were accused of unleashing violence.

It challenged Tinubu to explain why his condemnation of political violence appeared to be directed at opposition parties rather than members of his own political fold.

It asked: “Why has Mr. President refused to condemn APC governors who openly threaten opposition supporters? Why has he remained silent over public incitement by officials of his party? Why is his anger always directed at the opposition and never at those within his own political fold?”

The Council maintained that the ADC remained committed to peaceful and issue-based political engagement, noting that its campaign was focused on addressing Nigeria’s challenges, including hunger, insecurity, unemployment and corruption, as well as what it described as the failures of the Tinubu administration.

It also accused the APC of resorting to violence because it had little to offer Nigerians in terms of credible solutions to the country’s problems.

Consequently, the ADC-PCC outlined three demands: the immediate and public withdrawal of Tinubu’s “All Is Fair in Politics” remark; condemnation and a call to order for APC governors and party officials accused of inciting violence; and a directive to security agencies to protect all Nigerians impartially.

The Council also invoked former President Goodluck Jonathan’s position on political ambition and the sanctity of human life, insisting that no electoral contest should come at the expense of Nigerians’ lives.

“Nigeria belongs to all of us. No political ambition is worth the blood of any Nigerian.

“If former President Goodluck Jonathan could make that profound declaration in 2015, President Tinubu has no excuse not to say so and demonstrate the sincerity of his commitment to peace in 2026.

“The ADC will not be intimidated. We will continue to campaign peacefully, and in 2027, Nigerians will have the opportunity to vote for competence, integrity and a new beginning,” the statement added.
