Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness (seated, third left) participates in a Grange Pen Housing Development contract signing at the Housing Agency of Jamaica (HAJ) corporate office in St Andrew on Thursday. Also taking part are (seated, from left) China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC) Project Manager Hoinan Wong; CHEC Country Manager Dangran Bi; permanent secretary in the Ministry of Economic Growth and Job Creation Arlene Williams; HAJ Chairman Norman Brown; and HAJ Managing Director Doreen Prendergast. Looking on are (standing, from left) CHEC Legal Counsel Colleen Franklin; HAJ Senior Manager and Legal Services Peta-Gaye Ellington; Minister of Tourism Edmund Bartlett’ and permanent secretary in the Ministry of Tourism Jennifer Griffith.Photo: Karl Mclarty

A $24-billion housing development that will deliver 1,446 new units in Grange Pen, St James, and expand housing opportunities in the busy tourism parish has been welcomed by Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness as a significant step forward following Thursday’s signing of a construction agreement.

Under the deal signed by the Housing Agency of Jamaica (HAJ) and China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC), at least 20 per cent of the units will be reserved for tourism workers as the Government moves to tackle housing shortages in areas experiencing rapid tourism-related growth.

Speaking at the signing ceremony at the HAJ’s St Andrew corporate office, Holness said the development also forms part of a wider push by the Government to keep pace with employment opportunities, particularly along the north coast, where informal settlements tend to develop due to insufficient housing solutions.

“The idea is to ensure that we are positioning the housing stock where people work. That’s very important. A large part of the informal and insecure settlements that we have was that the jobs came first and the housing lagged behind. The jobs came first and there was no proper transportation system for people to leave where they lived to get to work. And so, people had to make do to live where the land was in proximity to where they work,” reasoned the prime minister.

Holness added that the Government has insisted that all new hotels provide housing for their workers, while he has directed the HAJ, and the National Housing Trust (NHT) to dedicate more housing solutions to the tourism sector.

“So, we are trying to get ahead of the curve and I would want to say that in the next 10 years we should not have this problem of informal settlements popping up because people just simply don’t have anywhere to live in proximity to where the jobs are,” added Holness.

He pointed out that the contract between HAJ and CHEC requires at least 60 per cent of the workforce on the housing development to be Jamaicans.

“In every project that we have done, we have put in place this requirement that there is a certain percentage of Jamaicans who must hold the jobs. On the north coast, where we’re doing the Montego Bay Perimeter Road, not only have we put in a quota for Jamaicans, we have put in place a system of training where the Jamaicans who are participating there are also certified at the end of their duty on that project. So we are ensuring that at the end of these large projects the Jamaicans who are trained, their skills are certified,” Holness said.

Thursday’s proceedings also included the signing of an HAJ contract to add 301 units to the existing 1,506 homes under the fifth phase of the Catherine Estate development in St Catherine.

Holness, who described Catherine Estate as one of the agency’s most successful housing developments, welcomed the increase, noting the demand for housing in the area.

“I’m saying it’s the most successful to date because of the size of it, but also because it has managed to maintain a price point. I was told that for the 1,000 units they have more than 20,000 applications,” he noted.

Meanwhile, Tourism Minister Edmund Bartlett pointed to earlier investments in the Grange Pen area, where he said more than $1 billion had been spent on the regularisation of existing settlements and the provision of community infrastructure.

According to Bartlett, the initial component of that development is now 90 per cent complete and included work on roads, water, electricity, and sewage systems.

“The prime minister is about ready to hand over 535 titles to 535 families who otherwise would have been called squatters or, to be more pedantic, informal settlers.

“Today, they are homeowners with tenure on a property that belong to them and they can leave [it] to their great, great grandchildren. So the brownfield was done. And we hope that with the development that CHEC is involved with us, we will see the full completion of that,” said Bartlett.

He added that discussions were under way with a mortgage provider to introduce a financing arrangement that would allow tourism workers to repay housing loans over periods of 30 to 40 years.

Bartlett said the proposed arrangement, which he described as a “patient mortgage”, is intended to make homeownership more accessible by reducing the monthly repayment burden on workers.

“This is an innovation that the Government of Jamaica, led by Prime Minister Andrew Holness, has been driving, and it’s our part in making sure that we don’t only have housing solutions, but affordable solutions,” added Bartlett.

World.title: Craigy T readies new music
World.content:
Craigy T.

On the heels of the success of his debut solo album, Ascension: Out of Many… 1, which topped the iTunes Reggae Albums global chart and earned Grammy consideration, international dancehall artiste Craigy T is preparing to release new music.

The entertainer has joined forces with producer KickRaux for his upcoming single, Music Within Me, slated for release in late November.

For Craigy T, the song carries a deeply personal message, reflecting the passion and resilience that have sustained him throughout his nearly three-decade musical career.

“Music Within Me kinda defines my very essence in its lyrics. It verbalises what keeps me going when times are tough. It was written several years ago and has chosen now to reveal itself,” he said.

The collaboration developed after the two connected through Instagram, with KickRaux expressing an interest in working with Craigy T after listening to Ascension.

“I did some research into his work and was equally impressed. Skip, skip, skip, and here we are,” Craigy T recalled.

Although their creative partnership is relatively new, the artiste said they have already established a productive working relationship, particularly when navigating their unconventional musical ideas.

“Both of us tend to have way-out, unorthodox ideas. Whenever one wanders too far, the other provides grounding for the project, and we interchange those roles throughout the process,” he explained.

For KickRaux, the objective was to create something distinctive without sacrificing the musical appeal that allows listeners to connect with a song.

“We live in an impersonal, digital world where trends and algorithms run our lives. As soon as something catches a hype, everyone starts copying it. Craigy T and I didn’t know where our collaboration would land, but the one rule was ‘Don’t blend in,’ ” he said.

“I used organic sounds to paint the musical backdrop. I wanted the music to be creative and forward-thinking, but not so left field that you couldn’t just put it on, hold a vibe, and enjoy yourself,” the producer added.

KickRaux said he was particularly impressed by Craigy T’s willingness to experiment and the vulnerability reflected in his solo material.

“Working with Craigy T feels like working with a new artiste, because he’s so open to trying new sounds. But at the same time, he’s reggae and dancehall royalty. A hitmaker who knows what people want to hear,” he said.

“You can really hear his classical training in the way he approaches harmonies. He’s always coming up with ideas you wouldn’t expect. We kept finding new ways to approach the music,” he continued.

Released on August 7, the 17-track Ascension: Out of Many… 1 showcased Craigy T’s versatility, blending dancehall, reggae, and soul influences. The project also attracted international radio spins and play list placements in territories including the United Kingdom, Japan, Latin America, and Africa.

While the album introduced audiences to a more personal dimension of his artistry, Craigy T believes his forthcoming single will take listeners even further into his creative world.

“I think Music Within Me is an evolution of the material in Ascension, not a departure. So, not different, but diving deeper into my mind,” he explained.

Meanwhile, the entertainer’s evolving solo journey has earned praise from international radio personality DJ GQ, who recently interviewed him on

Dancehall Cyaan Done, aired on SiriusXM’s Bob Marley Tuff Gong Radio.

Describing Ascension as a masterpiece, DJ GQ said the project represents a long-awaited opportunity for audiences to experience Craigy T’s individual creativity.

“Massive! This type of energy, vibe, and expression was long overdue. Definitely a masterpiece,” he said.

Having known the entertainer for more than 30 years, DJ GQ said one of the highlights of their recent conversation was discovering that he had unknowingly influenced Craigy T’s early career through a childhood stage show featuring Spragga Benz.

The radio personality also underscored the importance of providing platforms for established entertainers who continue to contribute to the evolution of Jamaican music.

“Veteran dancehall artistes don’t just guide and influence the new generation of music; they are literally the role models and legends for the genre!” he said.

As he prepares for the release of Music Within Me, Craigy T remains appreciative of the support he continues to receive while embracing new creative opportunities.

“I am truly grateful to be able to continue sharing my gift with my tribe. Every day is a new day with new experiences or sometimes similar experiences from a new perspective. I welcome life’s changes and new directions. It excites me,” he expressed.

Fans can also anticipate additional material from the partnership, with KickRaux confirming that more collaborations are on the horizon.

“Definitely look out for more from us,” Craigy T added.

World.title: US grounds all flights, sparking travel chaos
World.content:
MIAMI, United States — Passengers wait in the terminal of Miami International Airport on November 13, 2026. US aviation regulators issued an extremely rare ground stop of all flights across the country after a major communications outage which the Department of Homeland Security said did not appear to be the result of any “nefarious attack”. (Photo: AFP)

NEW YORK, United States (AFP) — All flights in the US were grounded Friday, sparking travel chaos across the vast country, after what government officials said was a major communications outage, insisting it was not the result of any “nefarious attack”.



The nationwide stop left tens of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events.

The incident marked only the second time such an alert was given in US airspace since the 9/11 attacks.

“So supposedly, nobody’s flying, but they haven’t told the public yet,” said an exasperated Joseph Anderson, 72, who was trying to fly from Las Vegas to Oakland, California.

“We’re trying to debate whether or not we need to reschedule or drive or what, but if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too.”

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) “issued a nationwide ground stop for all US airports following a communication issue impacting all air route traffic control centres,” the agency said. “FAA technicians are investigating the issue.”

In a subsequent message on X, the agency described the problem as “a temporary telecommunications outage” and said it was acting “out of an abundance of caution”.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no sign of a threat to the United States.

“This isn’t another 9/11,” he said.

“There was no indication, as of yet, that this was a nefarious attack against us, it’s just a telecommunication outage, as of right now,“” Mullin said, adding officials were “not ruling out anything at this point”.

There was a short nationwide stop in January 2023 when a pilot notification system failed, but the only other national stop happened in the wake of the 9/11 attacks, when no aircraft took to the skies for days.

Friday’s FAA order came a day after US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy formally asked Congress for US$30 billion to upgrade and modernise the US Air Traffic Control System.

“This investment is critical to complete the modernization of our national airspace — delivering a resilient telecommunications backbone for air traffic controllers, modern hardware and software, state-of-the-art control towers, and world-class airport infrastructure,” Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought wrote in a letter to lawmakers.

It also came the same day that Microsoft apologised for a global outage that wreaked havoc for millions of users, public services and businesses worldwide.

The company ruled out any malicious “cyber or AI” activity as the cause of the disruption, which affected several Microsoft products from Thursday. Most operations had resumed by late Friday.

World.title: MEXICAN STAND-OFF
World.content:
Jamaica Reggae Boyz squad members go through their paces during their final training session on Friday ahead of the Concacaf Nations League quarter-final, first-leg football match against Mexico at the National Stadium on Saturday. (Photo: Karl Mclarty)

Mexico are usually favourites heading into most matches in Concacaf competitions, but Jamaica Reggae Boyz interim Head Coach Rudolph Speid says his players are undaunted and confident of pulling off a major upset to put themselves in a strong position.

The national senior football men’s will take on the Mexicans this evening at 8:00 pm at the National Stadium in the first leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarter-finals.

Since the competition’s inception in 2019, Jamaica have only qualified for the semi-finals once in their history, back in the 2023/24 season when they beat Canada in the last eight.

They will now have one of their toughest tests yet as they take on the mighty Mexicans who soared to 10th in the FIFA Rankings following their Round-of-16 finish in last summer’s FIFA World Cup.

The Reggae Boyz have struggled against Mexico, winning just four of their 32 meetings. Their last victory came in the 2017 Concacaf Gold Cup semi-final, with the team winless in their last six encounters since.

Speid, though, says the team is eager to prove their worth against one of the world’s best.

“It’s surreal to be playing against such a good team twice but there’s a reason why the game is played. It’s because the result is not guaranteed by anyone,” he said. “These are the times that you trained for as a player, these are the games you want to play if you’re really a good player and ambitious, and these are the games that a coach would like to coach against some of the top coaches, so it’s all good.”

“This is a part of our development. It’s a rebuilding squad, and we have to be forged in fire if we want to go forward in the future.”

Jamaica, who finished runners-up behind Guatemala in the group stage last month, completed their fourth and final training session on Friday morning at Stadium East field. Speid believes the extended time together has been beneficial.

“Familiarity helps, it is good. We were able to just continue what we were doing [from the last window] and add a few surprises; so I think the team is more prepared than they would have been in the qualifying rounds.”

With Mexico boasting considerable attacking firepower, including Gilberto Mora, Julián Quiñones and Santiago Giménez, Speid will have to navigate the tie without goalkeeper and Captain Andre Blake, who is sidelined with a groin injury.

“He’s probably one of the best goalkeeper in Concacaf, if not the best, so it’s a big miss for us. We’re just hoping that he’s well though and he’ll join us later on when we go further in the competition,” said Speid.

The interim boss has also had to contend with several other injury concerns and withdrawals from the squad. However, he insists those setbacks will not serve as an excuse for his team not to compete.

“I always believe that whenever players get injured or for some reason they can’t turn up, Jamaica is a big enough country,” said Speid “We give a lot of other players opportunities, we’re still in a rebuilding phase, so it’s good for some of the youngsters to get a run out and new players to get a call-up. So we don’t really think about it a lot, we just move on with business.”

One player who has benefited from the injury list is striker Ricky Jade-Jones who earned his first call-up to the national team.

The 24 year old, who currently plays for FC St Pauli in Germany’s second division, says he’s hoping to make a good impression.

“Obviously I’m really excited and I couldn’t wait to just get started. The training’s been good, I feel good in myself. The team feels good, we’ve got a good bond. We’ve only been here for a couple of days and I feel really part of it already, so I’m looking forward to the game,” he said.

New Mexico boss Rafael Marquez, who took over from Javier Aguirre following the World Cup, has yet to get off the mark, going winless in his first four games.

Speid is an admirer of the former star defender but has no intentions of taking him lightly.

“I’m just as hungry as he is to win a game. Every game is new, we have to start all over. He was a wonderful player when he used to play for Barcelona, he definitely has some characteristics that we studied very well, so I’m hoping to beat him,” he said.

“I’ve seen them play a lot, pull off extraordinary victories, especially in the World Cup just recently. We know they’re ranked number 10, we know what they bring. They easily are the best team over the years in Concacaf but the teams from the Caribbean have improved a bit and we expect for that to come on show in the tie,” Speid added.

Jamaica, who conceded four goals in four games during the Nations League group stage, will have to be wary with the introduction of the away goal rule.

Both teams will be looking for the advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return leg at the Estadio BBVA.

World.title: JFF president confident win over Mexico will put Jamaica on the football map
World.content:
Michael Ricketts, president of the Jamaica Football FederationPhoto: Garfield Robinson

Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) President Michael Ricketts believes a win for Jamaica against Mexico could play a significant role in boosting the country’s football and commercial profile.



The Reggae Boyz host Mexico in their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final first leg today at the National Stadium, starting at 8 pm.

The national senior men’s team are coming off a successful group stage campaign where they finished second in Group B with their only loss from four games coming against Honduras.

However, they are now one of the region’s and world’s best in Mexico who have made the final of every Nations League since the competition’s inception in 2019.

After Jamaica’s historic third-place finish in 2023/2024 season, they crashed out in the quarter-final stage in the 2024/2025, losing to the USA 5-2 on aggregate.

That disappointment was compounded by a group-stage exit at the Concacaf Gold Cup last summer and their failure to automatically qualify for the FIFA World Cup last November.

Ricketts, though, is hoping that the players will show a better fight this time around.

“It’s going to be tough but we have to ensure that our players are mentally prepared and that’s key and probably that’s what we’ve been lacking over the last few years,” he told the Jamaica Observer.

“We have not been able to execute very well on the field of play but we’re looking forward to moulding a set of young players that will represent us well.”

Mexico are coming off an impressive FIFA World Cup campaign, where they served as hosts, after advancing to the round of 16 and narrowly losing to eventual third-place finishers England.

The Mexicans, ranked number 10 in the world, have an incredible record against Jamaica with 23 wins from 32 games.

Ricketts believes victory could put the world on notice that Jamaica intend to end their World Cup drought ahead of the 2030 edition.

“We are bracing ourselves for that and a good result against Mexico would certainly send a message around the world that we are on a path of recovery and we are on a path of recruiting young players that are committed to the process of getting us to the World Cup by the next edition in 2030,” the JFF boss said.

“To beat Mexico certainly would send a strong signal, would send a strong message and we not just want to beat Mexico but we want to do very well, we want, of course, to be into the Gold Cup when that time comes around.”

The JFF missed out on nearly $2 billion after missing last summer’s World Cup. Ricketts isn’t expecting any major financial gain from the Nations League but believes it can be the start of their recovery path.

“We are hopeful that we will be able to get things right at the latter part of this year so that next year financially and from a commercial perspective, we would be in a better position than we have been in the last few months,” he said. “We would have invested heavily in probably six World Cup qualifying tournaments and that would have cost us hundreds of millions of dollars. We must now try to recoup some of those lost funds.”

“Next year I’m pretty certain that things will be a lot better from a commercial standpoint. We, of course, maintain our main sponsor adidas and there are some local sponsors who have always been there for us and with us. As we get back into the marketplace for a new year, we are very optimistic and hopeful that we on the field of play will do enough so that we can attract some of these new business partners that will help us to grow the sport.”

— Daniel Blake

World.title: FAA grounds all flights across US amid communications problem
World.content:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a nationwide ground stop, grounding all flights across the United States (US) until further notice because of what it described as extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns.

According to CNN, the FAA said a communications problem affecting Air Route Traffic Control Centres, which manage flights travelling across the country, prompted the disruption.

The cause of the problem was not immediately known. However, preliminary reports from two law enforcement officials indicated that it was not a cyberattack, CNN reported.

The nationwide ground stop is a rare occurrence. The last time such a measure was implemented was in January 2023, when a pilot notification system went down. Before that, a nationwide ground stop was issued following the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

World.title: CORRECTION AND APOLOGY
World.content:
On October 16 2026, the Jamaica Observer on its online edition published an article entitled “Update: Two men killed after gun battle with police in Sligoville” which contained a photograph and several allegations and statements concerning Lamond Sutherland.

The information contained in the article was published based on information received from law enforcement authorities at the time. It has since been established that Mr Lamond Sutherland was incorrectly identified, that the allegations and statements were false and that he was not in any way a party to the incident.

Jamaica Observer unreservedly retracts the article and sincerely apologises to Mr Lamond, Sutherland who is still very much alive, for any distress, embarrassment or damage to his personal and professional reputation which may have been caused by the publication.

World.title: US suggested Ukraine could give up Donbas for NATO membership, Zelenskyy says
World.content:
Giving up Donbas has long been part of the proposals put forward by U.S. President Donald Trump's administration, including the 28-part plan for a peace agreement proposed by the White House in 2025. Russian President Vladimir Putin has previously demanded that Ukraine abandon its efforts to join NATO and accept strict limits on the size of its military.

“I have said repeatedly: Ukraine is not retreating and is not giving up its land to terrorists,” Zelenskyy told reporters.

The White House and U.S. State Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Zelenskyy said he was discussing a “comprehensive security package” with partners that would include specific guarantees from NATO and the EU, a strong Ukrainian army with adequate troops, weapons and financial support for a set period and a recovery plan with clear funding attached.

“If the American side confirms precisely this to us, together with other NATO partners, then I will ask our Ukrainian society what it thinks: do we accept it or not? I have no right to make that decision on my own,” Zelenskyy said. "Of course, this would be without any recognition of the occupied territories as Russian," he added.

“But we need specifics, and we don't have them yet. All of this is still under discussion,” the president said.

Veronika Melkozerova contributed to this report.

World.title: Finland rejects reported Russian demand to leave NATO as part of peace talks
World.content:
Russia proposed withdrawing its nuclear weapons from Belarus and refraining from stationing intermediate-range missiles there in exchange, Bild reported.

But it remains unclear which proposals Russian President Vladimir Putin would support after discussions between intermediaries, according to the report.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said a new security framework for Europe for after the war raised by the Americans “can be dangerous."

“Russia certainly cannot make decisions on behalf of all the societies that are members of NATO,” he told reporters on Friday.

Zelenskyy’s comments were not in direct response to the demands reported by Bild, but came after a meeting between Zelenskyy and U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on Thursday in Dublin.

“Putin's desire to change borders in Europe is a fact. I am sure this is part of his concept of revising security guarantees in Europe. This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations,” Zelenskyy said.

World.title: EU deal on Ukraine talks overshadows AI-focused summit in Dublin
World.content:
Ireland, which holds the EU’s rotating presidency and hosted the informal gathering, had billed the meeting as a rare chance for a high-level discussion on how to develop artificial intelligence in accordance with European values.

But the question of how to secure peace in Ukraine — and who should negotiate on Europe’s behalf — quickly dominated discussions, as leaders sparred over the format of future peace negotiations and warned about the risks of a potential deal brokered between Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Indeed, a meeting next week between the U.S. and Russian leaders has set Europe on edge, prompting warnings about a possible Yalta-type agreement in which superpowers would decide on European security questions over the heads of countries directly concerned, reminiscent of talks toward the end of World War II that divided Europe up between the four allied powers.

UAE’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al-Nahyan, members of the Ukrainian and Russian delegations hold talks mediated by U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff Jared Kushner in Abu Dhabi on November 10, 2026. | Pool photo by Altaf Qadri/AFP via Getty Images

“That is why I want to make our message to the U.S. very clear: Please, no surprises!” German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said regarding the Trump-Putin meeting, scheduled to take place during an APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 18-19. “Continue to play on Team Europe and on the same team as Ukraine. And let’s work together for genuine peace in Ukraine.”

The question of who should represent Europe in future discussions about Ukraine and the post-conflict security order was added to the summit’s agenda at the last minute, following a request from Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.

Earlier in the day, Merz had voiced preference for a narrower group made up of officials from Berlin, Paris and London, while Kaja Kallas, the EU’s chief diplomat, argued that she was best placed to lead discussions.

World.title: Why Europe failed to find a superhero to take on Putin
World.content:
The push to identify one representative to speak for Europe was understandable. The appeal of having a single, respected leader taking the reins is largely based on a desire to project European strength and unity — as well as an interest in making negotiations with Russia, the U.S. and Ukraine efficient and effective.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy himself said this week he wanted Europe to identify within days who will take its place in the talks, and suggested he’d prefer it was one person (he even indicated that he had a preference, though would not reveal a name).



He didn’t get his way. Instead, leaders at a summit in Dublin on Friday, decided that the “E5” made up four big EU countries ― Germany, France, Poland and Italy ― and the U.K., plus officials from the European Commission and Council, would take the work forward as a team.

Technical discussions

The search for a top representative to fill Europe’s seat at the negotiating table at the next round of peace talks had become a political obsession in Brussels that missed at least two big points.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy takes part in a press conference at Government Buildings in Dublin on November 11, 2026. | Paul Faith/AFP via Getty Images

The first is that the leadership level is not currently where the negotiations are at. Talks this week in Abu Dhabi were technical discussions between senior officials. The big political players like Putin and Zelenskyy were not there, never mind Trump. Russia sent a Kremlin aide to lead its team and Ukraine tasked its intelligence chief with making its case.

If these officials make progress toward a deal, leaders will no doubt want to get involved. Ultimately, it will be leaders who sign any peace agreements that follow — and there’s no limit on the number of EU presidents or prime ministers who could join such a meeting as signatories or guarantors of the final deal.

The next thing that needs to happen, according to both Ukraine and the U.S. envoys mediating the talks, is for Europe to join the discussion with Russia — at this technical level.

World.title: Le Pen offers to meet Zelenskyy in Brussels
World.content:
Marine Le Pen delivers a speech during a visit of the "Salon Made in France" at Parc des Expositions of Porte de Versailles, in Paris on November 13, 2026. | Geoffroy van der Hasselt/ AFP via Getty Images

The Ukrainian leader wants to persuade the far-right leader to continue supporting Ukraine if she becomes president of France.

PARIS — Far-right leader Marine Le Pen said she would be prepared to hold talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Brussels, in the wake of her promises to stop French financial aid to Ukraine.

Speaking on the sidelines of a trade fair in Paris, Le Pen said a meeting in Brussels would be “justified” because “the topic of Ukraine financing is rattling Europe.”

“The German chancellor is starting to threaten people, it’s starting to be an issue in Europe and it would be interesting to discuss this,” she said in a reference to Friedrich Merz’s threats to cut EU funds for countries who refuse to support Ukraine financially.

World.title: Cut off from Europe, Russia will have to rewire its Arctic gas trade
World.content:
The LNG trade “is going to look completely different,” said Malte Humpert, senior fellow and founder of the think tank Arctic Institute. The ban gives Moscow “a bigger incentive” to find another route, he said. “It’s not easy. It’s not cheap. It’s very slow,” but Russia will “figure it out.”

From black markets to new ports

An increase in black market LNG trade could be one way out. A classic shadow fleet has not been needed so far, since Yamal is not under sanctions, said Sebastian Rötters, sanctions campaigner at Urgewald.

Nor is a shadow fleet well suited to the job. They typically use old, unregistered oil tankers that can easily disguise their movements. On the other hand, there are fewer LNG carriers globally and they follow a limited number of routes, making them easier to track, said Martin Vladimirov, a senior analyst at the Center for the Study of Democracy, a think tank that follows EU sanctions policy.

Bovanenkovo gas field on the Yamal peninsula in the Arctic circle on May 21, 2019. | Alexander Nemenov/AFP via Getty Images

One possible workaround is a “virtual swap.” Russia could sell more gas to countries such as Turkey or China, which could then sell more of their own or other countries' gas to Europe. That would preserve Russia's income even as its LNG is barred from European ports, Vladimirov said.

But even if Moscow finds buyers, it still has to get the LNG to them. That means Russian ships unable to access Europe will need to rebuild their logistics chains to sail farther or transfer their cargoes to other ships elsewhere before sailing on to alternative markets.

Either way, officials are already gearing up to confront the anticipated increase in black market activity. The matter requires “more attention on the European level," said Lithuanian Energy Minister Lukas Savickas, whose government will helm the EU's six-month rotating presidency from January.

World.title: Microsoft outage renews European calls to detox from US tech
World.content:
Mensch didn't specifically address the Microsoft outage, which lasted nearly 24 hours and affected millions of users in 74 countries. Still, the shutdown of key tools like Outlook email and Teams messaging impacted plenty of the tech and government leaders gathered in Dublin to chart Europe’s AI future.

French President Emmanuel Macron closed the day with a post on X: “Our independence cannot be outsourced. It must be built here at home, in Europe,” he wrote. "When it comes to artificial intelligence, too, Europe has everything it takes to compete. We have no time to lose.”

An EU diplomat present at the leaders' talks said that "we need to pick up speed, permitting and investment to compete on the world market, to have sovereignty."

Tech sovereignty, including control over the cloud, chips and models that power AI, has been a rallying cry of the second mandate of European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, and was one of the key agenda items at Friday's gathering of the leaders of the EU's 27 member countries.

"We have outsourced too much of our digital infrastructure to actors outside the EU," Finnish European Parliament lawmaker Aura Salla said in a press release Friday following the outage. She suggested that government contracts specifically "must support European technology."

Others zoned in on the risk created by relying on digital infrastructure controlled by a couple of large companies.

World.title: Ex-Labour MP accused of sexual harassment joins Plaid Cymru
World.content:
In 2023, five women alleged that Davies, a former Commons select committee chair, subjected them to unwanted sexual attention, both physical and verbal, after coming into contact with them through his work as an MP. Davies had the whip suspended as a Labour MP immediately after the allegations were made public but remained a member of the party until 2025.

When the claims against Davies were first reported by POLITICO, he said he did not “recognize” them, adding: “If I have inadvertently caused offence to anyone, then I am naturally sorry.”

In these instances, the women had raised concerns about his behavior informally but had not complained in writing.

At least two women later filed official complaints with the Labour Party, resulting in an investigation lasting more than a year.

Davies was not eligible to stand as a candidate in the 2024 election because he was suspended, and quit the party ahead of a planned hearing on his conduct in 2025. As a result, the hearing never went ahead.

The former MP for Swansea West argued in the article published Thursday that the party engineered his removal as a candidate for factional reasons. “I was made to wait 23 weeks without any complaints. When complaints were made, they were ‘to support other women’ who had not made any complaints. None were reported to Parliament,” he said.

World.title: Hungary seizes millions in cash found buried in forests amid corruption investigation
World.content:
Hungarian authorities said they seized more than €17.5 million in cash buried in forests and hidden in other places across the country this week.

 

On 12 and 13 November, the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) carried out coordinated searches at multiple locations across Hungary, including in Budapest and the counties of Pest, Békés and Nógrád, as part of a criminal investigation involving Miklós Seszták, a former minister of national development.

During the searches, investigators uncovered large amounts of cash hidden in a variety of spots: buried in forests, concealed in agricultural buildings and warehouses, stashed inside residential properties and stored in a high-value safe in a remote location.

Over the course of the two-day operation, investigators recovered a total of 5,071,632,000 forints, €2,658,350 and $1,257,100. On Friday, NVVH staff paid the cash into the Hungarian State Treasury.

According to the investigation, there is reason to suspect that between 2015 and 2018, Seszták and the CEO of Hungarian National Asset Management (MNV) received more than 11 billion forints in illicit payments from representatives of companies contracted by Volánbusz, a national bus operator.

The NVVH previously announced that an earlier search carried out in October at the Kisvárda home of Seszták had uncovered safes of a type more commonly used by financial service providers and pawnshops.

On 30 September, the Buda Central District Court ordered the detention of Seszták at the request of the NVVH.

In late October, the court announced that Seszták's detention had been extended until 30 January. It cited the seriousness of the case and the risk that he might flee or go into hiding.

World.title: Latest news bulletin | November 14th, 2026 – Midday
World.content: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond in this Euronews news bulletin. In just a few minutes, our newsroom brings you the latest news and breaking news across world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel, with the context you need to make sense of a fast-moving day. Reported with the independence and the European perspective that define Euronews, this regular round-up gives you a clear and reliable overview of the stories shaping our world right now, wherever you are watching from.

World.title: US floats Ukraine ceding land to Russia in exchange for NATO membership: Zelenskyy
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Washington had proposed the idea of Ukraine ceding land to Russia in exchange for NATO membership as efforts to bring an end to the war continue.

 

"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelenskyy told reporters on Friday in comments embargoed until Saturday, the AFP news agency reported.

Zelenskyy added that Ukraine was discussing "specific security guarantees" from NATO and the European Union and that he would ask Ukrainians if they accepted the terms should Western nations confirm.

"I have no right to make that decision on my own," he said.

It comes after Russian President Vladimir Putin met with US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow earlier this week.

During their meeting, Putin signalled that Russia would not back down on territorial demands to control parts of Ukraine and rejected the idea of foreign peacekeeping troops being deployed in the country.

The US envoys later met with Zelenskyy in Ireland on Thursday to discuss ongoing diplomatic efforts, with the trio announcing that, moving forward, Europe would have a "voice" in peace negotiations.

"This will allow us to address the broader postwar European security arrangements alongside the territorial issues between Ukraine and Russia," Kushner wrote in a post on X.

Russian foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova appeared to dampen hopes of such an agreement on Friday, saying that as far as her department was aware, "the issue was not discussed during the talks with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow."

In further comments shared by the ministry on Friday morning, presidential aide Yuri Ushakov added: "For our part, the position of the Europeans has been comprehensively outlined."

"They are striving by every means possible to join the negotiations, but, as our President has said, they must decide whether they want peace or the continuation of the war," he said.

World.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet in China, White House says
World.content:
US President Donald Trump is set to meet with his Russian and Chinese counterparts Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in China next week, the White House said on Friday.

 

The trilateral meeting is scheduled to take place in Shenzhen in southeastern China on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, according to the White House.

"The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous," White House spokesperson Olivia Wales told reporters.

Trump is also expected to discuss the Iran war but not Ukraine, US officials said, per the AFP news agency.

A senior US official speaking on condition of anonymity said Washington had a "whole other track" of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at bringing about an end to the war in Ukraine.

"China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn't seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there," they said.

Moscow and Beijing have so far not commented on the reported meeting.

Trump is also scheduled to hold bilateral talks with Xi in Shenzhen.

The president is set to depart Washington on Monday for the Philippines, where he is due to attend a meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations before making his way to Shenzhen.

Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk is slated to join Trump in China but will not be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, officials said.

APEC

The 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will bring together leaders from 21 member economies from 18 to 19 November.

According to APEC, the summit will focus on key issues including artificial intelligence, trade tensions and economic growth.

Mao Ning, a spokesperson for China's foreign ministry, said Beijing was looking forward to the event and to achieving "more practical results" with partners in areas such as AI, trade, connectivity and digital economy.

World.title: Regular coffee drinking linked to changes in gut motility and microbiome
World.content:
A scientific study carried out by the University of Copenhagen has found that drinking coffee regularly may affect the functioning of the digestive system, especially bowel movements and colon contractions and is also linked to greater diversity of gut bacteria.

 

The study was published in the journal "Gut Microbiology", which specialises in research on gut microorganisms, and aimed to explore the relationship between habitual coffee consumption and the physiological conditions inside the digestive system.

What does coffee do inside your digestive system?

The research team used a small electronic capsule that participants swallowed to track the changes that occurred as it travelled through the digestive system.

The capsule measured a set of indicators, including the time it took contents to pass through the gastrointestinal tract, temperature, acidity levels and intestinal contractions.

The study involved 61 healthy adults in Denmark, whom the researchers divided into two groups according to how much coffee they consumed.

The first group consisted of people who drank between one and five cups of coffee a day on more than three of the eight days covered by the study, while the second group comprised people who drank coffee less frequently.

The results showed that people who consume coffee regularly have greater diversity in the microorganisms present in their intestines compared with participants who drink less coffee.

This finding is consistent with research suggesting that coffee may influence the composition of the gut microbiome, the community of bacteria and other microorganisms that live inside the digestive system.

Francesca Bucci, the lead researcher in the study and a PhD student in the Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports at the University of Copenhagen, said that regular coffee consumption seems to affect the physiology of the intestines.

One of the most notable results was that people who drink coffee regularly had much lower acidity levels in the small intestine than those who consume it less often.

The researchers also observed a link between higher coffee intake and a greater number of contractions in the colon, muscle movements that help push intestinal contents through the digestive system.

These contractions play a role in digestion and in keeping bowel movements regular, as they help move waste along and may help prevent constipation and keep the intestinal muscles in good condition.

Bucci said that intestinal contractions can support proper digestion, help reduce constipation and help maintain the functional state of the intestinal muscles.

By contrast, the researchers are still unable to determine whether the lower level of acidity in the small intestine benefits health or could have negative effects.

Is coffee responsible for the changes?

The researchers stress that the study cannot prove that coffee consumption is the direct cause of the changes observed in the digestive system.

However, Henrik Munch Roager, associate professor and head of the research group in the Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports at the University of Copenhagen, believes there are reasons to support the possibility that coffee plays a role in these changes.

He explained that previous studies have shown that coffee affects a range of processes that take place inside the digestive system, including the secretion of acids in the stomach.

He added that this evidence makes it likely that the differences the researchers observed are linked to the effects of coffee rather than being mere coincidence.

He pointed out that many people notice, based on their daily experience, that coffee affects their digestion.

The research team sees the next step as conducting a study that allows control over the amount of coffee participants drink, instead of merely observing their consumption habits and comparing the differences between them.

This type of study would help determine whether coffee is actually causing these changes and to understand the mechanisms through which it may affect bowel movements and contractions.

World.title: Russia urges IIHF to move Canada world juniors as hockey boycotts spread
World.content:
The Russian Ice Hockey Federation is insisting that the World Junior Championship, due to take place in Canada next month, be postponed or cancelled after Ottawa decided not to allow the Russian team to take part in the tournament.

 

As the official Russian news agency TASS reported on Thursday, the president of the Russian Ice Hockey Federation, Vladislav Tretiak, threatened to demand compensation from Canada and possibly also from Germany, which will host the men’s World Championship in 2027, if Russia is barred from participation.

Speaking at a meeting of the Presidential Council for the Development of Physical Culture and Sport in Moscow, Tretiak said he had also appealed to the International Ice Hockey Federation’s (IIHF) ethics committee to open an investigation and impose sanctions on national federations that are organising boycotts of games involving Russia.

"There are rules: if a team does not take to the ice, it suffers a technical defeat and sanctions are imposed," TASS quoted Tretiak as saying. "The IIHF has a way out - either they let us play, or, if we are unable to enter Canada, they move the championship, do not stage it at all, or impose sanctions on the Canadian ice hockey association."

Related Norway dropped from junior hockey championship to make room for Russia

"You cannot bomb Ukrainian cities and then send your juniors... as if you were civilised people"

Tretiak’s statement came a day after Canada confirmed that Russian players would not be allowed to compete in the 10-nation tournament, which is due to begin on 26 December in the province of Alberta. Canada adopted this stance in response to a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) last month that restored Russia’s right to take part in international ice hockey competitions.

That decision overturned the ban the IIHF had imposed on Russia after the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

"You cannot bomb Ukrainian cities and then send your juniors to Alberta to play hockey, as if you were civilised people. No Russian or Belarusian teams at the World Junior Championship. Not under your flags. Not under any other flags. Period," Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said in an unequivocal statement.

Russian President Vladimir Putin with young ice hockey players during a visit to the Volga-Arena multi-purpose sports complex in Nizhny Novgorod, 28.08.2026 Kirill Zykov/Sputnik

As the Russian sports daily Sport-Express reported (source in Russian), Russia had from the outset expected that visas for the World Championship would be refused, so the Russian Ice Hockey Federation was planning to put together a squad made up solely of players from North American NHL clubs. However, Ottawa said that even these Russians would not be able to play for the national team in any case because their work visas do not allow it.

In addition, Germany and several other countries have refused to sign the new schedule for the World Junior Championship if Russia is included. The head of the German Ice Hockey Association, Frank Lutz, said this at a meeting of the Bundestag’s sports committee (link in German) (source in Russian).

The next tournament in the ice hockey calendar is the women’s under-18 World Championship in Ostrava, Czechia, from 8 to 16 January 2027, but Prague has also made it clear in advance that it will not issue visas to Russian players.

For its part, Germany is considering dropping the men’s World Championship in spring 2027 against the background of a wave of boycotts. Several of the world’s leading ice hockey nations have said they will not play Russia after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled that Russia and Belarus should be readmitted to international ice hockey competitions.

Meanwhile, Germany’s "fringe" parties, the far-right Alternative for Germany and the far-left Die Linke, have called (source in Russian) (link in German) on Berlin not to obstruct the participation of the Russian team.

The International Ice Hockey Federation is so far refraining from commenting on the dispute, finding itself at the centre of a rapidly escalating conflict. A number of national federations, including those of Canada, Sweden, Finland, Germany, Czechia and Latvia, have already announced that they will not play matches against Russia. Some tournament sponsors have also threatened to end their cooperation if Russia is allowed to take part.

Related Hockey nations refuse to play Russia as Germany weighs pulling out as host

For the IIHF, moving the World Junior Championship at such a late stage would be extremely difficult; it would also be very hard to find another country willing to take over as host from Canada. On Sunday Norway said it had received notification from the IIHF that it was being excluded from the tournament, to make room for Russia. The federation itself has not yet announced this change.

Several northern countries plan to bar all Russian athletes

Finland is tightening (source in Russian) (link in English) restrictions on the entry of Russian citizens into the country. On 12 November 2026 the government adopted a decree stating that the entry of Russian citizens poses a threat to Finland’s international relations. The new restrictions cover short-term work carried out on the basis of a visa, including professional sport.

"As long as Russia’s aggressive war continues, Russian athletes have no business in Finland. Their entry into the country would pose a threat to Finland’s international relations. The same applies to other types of short-term work on visas that do not serve Finland’s vital national interests," said Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen.

Finnish Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen speaks at a joint press conference with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot in Helsinki, 14 September 2026 Mikko Stig/Str / Lehtikuva

The restrictions will apply to all Russian athletes, including those competing under neutral status. The Foreign Ministry said Russia "uses sport as a propaganda tool and seeks to exploit it to advance the aims of its illegal war of aggression".

Oslo has announced similar steps following Helsinki’s decision. The Norwegian government intends to expel Russian and Belarusian professional athletes and their entourages if they try to enter the country to take part in sporting events while the war in Ukraine continues.

The Norwegian government statement stresses that Russian elite sport is closely linked to the authorities and therefore cannot be "considered in isolation" from the war in Ukraine. Belarus, it notes, has supported and facilitated Russia’s war, according to the text (link in Norwegian) (source in Russian).

"Since Russia continues its brutal war of aggression, the government does not want Russian and Belarusian professional athletes and their support staff to come to Norway to take part in international sporting events," said Minister of Culture and Equality Lubna Boby Jaffery.

The government decision, which will come into force "in the near future", could affect the participation of Moscow and Minsk in several events, in particular the opening round of the FIS Ski Jumping World Cup in Lillehammer from 20 to 22 November.

Finally, the authorities in Tallinn have notified the International Ski and Snowboard Federation (FIS) that athletes from Russia and Belarus will not be able to take part in competitions held in Estonia. From 18 to 24 January, Otepää will host the World Championships for juniors and under-23 athletes in Nordic skiing, and in February the World Biathlon Championships will take place at the Tehvandi Sports Centre ski stadium.

"Estonia has firmly condemned Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine from the very beginning. Since then, the Estonian government, the Ministry of Culture and the Estonian Olympic Committee have held to a common position that Russian and Belarusian athletes and teams must not take part in international sports competitions until the war in Ukraine is over," says a letter from the Ministry of Culture to FIS, the details of which have been reported (source in Russian) in the press.

At the same time, there were reports that Russia has refused (source in Russian) to take part in the European Boxing Championships for athletes aged 19 to 22, which will be held from 15 to 24 November in Porec, Croatia. The reasons were the Croatian authorities’ requirement that they compete without the Russian flag and anthem, and the refusal to issue visas to members of the Russian delegation.

World.title: Can Europe’s tech firms really replace Amazon, Google and Microsoft?
World.content:
Microsoft Outlook and Teams users around the world, including in Europe, were locked out of their emails and meetings this week after a global outage. The disruption has renewed questions about how much the continent relies on a few American firms.

 

“The episode shows once again the downside of depending so heavily on a handful of large US tech companies,” Tommaso Valletti told Euronews Next.

Valletti is Professor of Economics at Imperial College Business School in London, United Kingdom, and was the European Commission’s chief competition economist from 2016 to 2019.

The disruption began on Thursday afternoon European time and hit users in 74 countries and territories, according to the outage tracker Downdetector. In the UK, some doctors' surgeries told patients to phone them with urgent queries.

Microsoft said there was no sign of a cyber attack but has not yet named a root cause. Services were still being gradually restored on Friday. It follows Microsoft 365 outages in January and August.

How dependent is Europe?

Amazon, Microsoft and Google together hold about 70% of the European cloud market, according to Synergy Research Group. European providers account for around 15%, down from about 29% in 2017. The largest of them, Germany’s SAP and Deutsche Telekom, hold just 2% each.

Euronews has previously reported that around 80% of Europe’s digital infrastructure and technology comes from outside the EU.

That sits uneasily with the public. Most EU citizens want European-controlled digital infrastructure, according to the latest Eurobarometer survey. Support is highest in Sweden (94%), Finland (93%) and Denmark (92%).

Brussels wants Europe to buy European

On Wednesday, MEPs presented their draft report on the Commission’s proposed Cloud and AI Development Act. The report calls for public authorities to buy more cloud services from European providers.

“Our critical systems run on someone else’s technology, and someone else can switch it off,” warned Dutch Green MEP Reinier van Lanschot.

Fears of a so-called “kill switch” grew in June, when Anthropic suspended access to its Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models to comply with US export controls. Access was restored on 1 July.

The Commission also wants to triple the EU’s data centre capacity within five to seven years. Bidding for up to seven EU-backed AI “gigafactories” closed on Thursday.

Who could take on the giants?

Europe has no single rival to Microsoft, Amazon or Google. Instead, it has contenders at different layers of the technology stack.

France’s Mistral AI is Europe’s best-known maker of AI models. It was valued at €21 billion after a €3 billion funding round led by Samsung in September.

In cloud computing, STACKIT, owned by the Lidl and Kaufland parent company Schwarz Group, is building an €11 billion AI data centre in Brandenburg, Germany. In April, STACKIT and France’s OVHcloud, Scaleway and Mistral were among the firms that won places on the Commission’s own sovereign cloud contract, worth up to €180 million.

In hardware, Germany’s Infineon is a leading maker of the power chips that run AI data centres. Analysts at this week’s SEMICON Europa trade fair in Munich, Germany, identified power chips as Europe’s strongest way into the AI boom.

Will Europeans switch?

Willingness to pay more for an EU-based provider varies widely. Danes (76%), Swedes and Croatians (both 73%) are the most willing, while Estonians (35%), Bulgarians and Czechs (both 45%) are the least, according to Eurobarometer.

Businesses are cautious too. In a survey by the German digital association Bitkom, 85% of German companies said the country was too dependent on US cloud providers, yet 71% use one. Research firm IDC found that only 4% of European organisations plan to use local providers exclusively.

US firms are also adapting. Amazon Web Services launched its European Sovereign Cloud in Brandenburg in January, run by a separate EU-based company.

Synergy’s chief analyst, John Dinsdale, has told CNBC that European providers will struggle to reverse their loss of market share.

What happens next?

Parliament committees will discuss the proposed Cloud and AI Development Act draft report on 1 December. A committee vote is provisionally scheduled for mid-March 2027, followed by a plenary vote in April.

Microsoft has said it will publish a report on the cause of the outage once services are fully restored.

World.title: Passengers continue to face delays and cancellations after US lifts nationwide ground stop
World.content:
Passengers travelling to and from the United States continue to face delays and cancellations to flights on Saturday morning despite the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) having lifted a nationwide ground stop.

 

The rare order had been issued on Friday following a "telecommunications outage," with all flights halted across the country.

The FAA has since lifted the ground stop and said that some flight departures were resuming.

"Before clearing flights to resume, we thoroughly tested our systems to confirm they were stable and that operations remain reliable," the agency said, while advising travellers to contact airlines for flight updates.

US Transport Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the stoppage on what he called an "incredibly old" air traffic control system and warned that it would take time for normal operations to resume.

"At 8:15 (pm) tonight, eastern time, we've opened up the airspace. Now does that mean every flight is going to fly? Right now, it's going to be slow," he told reporters. "It depends on do we have crews available, do we have pilots and flight attendants available to fly your flight. We're going to try to move as many of those as we can tonight."

"But it's going to take us some time to unwind what's happened," he added.

Travelers wait at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport in DFW Airport, Texas, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.

Flight-tracking site Flightradar24's airport disruption map shows major problems at airports across the US on Saturday morning.

FlightAware, another tracking service, put the number of cancellations to flights to or from the US on Friday at more than 8,860. It said around 2,650 more have been cancelled so far on Saturday.

United Airlines, Delta and American have all said they are resuming flight operations.

"We're focused on operating as many remaining flights as possible this evening while positioning the airline for the strongest possible recovery in the days ahead," American said in a statement late on Friday.

World.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
World.content:
The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US peace envoys asked whether Kyiv would withdraw from its eastern region of ‌Donbas ⁠in exchange ⁠for joining NATO, according to remarks to the media published on Saturday.

The suggestion was made following the latest round of peace talks in Abu Dhabi to bring Russia's nearly 5-year war in Ukraine to a close.

What did Zelenskyy say?

The Ukrainian leader told reporters: "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would ⁠Ukraine ​withdraw from Donbas?'"

Zelenskyy repeated Kyiv's position that it was not willing to cede territory to Russia. But he added that if the country reached a comprehensive deal, including security guarantees, a ‌strong ​and well-funded Ukrainian army and funds to rebuild, he would put the question ​to the public in a referendum.

"That ​is why ⁠I believe NATO is back on the ⁠agenda. ​But you have also heard [Russian President Vladimir] Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation."

Zelenskyy said the prospect of NATO membership in exchange for withdrawing from Donbas has not been raised before.

He also warned about Moscow's plan to change the continent's security architecture, saying it could lead to more conflict.

Putin has demanded that NATO pull back its troops from the Russian border, which European Union leaders have strongly criticized.

"This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations," Zelenskyy added.

"Real security in Europe means the EU and NATO. That's it. There is no other security in Europe."

Europe chooses representatives for Ukraine peace talks To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Europe to play bigger role in peace talks

On Friday, the EU said several European diplomats would take part in future Ukraine peace talks, including Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Poland.

Moscow has long insisted that European states be excluded from the negotiations because they support Ukraine.

Russian forces strike Zaporizhzhia

The comments come as Russia’s Defence Ministry said its ⁠forces ⁠had captured the ​settlement of Tersianka in ​Ukraine’s southeastern ​Zaporizhzhia ‌region, news agency Interfax reported.

Interfax cited the ministry as saying that Russian ​forces had struck Ukrainian energy and ​transport infrastructure used by ⁠the ​military, along with ammunition ​depots and ​drone production ‌and storage sites.

Russia has targeted power stations across Ukraine in waves of ballistic and cruise missile attacks, cutting power and heating to millions of people as temperatures plunge.

Zelenskyy warned that Putin was "betting everything" on this winter's war campaign, which Kyiv insists is aimed at hurting public morale.

World.title: New facilities in Laos and Cambodia: Is China expanding its military presence in Southeast Asia?
World.content:
China has been growing its economic relationships in Southeast Asia. Now new military facilities in Laos and Cambodia are causing smaller countries to worry China's military networks are also expanding.

It's often said that maintaining good relations with your neighbors is essential. So in early November, China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi invited his counterparts from Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand and Myanmar to Beijing.

There the six countries agreed on closer economic and security cooperation.

The visit is just one example of China's growing influence on Southeast Asia. It's not just about trade or infrastructure either, it's also increasingly about military cooperation.

New airbase in Laos

For instance, at the end of September, China and Laos opened a joint military support and training center north of the Laotian capital, Vientiane. Initially Laotian air force pilots are to be trained at the Ban Keun airfield, China has said.

Earlier in 2025 China expanded its footprint at Cambodia's Ream naval base. China uses the facility on the Gulf of Thailand for logistics and training. And while Japanese and Vietnamese ships can visit the port, they're docked at a southern quay and it's unclear if other navies can use the same facilities under the same conditions as China.

"It remains to be seen how this [Ban Keun] will change China's military access to Southeast Asia," says Marco Bünte, a professor of Asian politics at the University Erlangen Nuremberg in Germany.

A satellite image shows construction of Ban Keun airfield in Laos Image: Vantor/REUTERS

In recent years, China has significantly expanded its economic influence in the region.

The China-Laos railway and other infrastructure projects connect Laos more closely with its northern neighbor. Laos is also heavily indebted to China.

Bünte points out that Laos and Cambodia have been close military partners of China for some time and the new facility in Laos can be seen as another step towards deepening cooperation.

If that proves correct, "China would gain strategic depth in mainland Southeast Asia," Bünte explained. "It would also give China better military access to the South China Sea."

Johann Fuhrmann, head of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation's Beijing office, points out that one should distinguish between training Laotian pilots and any potential use of the facilities by Chinese armed forces later.

"China gains influence when it co-designs the training and operation of such facilities over several years," Fuhrmann told DW.



Laos: A country in the grip of the Chinese? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Chinese planes in Laos

But nobody should underestimate China's military positioning, Bünte continued. "China is expanding its military operational capabilities here although I wouldn't speak of military hegemony because China hasn't achieved that yet."

With regard to the Laotian airbase, China says that Laotian pilots will be trained there. But beside military transporters and helicopters, Laos actually only has three light combat aircraft by Russia's Yakovlev works.

According to the aviation media outlet FlightGlobal, four more K-8s, Chinese two-seat intermediate jet trainer and light attack aircrafts, are in service there. Satellite images analyzed by the Reuters news agency in early October show eight K-8s at the base — even thought this doesn't necessarily mean they are stationed there permanently.

Fuhrmann doesn't think anybody should jump to conclusions about this.

"The idea of ​​a Chinese air corridor is more of a future scenario than something that has already been proven," he says.

For example, the runway at Ban Keun is only 2,000 meters (6,562 feet) long, which makes it too short for large Chinese bombers. These usually require 3,000 meters.

A 2022 satellite image shows the Ream naval base in Cambodia Image: picture alliance/AP

The crucial question is what rights China will be granted, Fuhrmann continues: "Will China have to obtain the approval of the respective government for every new use? Or are there longer-term commitments that both sides can invoke, even in times of crisis?"

Surrounding countries are reacting differently to what appears to be China's growing influence in Laos, Cambodia and Myanmar because these countries are already considered closer to China.

Other Southeast Asian nations are hedging, trying to expand their relationship with China without severing ties with the US and also maintaining economic links with other Western nations. China's involvement offers them additional options and Beijing wants to explore those possibilities. That's just pragmatic though, Bünte says of the smaller Asian nations.

"Overall, these states… try to keep as many options open as possible," he notes.

China's gray zone warfare in the Pacific To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

China: 'Not against third parties'

Vietnam and the Philippines are watching developments particularly closely. Both have territorial disputes with China in the South China Sea. But Vietnam also has close historical ties to Laos and trained its own military there.

In early November, the Vietnamese government declared that any military cooperation must serve peace and stability and referred to the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia, commonly known as the ASEAN Treaty. China is not an ASEAN member but has also stated that its activities are not directed against any third parties.

"So far, these are individual steps," Bünte adds. "We would have to wait and see if this leads to a broader military alliance in the years to come."

Fuhrmann says that Western nations should help strengthen the smaller countries in the region and take their interests seriously.

"Ultimately, a counterweight can only be achieved through tangible contributions, not through warnings or lectures from Europe," he says.

This story was originally published in German.

World.title: Germany news: Solar power production approaches record high
World.content:
Skip next section Budget crisis looming if spending is not cut — experts

Leading economics experts have predicted a serious German budget crisis from next year if the issue of spending is not addressed.

Their remarks come as the budget committee of the Bundestag, the lower house of parliament, early on Friday approved a provisional 2027 federal budget after nearly 16 hours of negotiations.

The budget foresees new debt, including loans from special funds, totalling around €210 billion ($231.5 billion).

Spending in the core budget rises to a record €561 billion, while net borrowing climbs to almost €123 billion in the core budget alone.

€200 billion in new borrowing: Germany's not so frugal budget To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"This budget policy cannot be sustained in the long term," Clemens Fuest, president of the Ifo Institute in Munich, told the Sunday edition of Die Welt newspaper, saying spending priorities had to be established

"All other spending should be frozen or, if possible, cut," Fuest said, adding that tax rises would be inevitable if this did not happen.

Jens Boysen-Hogrefe of the Kiel Institute for the World Economy (IfW Kiel) sees things similarly.

"Owing to economic fluctuations and special effects, there may be some breathing room in individual years, but the trend is clearly negative," he said, owing to the fact that the population is aging while interest payments are rising.

"Additional levies are likely even with strong spending discipline," he said.

Ansgar Heveling, the president of the Bundesrechnungshof, the federal audit court that monitors financial management by the government, called on the coalition government to do make more effort to consolidate the budget.

Noting that every third euro spent by the government is financed by borrowing, he said it was clear that it was living beyond its means, and warned that the share of interest spending in the federal budget would double by 2020.

World.title: Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany
World.content:
His life is a reflection of contemporary German history, which Biermann has addressed via his songs and sharp wit. Turning 90, he’s as feisty as ever.

He mocks Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as "political lovers," denounces the "endless fratricidal war" over the Palestinian territories, and repeatedly invokes "Lady Liberty." It is a celebration of the freedom he once so painfully lacked in the former East Germany, and of the freedom people around the world still yearn for.

These themes run throughout Wolf Biermann's new album "Unterm Haar nur Himmel" ("Beneath Hair, Only Sky") released to mark his 90th birthday. The album's title is a characteristically poetic phrase coined by Biermann himself. It evokes the idea that however restrictive the world may become, the human mind and spirit remain free. Beneath the hair lies open sky: a metaphor for inner freedom, independence and imagination.

Biermann remains one of Germany's most influential singer-songwriters, and at 90, he shows little sign of putting down his guitar. Often described as Germany's answer to Bob Dylan, the outspoken troubadour continues to weigh in on the issues shaping the world today.

In his recent song "Moritat von den Liebespaaren" ("Ballad of the Lovers"), he delivers a simple but urgent message: no single person can save the world, yet everyone can help make it a better place. Above all, the song is a call to take responsibility for one's own life rather than remain a bystander.

'Operation Gomorrah' reduced Hamburg to rubble in 1943 and Wolf Biermann grew up — just like these children — amid the ruins Image: dpa/picture alliance

A child caught in the Allied firestorm

This outspokenness was instilled in Biermann early on. When he was born in Hamburg in 1936, Adolf Hitler was already in power. His father was a dockworker, a committed communist, a resistance fighter against the Nazis — and Jewish. Wolf was just three months old when the Gestapo, Hitler's secret police, arrested his father. He initially served time in prison before he was murdered by the Nazis at Auschwitz in early 1943.

Just a few months later, British and American bombers attacked Hamburg, unleashing a devastating firestorm. "Nothing in my life has shaped me more," Biermann has repeatedly said in interviews. When the air raid sirens sounded, his mother took him into an air raid shelter. The house above them was burning.

Yet Biermann says his memories of that time are rooted in a profound sense of trust in life. In an interview with the German magazine Chrismon, he recalled: "I pressed my face into my mother's soft coat so I could breathe. A sense of security in the midst of the end of the world. We stumbled out over the neighboring house and into the open. The firestorm lifted a burning roof into the air. Roaring corrugated metal, smoke everywhere. We searched for a way out. (...) Death was everywhere. 40,000 people died. They had no chance. But I did. My strong mama."

Avenging his father

His mother instilled communist and anti-fascist ideas in him with almost religious fervor. "My mother had only one goal after those dark years," Biermann recalls. "I was supposed to survive so that I could, as she put it rather grandly, one day take revenge for my father's death. I was supposed to build communism."

In 1953, while countless people were fleeing from East Germany, Biermann moved there of his own free will — after all, communism was the official state ideology. He was just 16 at the time. In East Berlin, he studied political economy, mathematics and philosophy. His role models were writers Bertolt Brecht and Heinrich Heine. He began working as an assistant director at the Berliner Ensemble. He also began writing and performing his political songs.

He soon realized that life in East Germany was far from the communist paradise he had imagined and he wrote about this openly in his songs. "The party bosses were torn," Biermann recalls. "They were delighted by this young poet who could play the guitar so beautifully and sing such cheeky songs. They thought they just needed to bring me into line. Even today, I'm amazed that I wound up cast in the role of the heroic dragon slayer."

After 11 years, Biermann was thrilled to perform in front of a large audience in West Germany again in 1976 Image: Sebastian Ahlers/DHM

Exiled from East Germany

In 1965, East Germany's ruling Socialist Unity Party, the SED, imposed a blanket ban on Biermann performing or publishing his work. His East Berlin apartment, which was under constant surveillance, soon became a gathering place for dissidents and critical thinkers.

Yet, to his great surprise, the East German authorities allowed him to travel to Cologne, West Germany in 1976. There, around 7,000 people flocked to see him. For four and a half hours, he strummed and sang, mocking the East German regime. His songs were so popular that bootleg copies found their way back to East Germany.

On November 16, while still on tour in West Germany, Biermann heard the news on his car radio that he had been stripped of his right to continue residing in the German Democratic Republic.
