World.title: Defence Minister: MiG-29s and F-16s will guard Bulgaria’s skies ‘on rotational basis’ in 2027
World.content:
Bulgarian skies will be guarded on a rotational basis by MiG-29s and F-16 fighter jets in 2027, Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov told a November 13 news conference about the defence budget for next year.

Stoyanov did not explain what is meant by rotation, but he said that in 2027, F-16s will only be on duty during the day because they are not certified and prepared for night flights.

He made it clear that the military will continue to rely on the nearly 40-year-old Soviet MiG-29 fighter jets, without it being clear how many of them are still operational, where spare parts will be obtained, and where they will be repaired and tested for safety.

At the same time, Stoyanov spoke of problems surrounding the use of the new US-made F-16 fighter jets. Bulgaria has already acquired eight of them and is waiting for another eight, which will probably arrive in Bulgaria in 2029, a delay from the initial schedule.

The first eight F-16s will also be modified. For example, they must be equipped with the new AN/ALQ-254(V)1 Viper Shield electronic warfare suite.

This is a mandatory electronic warfare package because it is related to the survival of the F-16 against modern radars and electronic threats. Stoyanov said that the US had given an assurance that the Viper Shield systems would be delivered and installed in 2027.

In addition, according to Stoyanov, the already trained Bulgarian pilots are prepared for air-to-air mode, not air-to-ground, that is, they cannot hit ground targets.

The repair of the engines, as well as the repair of maintenance units for the MiG-29 aircraft , is to be ensured.

“There is no way we can continue to fulfill our functional obligations, including our obligations to Nato structures, without the MiG-29 aircraft,” Stoyanov said.

There are also two new projects included in the new budget. They are related to the maintenance of the F-16. One is specifically for the maintenance of the F-16, and the second project is for the acquisition of additional missile armament for the aircraft.

As to when the F-16s can do duty fulltime, Stoyanov said that this could happen when the Viper Shield systems are received. But he added that the necessary pilots must also be available.

The draft budget of the Defence Ministry for 2027 envisages expenditures amounting to 2.23 per cent of gross domestic product.

The total planned finance for defence spending amounts to 3.151 billion euro, which is an increase of 17 per cent compared with 2026.

“The largest increase is in capital expenditures – from 868 million euro this year to over 1.223 billion euro next year,” Stoyanov said. This represents 40.83 per cent of the ministry’s budget budget.

“This is a budget for accelerated modernisation. With Nato’s requirement for a share of capital expenditures above 20 per cent, we exceed 40 per cent,” he said.

Stoyanov said that Bulgaria is working on many projects, both under the SAFE loan mechanism and from the Bulgarian budget.

This includes the acquisition of seven new three-coordinate (3D) radars , a coastal anti-ship missile system from the United States , French Caesar self-propelled artillery systems (SAU), German Iris ground-based air defence systems, 155 mm shells, vehicles, multiple launch rocket systems, drones.

The budget envisages purchasing six firefighting aircraft.

“We are working on the implementation of a project to acquire up to six firefighting aircraft. If the procedure passes without appeals, there is a possibility that the first two will be delivered by the end of 2027, after which the procedure for their absorption will begin,” Stoyanov said.

Stoyanov said that new projects will also be launched with national funds, including modernisation of the avionics of the C-27J Spartan transport aircraft and maintenance of the MiG-29.

It is also planned to acquire new small arms, unmanned aerial systems and space-based platforms; for reconnaissance and surveillance of land and sea targets, strike and FPV drones.

Personnel costs are maintained, with an additional four million euro to compensate for the increase in the minimum wage.

Military personnel will welcome the new year with frozen salaries, due to the freezing for the second time of the automatic increase tied to the average salary. ” If we increase salaries, we have to cut capital expenditures , ” Dimitar Stoyanov said recently.

To fill the shortage in the Bulgarian military, a target of 27.5 million euros from the central budget has been earmarked for the appointment of new military personnel.

At the same time, the resources saved from the dismissal of over 400 employees in the Ministry’s administration this year are being redirected to positions in the military formations.

Stoyanov hopes to recruit at least 1000 new military personnel in 2027, but he made it clear that he is not very optimistic.

The military itself admits that in some units there is even a 25 per cent shortage of personnel, with the situation being the worst in the army.

The Defence Ministry has tried to patch things up with initiatives such as “Be a Soldier” and with changes in the law to introduce so-called voluntary service, but in practice there has been little positive result and the personnel gap remains.

(Archive photo of Bulgarian Air Force Mig-29s, a Spartan and F-16s: Defence Ministry)

World.title: Opposition parties slam PM Radev over ‘reservations’ on Dublin declaration on European security
World.content:
In statements on November 13, opposition parties slammed Bulgarian Prime Minister Roumen Radev over Bulgaria’s position to support “with reservations” France’s initiative on key principles of European security, presented in Dublin.

While some media reports said that Bulgaria was alone among EU countries in not signing the declaration, the website of the President of France showed Bulgaria among the signatories, and the Bulgarian government information service said that the country had supported it, with reservations about the preamble.

Daniel Mitov, an MP for Boiko Borissov’s opposition coalition GERB-UDF and a former foreign minister, said that Bulgaria continues to pursue an unclear foreign policy.

“It was not clear again what he (Radev) signed, what he did not sign and with what reservations,” Mitov said.

“We have Schrödinger’s foreign policy again – we are both there and not there. They never explained what these reservations are,” he said.

“Obviously, Prime Minister Radev is not talking to Bulgarian citizens through such explanations. He is talking to his masters in the Kremlin and giving them a signal that he is actually defending their interests in European formats,” Mitov said.

Borissov said: “Did we sign the declaration or didn’t we? I didn’t understand! German media says we didn’t, the Elysee Palace says we did”.

Ivailo Mirchev, co-leader of opposition coalition Democratic Bulgaria, said: “This is yet another ‘hybrid’ position from Bulgaria—we have joined, yet we haven’t joined”.

“Mr. Radev is clearly afraid of Russia. We ought to treat our partners as a true ally would,” Mirchev said.

Radev, speaking on November 13, said that Bulgaria supported the declaration with reservations only regarding the preamble.

“And we support the declaration in its working part, where we have clearly expressed principles for joint efforts to counter organized crime, terrorism, hybrid attacks, the production and distribution of drugs, and countering illegal immigration,” Radev said.

“But we also take into account that negotiations are currently underway, finally at a high diplomatic level, for a peaceful solution to the war in Ukraine. It is here that we think that the language of common European documents should reflect the dynamics of these political processes, especially when it comes to negotiations,” he said.

“That is why we also expressed reservations about the preamble of the declaration, so that these formulations correspond to these dynamics. So that we can have a broader scope of dialogue and not exclude peaceful solutions in their entirety.”

Radev said that in the earlier versions, there was a formulation about the importance of the negotiations in Abu Dhabi “and that we should support them, then that disappeared, dropped out”.

“We insist on having such a text, to take it into account and not to narrow the field for dialogue and the options for finding a solution. We supported this declaration with reservations only in the preamble. What we have reservations about – these are the formulations in light of the negotiations that have already begun. This is an adopted document by Bulgaria and we welcome it, my reservations to the preamble are recorded.”

Regarding Bulgaria’s position on a new EU loan for Ukraine, Radev said: “Our position is clear – we support all efforts for peace”.

“I do not accept the imposition of the position for peace from a position of force, because we saw a year and a half ago, when I stated it, that this will only lead to more victims, more destruction and an even greater escalation of the conflict, which is already a risk not only for Europe, but for the entire world,” he said .

“We must take into account that Bulgaria, unlike other EU member states, is the country with the largest historical community in Ukraine. And we are deeply concerned by the fact that Bulgarians continue to die in this war every day,” Radev said.

“And that is why we want peace to be restored as quickly as possible. The task of our government is to help our compatriots in Ukraine live in peace as soon as possible, but also to have access to education, healthcare, electricity, and heating during this transitional period. And this will not be solved by investing in military means.”

Radev again referred to Bulgaria being in an excessive deficit procedure, as he has before when speaking about assistance for Ukraine.

“We are in an excessive deficit procedure. We have problems with the reserves in the state. And we have no way in this situation to provide financial resources, but in no case do we hinder the decisions of other member states,” he said.

“Whoever decides to help and invest financial resources in whatever they decide. So we are not blocking anyone in this situation,” Radev said.

“We are ready to talk about mechanisms that will guarantee that these funds will not go to weapons, but to humanitarian activities, to support with electricity, to medical activities, and this is very important for us – we want to see mechanisms that will target these funds, if we invest such as a guarantor, to go specifically to our community. It is compactly expressed in several regions of Ukraine,” he said.

(Photo: government.bg)

World.title: War of words follows consumer watchdog action against retail chains in Bulgaria
World.content:
A war of words lasting days has followed action by Bulgaria’s consumer protection body against retail chains in Bulgaria, with the row inevitably also attracting political comments.

As The Sofia Globe reported on November 9, Bulgaria’s Consumer Protection Commission (CPC) said that it had fined supermarket chain Kaufland Bulgaria 75.7 million euro, citing “unfair trade practices towards Bulgarian food producers”.

The regulator announced three violations against suppliers: pressure to reduce delivery prices, unfair deduction of fees for services, and unjustified delay in price increase negotiations. The decision is subject to appeal in court.

The chain rejects the accusations, claims that the total added value they generate for the state is almost 14 billion euro and it is preparing for a legal battle.

Mihail Petrov, CEO of Kaufland Bulgaria: “And if Kaufland goes on a bobsled ride down, then the bankruptcy of Corpbank will seem like a spring breeze to them. Kaufland has a lot of loans, a lot of suppliers, it has 8,800 employees and stop practicing on it. I can’t wait to go to court and turn the CPC’s act into dust”.

The retail chain’s director’s warnings about a possible outflow of investments prompted a sharp response from Economy Minister Alexander Pulev, who described Petrov’s tone as arrogant and said that the government would not give in to such warnings.

“We are not at war with retail chains, we are at war with unfair trade practices,” Pulev said.

The FMCG (Fast Moving Consumer Goods) market is quite profitable, quite liquid, even if there is an outflow in the market position of a chain, this vacuum will be filled literally within a few weeks by their competitors,” he said.

“Before threatening the Bulgarian state, let this gentleman open the statistics and look at the fact that literally the latest data for this year show a 100 per cent growth in foreign direct investment in the country, so I am calm, I have no reason for any concern about this type of arrogance,” Pulev said.

On Facebook, Prime Minister Roumen Radev’s Progressive Bulgaria ruling party said: “No matter how big you are, you are not above the law.

“When he (Petov) makes an analogy with CorpBank, the Kaufland manager confuses the law with lawlessness,” Progressive Bulgaria said.

“No one is stronger than the state when it applies the law to protect the rights of its citizens. Such declarations only confirm the correctness of the control bodies. Instead of arguments, we hear threats,” the ruling party said.

The Confederation of Independent Trade Unions in Bulgaria (CITUB) also expressed serious concern about the public statements by the management of Kaufland Bulgaria .

CITUB said that it does dispute the company’s right to defend its interests through legal means, but it is unacceptable for the jobs and fate of employees to be used as an argument to exert pressure on state institutions.

“Every company has the right to defend its interests in court. At the same time, CITUB considers it unacceptable for the jobs and fate of workers to be used as an argument for putting pressure on state institutions in connection with the exercise of their legal powers,” the trade union organisation said.

Ivailo Mirchev, an MP for opposition coalition Democratic Bulgaria, said that Petrov’s statement was arrogant and unacceptable.

Instead of scaring with catastrophic scenarios, the management of Kaufland should think about whether it has always been fair to Bulgarian producers over the years and whether it has had unacceptable commercial practices, Mirchev said.

Milena Dragiyska, chief executive of Lidl Bulgaria – a Lidl shop in Vidin was shut down temporarily earlier this week by the Bulgarian Food Safety Agency over alleged violations – described to the media how the pressure was affecting the daily work in the shops.

Dragiyska said there have been cases where seven, eight or nine inspectors have arrived at employees who are on their own shift.

She alleged that inspectors had apologised to staff, explaining that they were ordered to find grounds for a sanction.

“Actually, the big question is what is the goal? That is not clear to us,” Dragiyska said.

She warned that the consequences of this pressure could affect thousands of jobs and Bulgarian producers who rely on the chains for the sale of their goods. According to her, Lidl alone works with over 300 Bulgarian producers, and the volume of joint work is growing.

Dragiyska insisted that the conversation with the state focus on irrigation, labour, financing and the competitiveness of Bulgarian production.

Bulgarian food producers and processors have said that state pressure on large retail chains is also threatening their own production.

Zhivka Grozdeva from the Association of Fruit Growers in Bulgaria believes that the voice of producers who have been working successfully with the chains for years remains silenced in the public conversation.

At a conference of the Association for Modern Trade – an association of which most major retailers in Bulgaria are members – Grozdeva said that large retailers provide a market for significant quantities of Bulgarian fruits and vegetables.

” Without them, part of the production would remain unsold or even unpicked ,” said Grozdeva, who is also a fruit producer.

She said that no one is obliged to work with chains if they prefer another option.

Asked to comment on the average markups on Bulgarian fruit, she estimated that they amount to about 10 per cent-15 per cent, unlike small shops, where, according to her, it reaches 50 per cent.

Grozdeva described the relationship with the chains as a direct negotiation process: the manufacturer sends an offer, the retailer responds, and both parties specify the terms and deliveries.

According to her, the main obstacles to Bulgarian production lie elsewhere – in insecure access to water for irrigation, as irrigation systems cover 1/7 of the country’s territory, the shortage of workers, and the growing administrative burden.

“They increase costs and make it difficult to compete with producers from other countries,” Grozdeva said.

“I see a partner in the large chains,” Vladislav Mihaylov from the National Association of Dairy Processors said during the Association for Modern Trade conference.

Mihaylov described the pressure on foreign chains in recent weeks as an “undeclared war”.

“Nobody wins from any war. Neither the state nor the consumers. We, the producers, are between a rock and a hard place,” Mihaylov said.

Nikolai Vulkavnov, executive director of the Association of Modern Trade, said: “Progress is not measured solely by the price of cheese in the shop”.

He said that constant changes in rules, unpredictable enforcement and huge sanctions could lead to investments being frozen or withdrawn, with consequences for jobs and incomes.

“There will be no new jobs, existing ones may be cut, salaries may fall,” Vulkanov said.

On November 13, GERB leader Boiko Borissov sharply criticised Kaufland Bulgaria’s Petrov’s statement.

Borissov described Petrov’s words as absolutely unacceptable: “They will certainly fire him and all this has to happen, because no one will like such a statement, no one will allow it”.

The GERB leader said that he was wondering whether the government wanted to take Bulgaria back to the time of the communist-era state-owned shops.

Borissov said that he suspects that those close to the government are interested in the properties of Kaufland and other large retail chains.

“I guess because communists never do anything for their own sake, and the best properties in big cities are in these chains,” Borissov said.

In my opinion, one of Radev’s oligarchs has looked around in the chains and now they will do everything possible to expel them. They are worth chasing, I emphasise, with such behaviour, but they do nothing for their own sake,” he said.

(Photo: Bartosz Wacawski/ freeimages.com)

World.title: Bulgaria supported ‘with reservations’ declaration in Dublin on European security
World.content:
Bulgaria has supported with reservations the French initiative on key principles of European security, presented at the Ninth Summit of the European Political Community in Dublin, the government government information service said on November 13.

Radev expressed written reservations to the preamble of the declaration, requesting that the political messages be adapted to the current stage of the peace negotiations in Ukraine, the statement said.

The statement followed media reports that Bulgaria was alone among European Union member states to not have signed the declaration.

Bulgaria supports the achievement of a just and lasting peace in Ukraine through negotiations, the new round of talks in Abu Dhabi with the mediation of the United States is an important step in this direction, according to the statement.

“European positions must support this process, and the language of the common documents must reflect the dynamics of the processes and expectations from the peace negotiations,” it said.

The preamble of the document speaks of “the unprovoked full-scale Russian aggression against Ukraine and the growing threats to the stability of Europe”.

It also says that the signatories “reaffirm their firm support for the independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders”.

They emphasise that Russia’s hybrid campaigns and attempts to undermine support for Ukraine will only strengthen their commitment to Ukraine and their resolve.

The signatories recall that the path to peace in Ukraine must be decided together with Ukraine and that any issue affecting European security must be resolved together with Europeans.

It is emphasised that Ukraine’s security is an integral part of Euro-Atlantic security and that the future development of European strategic stability will be conditioned by the end of the war in Ukraine.

This is the full text of the declaration, as posted on the website of the President of France:

Committed to peace and upholding international law, and in the face of unprovoked full-scale Russian aggression against Ukraine and growing threats to Europe stability, the signatory states, gathered for the 9th Summit of the European Political Community in Dublin on the 12th of November 2026, consider strengthening European security and defending their security interests as their common objective.

The signatory states reiterate their firm support for the independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognised borders

They underline the necessity to provide robust and credible security guarantees to Ukraine and reiterate, for those concerned, their intention to do so, in order to prevent the recurrence of aggression in Europe in the future.

They underline that Russia’s hybrid campaigns and attempts to undermine support to Ukraine will only strengthen their commitment to Ukraine and their resolve.

The signatory states recall that the path to peace in Ukraine should be decided with Ukraine and that any matter affecting European security should be decided with the Europeans.

They consider that the following key principles of European security can contribute to provide a path to a just and lasting peace for Ukraine, which will be of utmost importance for stability in Europe

They emphasize that Ukraine’s security is an integral part of Euro-Atlantic security and that future developments in European strategic stability will be conditional upon the conclusion of the war in Ukraine.

I. General Principles

The signatory states reaffirm the following general principles related to European security :

International law and the Charter of the United Nations are the cornerstone of this Declaration. In addition, the signatory states reaffirm the rules and principles upon which European security is and must remain founded, notably where applicable to the relevant signatory states, the North Atlantic Treaty (1949), the Statute of the Council of Europe (1949), the Treaty on the European Union and the Treaty on the functioning of the European Union (1950, 1957, 1986, 1992 and sq.), the Helsinki Final Act (1975), the Charter of Paris for a New Europe (1990), the Agreement on the European Economic Area (1992), and the Istanbul Charter for Security in Europe (1999). Common objectives contained in this Declaration are rooted in these fundamental documents and the signatories which are parties to them aim to ensure their effective implementation In this regard, the signatory states underline the importance of the following principles, which form the foundations of peace and stability on the European continent : respect for the sovereign equality of states and the rights inherent in sovereignty, such as the territorial integrity, the inviolability of borders, non-interference in domestic affairs, and the right of states to freely determine their relations with other states, and to choose whether or not to participate in treaties, alliances, or international organizations ; the refraining from the threat of or the use of force, including irresponsible nuclear rhetoric and coercion, and the peaceful settlement of disputes, in accordance with international law and good neighbourly relations ; the right to individual or collective self-defence in the event of an armed attack ; and the respect for the international law, including the international law of the sea as reflected by UNCLOS. The signatory states recognise that European states bear a primary responsibility and are assuming greater responsibility for the security of Europe, which will also contribute positively to global and transatlantic security. The signatory states reaffirm their commitment to human rights, and fundamental freedoms for all, without distinction of any kind, including on the grounds of race, sex, language, or religion, including in the digital realm, as well as the right of all nations to freely determine their political status, in accordance with international law. Democracy, rule of law, human rights and respect of the humanitarian international law are essential elements of comprehensive security and contribute to resilient societies capable of resisting both internal and external pressures. Enhanced participatory democracy, transparency and enabling civic space, including media freedom and freedom of expression, are indispensable safeguards of democratic resilience and long-term security. International law also applies to the global commons we share. Free, safe, autonomous and unhindered access to these spaces must be ensured within the limits of international law, in the air, on the seas, in outer space and in cyberspace. This declaration and the associated common objectives are in line with international mechanisms and the missions of existing multilateral organizations and forums in Europe (NATO, EU, OSCE, Council of Europe). Signatories who are members of NATO reaffirm that NATO is the foundation of their collective security and that the Alliance remains the cornerstone of their collective defence. They recall their ironclad commitment to collective defence under Article 5 of the Washington Treaty. They reaffirm their unwavering commitment to the transatlantic bond and to the Euro-Atlantic security. They recall their determination to build a stronger Europe in a stronger NATO, working together with the United States and Canada which continue to play an essential role in NATO and assuming greater responsibilities for the Alliance’s collective defence. Signatories who are members of the European Union reaffirm their commitment to a stronger and more capable European Union that is better equipped to act and deal autonomously with immediate and future challenges and threats with a 360° approach, while recognizing the challenge and threats on the Eastern Flank. Enlargement of the European Union, anchored in a merit-based process and as a geostrategic investment in peace, security, stability and prosperity, also contributes – together with the European Neighbourhood Policy – to the security of the continent. In this global context, the security of the continent depends on strengthening both national and collective defence capabilities in the appropriate forums to address threats with a 360° approach, with the aim of deterring any aggressive actions and being able to defend against them. It also relies on strengthening the resilience and robustness of our democracies, as well as human rights and rule of law. International cooperation, to complement and deepen European and transatlantic frameworks, should always be pursued with a 360° approach. Diversifying partnerships with countries that are committed to upholding the principles of international law and the UN Charter, and that offer balanced and mutually beneficial relationships under the principle of good neighbourly relationships contributes to security and stability in Europe and to address shared challenges and advance common interests.

II. Common objectives

With the aim of strengthening security in Europe, the signatory states support the following common objectives in accordance with their respective international commitments and constitutional laws :

Security – the signatory states will uphold security, peace and stability in Europe in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations and their respective international commitments, including through bilateral agreements between them and for the states concerned by further strengthening the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation and the European Union, which are cornerstones for our security. National security and Defence efforts – in accordance with their respective international commitments, security and defence policies and constitutional obligations, the signatory states reaffirm their commitments to strengthening their capabilities in order to respond to their legitimate security needs, enhance their security and ensure the defence of Europe. To this end, and according to their respective commitments, they will make the most effective use of their resources and continue to develop cooperation among themselves and with relevant organizations, as each of them deems appropriate. Collective resilience – in the face of destabilizing actions conducted below the threshold of armed attack, including through cyber and hybrid activities and coercion, and the expansion of conflict into new areas, the signatory states will work in order to develop the tools necessary to prevent, deter and respond to these challenges, to strengthen the protection of their critical infrastructure, to enhance their resilience, and to cooperate on a voluntary basis to improve the detection and attribution of these attacks, with the aim of discouraging the threats and providing a coordinated response and holding to account those responsible. Risk management and reduction– the signatory states support discussions on further risk management and reduction mechanisms that contribute to stability in Europe, once the conditions are met and peace is restored in Europe. This could address particular risks, be it military or coming from actions conducted below the threshold of armed aggression, aiming at ensuring the stability of the entire continent. Operational Planning – the signatory states will continue to strengthen their collective working practices and their joint operational capabilities for the defence and security of Europe, notably through NATO for those being members of it, as well through other cooperation mechanisms and inclusive coalitions. Industrial cooperation – the concerned signatory states will continue to strengthen their defence industrial production capacity and cooperation across Europe to develop resilient, secure and more independent supply chains and infrastructure for their defence equipment, without prejudice to cooperation with trusted partners. They will promote, as appropriate, cooperation projects between all European actors and foster a competitive European defence equipment market across Europe. They will actively work to create the necessary conditions to mobilize private capital, and support the growth of European defence companies Strategic Dialogues – the signatory states will continue deepening their exchanges and dialogues on strategic issues related to European security, complementing and benefiting from existing collective security frameworks for those participating in them and bilateral arrangements. Democratic integrity – Human rights, rule of law and democratic systems, upon which European societies are fundamentally based, and must be protected and strengthened, to ensure their integrity and resilience in the face of growing deliberate campaigns aimed at undermining those values, including Foreign Information Manipulation and Interferences (FIMI). The signatory states will continue to promote solidarity, cooperation, and the use of the necessary mechanisms and institutions to achieve this goal. Fight against terrorism – the signatory states reaffirm their commitments in the fight against terrorism. In this framework, they condemn terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including state-sponsored terrorism in the strongest possible terms and will continue their cooperation to respond collectively to this threat, in accordance with international law. Response to illicit drug and human-trafficking and migrant-smuggling as well as organised crime networks in Europe – the signatory states reaffirm that illicit drug and human-trafficking as well as organized crimes networks are a major threat to the security, safety and health of the citizens in Europe. They remain committed to fighting illicit drug and human-trafficking and organised crime networks in accordance with international law with the strongest determination and to safeguard the integrity of European societies. Security of supply – the signatory states will continue to work towards the reduction of their dependencies as well as regarding supply chains for critical components or materials. By diversifying and setting up new trade partnerships, they will enable Europe to better respond to the challenges it faces. Protection of global commons – the signatory states will contribute to the protection and security of global commons, ensuring, within the limits of international law, safe, autonomous and unhindered access to these areas, and taking greater responsibility when European interests are involved. In accordance with international law, the protection of freedom of navigation on international waterways, in particular, requires upholding the high seas as a space of freedom, cooperation, and law. These same principles apply, as appropriate, to other shared global commons. Contribution of Europe to Global food security – building on the principles of protecting global commons, the signatory states reaffirm the necessity of the freedom of navigation and of the safety of commercial shipping, notably in the Black Sea, and that the uninterrupted functioning of all maritime routes is essential for global food security.

The above is without prejudice to the specific character of the security and defence policy and interests of the signatory states, and their respective constitutional laws and international commitments.

The Signatory States :

Republic of Albania, Principality of Andorra, Republic of Austria, Kingdom of Belgium, Republic of Bulgaria, Republic of Croatia, Republic of Cyprus, Czech Republic, Kingdom of Denmark, Republic of Estonia, Republic of Finland, French Republic, Georgia, Federal Republic of Germany, Hellenic Republic, Hungary, Republic of Iceland, Ireland, Italian Republic, Republic of Latvia, Principality of Liechtenstein, Republic of Lithuania, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, Republic of Malta, Republic of Moldova, Principality of Monaco, Montenegro, Kingdom of the Netherlands, Republic of North Macedonia, Kingdom of Norway, Republic of Poland, Portuguese Republic, Romania, Republic of San Marino, Slovak Republic, Republic of Slovenia, Kingdom of Spain, Kingdom of Sweden, Ukraine, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

World.title: November 15 is the statutory deadline to fit vehicles with tyres suitable for winter conditions
World.content:
From November 15 to March 1, motor vehicles in Bulgaria must by law be fitted with tyres suitable for winter conditions.

According to the law, approved by Bulgaria’s Parliament in 2016, cars must have tyres designed for winter conditions or that have a tread depth of no less than or equal to four millimetres, the Interior Ministry said.

The Road Traffic Act allows the use of all-season or even summer tyres if they meet the grip requirement, but experts strongly recommend winter tyres for better safety in cold weather.

The traditional Interior Ministry “Winter” campaign, which aims to increase drivers’ attention to preparing their cars for the upcoming winter season, started on November 1.

(Photo: Clive Leviev-Sawyer)

World.title: Advent Zagreb 2026: Festive Cheer, Cultural Highlights, and a Packed Calendar
World.content:
November the 14th, 2026 – It’s that time of year again! Advent Zagreb 2026 is just around the corner, promising a programme packed with festive cheer and a very full calendar.

The most wonderful time of the year is knocking at the door. Advent in Zagreb, which is considered one of the best in Europe, starts on the 28th of November and lasts until the 7th of January.

The multi-award-winning Advent Zagreb once again brings a rich cultural, entertainment and food programme, which, along with New Year’s events, will take place from the 28th of November 2026 to the 7th of January 2027. Organised by the City of Zagreb, the Zagreb Tourist Board (TZGZ) and numerous institutional and private partners, the programme will officially kick off with the traditional lighting of the first Advent candle on Ban Jelačić Square, after which the other locations will open.

zagreb’s progression as a festive city delight

Boska i Kreso/TZGZ

Director of TZGZ, Martina Bienenfeld, stated that “Advent Zagreb has grown into one of the most recognisable Advent events in Europe, and this year’s edition brings new cultural content and more strongly connects city locations into a unique holiday experience. We pay special attention to culture and programmes for children and families. Among this year’s novelties intended for the youngest, I’d highlight LumiLicious on Mažuranac, which starts on the 6th of December, the feast of St Nicholas. Novelties are also The Magic Within on Marulić Square and the festive decoration of the Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts, whose ceremonial openings are planned for the 18th of December. Together with the new arrangement of the space in front of the Croatian National Theatre, these contents will connect the locations of the Green Horseshoe into a unique Advent promenade. In this way we enrich the Advent offer and open new possibilities for exploring the city, while at the same time putting Zagreb’s historical spaces, architecture and cultural heritage in the foreground.

The international recognisability of Advent Zagreb is also confirmed by this year’s awards and recommendations from world media. We are particularly pleased that Zagreb has been declared the best European destination for a Christmas city break in the selection of the European Best Destinations organisation, while the prestigious Time Out ranked it first on its list of the best European destinations for a winter city break in 2026, highlighting its attractiveness for family travel. Such recognitions have significant promotional value because they strengthen Zagreb’s international visibility, encourage interest in coming and contribute to its positioning on key source markets. In this context we continue with intensive promotional activities on 17 international markets, including targeted campaigns at stations of the London Underground and the Milan metro, as well as long-standing cooperation with Croatia Airlines and HŽ Passenger Transport.

Julien Duval/TZGZ

I believe that Advent Zagreb will once again achieve good tourist results this year and further strengthen Zagreb’s position as an attractive year-round destination. At the same time, we do not measure its success exclusively by tourist indicators, but also by the quality of the experience it provides to visitors and our fellow citizens. Precisely in this balance between tourist attractiveness and value for the local community we see the foundation of its long-term development and sustainability.”

The entire programme, detailed schedules of all events and current information can be found here, and we’ll also bring you descriptions of each below.

what’s on this festive season for europe’s best advent?

Julien Duval/TZGZ

What we’ve been waiting for all year finally starts on the last weekend of November. Zagreb has won a new title – it is the best Christmas city-break destination 2026 according to European Best Destinations. Along with well-known attractions such as the Ice Park, Advent on Zrinjevac, Fuliranje and numerous other events, there are also novelties for the youngest on Mažuranac, and the entire Upper Town, as well as the Green Horseshoe of the Lower Town, become a unique Advent promenade. Run with Santa Claus, dance or skate in the parks, sing on the tram or just stop and enjoy.

if you’re the musical type…

Samir Ceric Kovacevic/TZGZ

Advent concerts of the Zagreb Soloists

Museum of the City of Zagreb, on the 3rd, 6th, 10th and 13th of December at 18:00

The Zagreb Soloists continue the tradition of Advent concerts at the Museum of the City of Zagreb. At each of the four concerts the Zagreb Soloists will be joined by a young musician.

Advent concerts of the Zagreb Chamber Orchestra

Church of St Joseph, Journalists’ House

Advent concerts of the Zagreb Chamber Orchestra in the city’s historical spaces. The Church of St Joseph is the location of the first concert on the 29th of November, followed by three more at the Journalists’ House on the 5th 13th and 19th of December with performances by renowned Croatian and international soloists.

Advent concerts of the Chamber Choir “Ivan Filipović” – Zagreb Voices

Church of St John the Baptist 29 Nov, Basilica of St Anthony of Padua on the 13th of December, the Church of St Francis of Assisi on the 29th of December

Concerts of the Chamber Choir “Ivan Filipović” – Zagreb Voices bring a combination of classical music, choral compositions and Croatian traditional Advent and Christmas songs. Contemporary choral arrangements of Croatian musical heritage are performed for the first time.

Music in St Mark’s Church

St Mark’s Church, on the 13th 20th and 24th of December (Midnight Mass)

Advent tradition, performances of classical and sacred music that echo within the historical walls of the Church of St Mark. Admission is free.

Advent with the Opera of the Croatian National Theatre in Zagreb

Republic of Croatia Square, balcony of the CNT, the 5th of December at 17:30 and the 7th of December at 19:00

From the balcony of the Zagreb CNT, young soloists accompanied by piano perform opera and Advent compositions. Two half-hour concerts for residents and guests alike will fill the space in front of the theatre with holiday melodies.

seasonal music

Boska i Kreso/TZGZ

From Christmas balconies to Zagreb

Balcony at the Stone Gate, balcony at Tkalčićeva 33, balcony of the CNT



Christmas melodies from Zagreb balconies performed by the six-member brass ensemble Ad gloriam brass. A unique musical experience of European flair and classical music, film themes and Christmas songs.

Festival of Advent and Christmas songs

Society of University Teachers and Other Scientists, Greek Catholic Co-Cathedral of Sts Cyril and Methodius, Church of St Peter the Apostle, Church of St Mark, Church of St Blaise, Stone Gate, terrace of Cravaticum – the Tie Museum



The Festival of Advent and Christmas songs brings festive concerts of Advent-Christmas music of different genres and eras. From classical to klapa and holiday pop songs at the 11th edition of the festival at six city locations. A children’s concert will also be held as part of the festival.

Zagreb Advent postcards

Oktogon, Neboder, Baković Sisters Passage



The vocal quartet Vox in the heart of Zagreb performs Advent compositions from Croatian and world musical heritage. With pop-up concerts, short performances without prior announcement, they will surprise random passers-by with the musical magic of Advent.

Advent under the lantern

Lotrščak Tower



Join the lamp-lighter and singers every Wednesday, Thursday and Friday until Christmas Eve at Lotrščak Tower. Light the gas lamps while singing kolende at Advent under the lantern in the Upper Town.

Advent symphony of the city

Radićeva – Tomićeva – Stone Gate – Bloody Bridge – Mažuranić Square



An Advent walk through Zagreb accompanied by Christmas songs performed by the Musical-Artistic Atelier Kralj. The Advent symphony of the city from 19:00 to 20:30 at various locations in the heart of Zagreb.

Musical control – Zagreb promenade

Ljubljanica depot, Zrinjevac Park



The Musical Control of the Zagreb ZET Orchestra on Saturday morning will surprise passengers at selected locations in the city. The ride starts at 10:00 from Ljubljanica and ends in Zrinjevac Park.

‘Flash mob’ on the tram

Zagreb trams



Surprise flash-mob concerts on Zagreb trams are a Christmas tradition. Sing along with the choir during the ride through the Lower Town.

single day events

Samir Ceric Kovacevic/TZGZ

Advent Run

Zagreb streets, 6th of December at 12:00



Zagreb Advent Run, a costume race for the whole family through the city, again has a humanitarian character this year. It is run as part of the Croatian national campaign for early detection of high cholesterol and blood pressure. You can choose to run five or ten kilometres.

Broadcast of the ballet The Nutcracker

Republic of Croatia Square, in front of the CNT, on the 19th of December 2026 at 18:00



Broadcast of the most performed classical ballet in the world in front of the Croatian National Theatre on 19 December from 18:00. The beloved Nutcracker in the ambitious version of the famous Russian ballet dancer Rudolf Nureyev.

Choirs on Christmas Eve – Midday Advent Melodies

Ban Josip Jelačić Square, 24th of December at 11:00



This year again on Ban Jelačić Square Zagreb choirs bring Christmas magic with a joint performance of fairy-tale evergreens. Enjoy the harmonious polyphony of the choirs accompanied by guitar and piano.

workshops and activities

Ernest Mazarekic/TZGZ

Christmas story at the Ethnographic Museum

Mažuranić Square 14



The Christmas programme at the Ethnographic Museum brings an exhibition of Pannonian nativity scenes from Burgenland and an exhibition dedicated to 30 years of exhibiting Croatian Christmas nativity scenes in Rome and the Vatican. You can also make your own Christmas nativity scenes from cornhusks and wool.

Advent at the Museum of the City of Zagreb

Opatička 20



The Advent programme of the Museum of the City of Zagreb brings an exhibition of Advent cards and objects “Christmas Story”, tours “Forgotten Holidays” and creative workshops for making Advent wreaths. For children there are theatre performances on the occasion of the feast of St Nicholas, and for quiz lovers a special edition of KviZG.

Advent at the Croatian Natural History Museum

Demetrova 1



The Croatian Natural History Museum uniquely connects science, art, music and entertainment. There are lectures and projections about the secrets of the universe, interactive scientific and creative workshops, as well as theatre performances and Advent concerts in the museum atrium.

Advent in the Crafts Passage

Ilica 49



A Christmas fairy tale at the Croatian Crafts Matrix in Ilica. There are hand-made souvenirs and appropriate workshops by the greatest masters. All accompanied by concerts of Christmas songs on the gallery of the Croatian Crafts Matrix.

for the kids

Samir Ceric Kovacevic/TZGZ

Teatrino klincolino

Antun, Ivan and Vladimir Mažuranić Square



The children’s puppet theatre at this year’s Advent performs more than thirty performances of popular and lesser-known children’s stories. Creative puppets perform on Mažuranić Square.

Living Christmas nativity scene

Opatovina Park, 19th to the 23rd of December, 26th to the 30th of December, 1st and the 6th of January

Traditional staging of the living nativity scene at Opatovina. Young people from the Cenacolo Community designed the entire performance themselves and perform it with the help of parents and friends. Performances are held at 16:00, 17:00 and 19:00.

The Magic Within

Marko Marulić Square



The projection runs from the 18th of December to the 1st of January on the building of the Croatian State Archives, which turns into a stylised Christmas house. Together with the neighbouring buildings of FKIT and PMF it will create a visual whole of recognisable architecture.

Very Merry Square

Ban Josip Jelačić Square



The Christmas tree on Ban Jelačić Square is the central symbol of the Christmas holidays in the city. Surrounded by snow-covered pines and sparkling lights, the Square becomes a real winter fairy tale with Manduševac as the most beautiful Advent wreath.

LumiLicious

Antun, Ivan and Vladimir Mažuranić Square from the 6th of December to the 1st of January



Mažuranac comes alive with Christmas magic. Walk through snowy pine forests and discover a world of imagination among oversized Christmas decorations. There are LUMI and LICI, an interactive audiovisual installation that invites children to bring two cute digital characters to life.

HNK – Layers of Christmas

Republic of Croatia Square



This Advent the building of the Croatian National Theatre will be wrapped in Christmas attire. Republic of Croatia Square becomes a glowing forest which is absolutely perfect for photos.

Let It Glow

Flower Square (Cvjetni trg)

The popular Flower Square, through lavish decorations, sparkling installations and interactive elements, combines the charm of old Zagreb with a modern Christmas atmosphere. A special photo point is the perfect place for unforgettable holiday moments.

Advent Open House Zagreb

9th and and the 16th of December

Advent Open House Zagreb opens the doors of normally inaccessible, most attractive architectural works in the city centre with expert guidance in Croatian and English. The festival encourages reflection on the values of the city. Click here to register.

Bells in the Oktogon

Oktogon, from the 13th to the 29th of December

In Zagreb’s Oktogon you will find a sound installation of 24 bells that every full hour perform an atmospheric version of the composition “Imagine”.

Polar Worlds

Grič Tunnel

A true polar dream in the Grič Tunnel – new scenes inspired by glaciers and crystal formations that transform it into an imaginary landscape of polar worlds. Experience the Grič Tunnel in a new edition.

Moon Garden

King Béla IV Park

Step into the magical Moon Garden in King Béla IV Park. Make a special wish on the Moon with an unforgettable view of the city.

Winter Nocturne

Grič Park, Strossmayer Promenade

Winter Nocturne brings a winter atmosphere to Grič Park, inspired by the stars and Chopin’s nocturnes. The benches are free throughout Advent.

Bells and Bell Towers of Croatia: Symphony of Peace and Togetherness

Palace of the Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts (HAZU), Nikola Šubić Zrinski Square 11

Saša Šekoranja presents drawings and video installations of bell towers from all over Croatia in the HAZU Palace. Their sounds create a unique Advent symphony of togetherness, love and holiday joy.

ADVENT IN HOTELS

Julien Duval/TZGZ

Hilton Hotels

Hilton Hotels: DoubleTree, Garden Inn, Canopy



Festive decorations, a warm atmosphere, signature cocktails and special offers at Hilton Hotels Zagreb.

Hotel Jägerhorn

Ilica 14



A small but idyllic Advent is hidden in the passage of Hotel Jägerhorn, the oldest in the city.

Advent Bachata Congress

Hotel Diplomat, Zrinjevac



An international dance congress from the 11th to the 14th of December gathers hundreds of bachata and salsa dancers from all over the world. Free dance programme on Zrinjevac on the 13th of December from 16:00 to 19:00.

Fuliranje

Hotel Esplanade



The Fuliranje – Christmas Station is a new edition of the popular Zagreb Advent project. The Oleander terrace of Hotel Esplanade turns into a unique Christmas destination. There is an impressive covered and heated greenhouse, a Christmas living room that in the evening turns into a large Christmas Disco Club.

LOCATIONS IN THE CITY CENTRE

Julien Duval/TZGZ

EU Advent

European Square



EU Advent on European Square brings a new theme – The City that Loves. Through performances by female vocalists, DJ programmes and stand-up evenings, European Square becomes a place of meetings, music, laughter, tastes and togetherness.

Baš Naš Vremeplov

Ban Josip Jelačić Square

January, Ban Josip Jelačić Square will beecome a place where the past and the present meet until January the 7th, 2027. Baš Naš Vremeplov (Our Time Machine) invites all generations to gather in the very heart of Zagreb.

Advent on Zrinjevac

Zrinjevac Park



Thousands of sparkling lights, music from the pavilion, the scents of winter delicacies and charming Advent houses – Zrinjevac once again opens the doors to the most beautiful holiday moments! This year it becomes a magical poetry promenade. Verses of Croatian poets about love, Christmas and Zagreb come to life among the century-old plane trees.

Fuliranje

Strossmayer Square



Until the 7th of January, Fuliranje on Josip Juraj Strossmayer Square brings an open-air winter living room. Creative workshops, children’s and family programmes, musical performances, theatrical and educational content, as well as top gastronomic offerings.

Ice Park

King Tomislav Square



In the heart of Zagreb, against the magnificent backdrop of the Art Pavilion and the glow of thousands of lights, the Ice Park once again becomes a favourite place for winter gatherings. From the first steps on the ice to evening get-togethers with music and favourite winter delicacies. The most beautiful outdoor winter stage is once again adorned by the Nutcracker on Ice performance.

Caffe de Matoš – Advent in the Upper Town

Strossmayer Promenade and Gradec Plateau



On Strossmayer Promenade, Caffe de Matoš offers a daily musical programme of young bands in cooperation with the Music House. A photo point with the best view of Zagreb. On the nearby Gradec Plateau, Caffe de Matoš revives the spirit of old Zagreb in a special holiday edition. Thousands of lanterns, red houses and a magical forest, with an unforgettable view of illuminated Zagreb.

The Great ZbiGatsby on Stross

Strossmayer Promenade – west



On Zagreb’s most romantic promenade, feel a touch of old Zagreb. Tak imam te rad – The Great ZbiGatsby on Stross brings the warmth of holiday gatherings with the charm and elegance of the 1920s and 1930s.

World.title: New Croatian Tourism Law: Different Deadlines for Landlords to Re-Categorise Apartments
World.content:
November the 14th, 2026 – A new Croatian tourism law could mean that private landlords end up having different deadlines to re-categorise their apartments. Some will get five years, others will be given ten.

The mandatory re-categorisation of apartments every ten years, registration numbers for advertising accommodation via online platforms, stricter inspection supervision and higher penalties for illegal operations are some of the changes envisaged by the final proposal of the new Hospitality Activity Act, which the Croatian Parliament discussed on Thursday. Poslovni reports that although the government is announcing more order on the tourist market and an increase in the quality of service, small landlords are warning of additional obligations and uncertainty about future operating conditions.

State Secretary at the Ministry of Tourism and Sport Monika Udovičić, president of the association Spasimo male obiteljske iznajmljivače (SMOi) Vedran Tomić, and president of the Guild of Hospitality and Tourism Workers of the Croatian Chamber of Trades and Crafts Hrvoje Margan all spoke about the new rules.

different deadlines for different landlords

According to the final proposal of the law, rooms, apartments and holiday homes will in future have to undergo re-categorisation every ten years. However, different transitional deadlines are envisaged for existing landlords, depending on when their approval decision was issued. According to Article 80 of the final proposal of the law, landlords whose decision was issued by the 31st of December 2015 will have to align their operations and obtain a new decision within five years of the entry into force of the relevant ordinance.

For those whose decision was issued as of the 1st of January 2016, a deadline of ten years from the entry into force of the ordinance is envisaged. This means that the deadlines do not automatically start running from the beginning of 2027, but from the day the new ordinance defining the conditions enters into force. After alignment, periodic checks will follow every ten years, which the competent administrative bodies will carry out ex officio. If it is established that the facility no longer meets the prescribed conditions, its type or category may be changed, and in certain cases the decision may be revoked.

the new rules aren’t “anti-landlord”, the powers that be claim

It was explained that hotels and campsites have so far undergone re-categorisation every four years, while the new law extends that period to five years. For small landlords, re-categorisation every ten years is envisaged. The reason for introducing the new checks, according to her, is the fact that there are facilities on the market that were categorised more than 20 years ago and whose compliance with standards has not been re-checked since then.

“This new rule isn’t directed against landlords,” the State Secretary said. She added that those who meet the prescribed conditions need not fear losing their decision. She also emphasised that the goal of the new ordinances is not to prevent existing landlords from operating, but to align standards with modern requirements.

possible consequences…

SMOi president Vedran Tomić questions the need for new categorisation, considering that online platforms and guest reviews have already become an important indicator of accommodation quality. He referred to an analysis of more than 1.6 million reviews according to which, he claims, Croatian private accommodation was rated better than hotel accommodation. Tomić believes that the entire reform is aimed at reducing the share of private accommodation and increasing hotel capacities.

Udovičić rejects such claims and stresses that the Ministry wants to protect family accommodation, but also to distinguish landlords for whom this is a traditional activity from pure rentierism, especially in residential buildings. According to her, Croatia has been receiving approximately ten thousand new beds in private accommodation year after year, while demand has not grown at the same pace, which has also affected occupancy rates.

The Ministry is therefore seeking to further encourage the quality and recognisability of family accommodation. Tomić, however, believes that the market, and not the state, should decide on the further growth of accommodation capacities.

a new rule from may the 1st, 2027

Another important change concerns all landlords who advertise their accommodation units via online platforms for short-term rental. Each such unit will have to have a unique registration number that will be submitted to the platform and displayed in the . Udovičić announced that the issuance of this number will be free of charge, and the procedure digital, via a system available through e-Citizens. According to the final proposal of the law, the provisions on registration numbers and data exchange with platforms should start to apply on the 1st of May 2027. The goal is to link accommodation data with the competent authorities and more effectively suppress unregistered renting. Unlike the registration numbers, most of the other provisions of the new law, if adopted in the proposed form, should enter into force on the 1st of January 2027.

support for more transparency and digitalisation

Hrvoje Margan, president of the Guild of Hospitality and Tourism Workers of the Croatian Chamber of Trades and Crafts, welcomed the adoption of the new law and the announced digitalisation of administrative procedures. Nevertheless, he warned that it is necessary to carefully regulate the minimum technical conditions so that the new ordinances do not become an additional administrative burden for hospitality operators. “We don’t want the ordinances to become a cleansing mechanism for hospitality operators,” he said. Udovičić replied that neither the law nor the future ordinances are conceived as a way of abolishing existing decisions, but as an instrument for modernising the system and raising quality.

The final proposal of the new Hospitality Activity Act has passed parliamentary debate, but still has to be voted on. Until its adoption and the entry into force of the new ordinances, landlords continue to operate according to the current regulations.

World.title: Continental Croatian Tourism up 60%, Million-Euro Incentives in 2027
World.content:
November the 14th, 2026 – Continental Croatian tourism is up by 60%, with new million-euro incentives coming in 2027 aimed at less developed inland regions.

The Croatian National Tourist Board recently launched a new cycle of public tenders for 2027, focused on the development of continental and less developed tourist regions and the promotion of events. Zrinka Gabelica Toplek reports for Poslovni that the decision to announce the tenders was made by the HTZ Tourism Council at its 9th session, and funding is secured through dedicated resources from the Fund for Touristically Underdeveloped Areas and the Mainland and the Fund for Associated Tourist Boards.

big increases for continental croatia

The adopted Open Call for Expressions of Interest aims at cooperation with organisers of “TOP events” of national significance and other events in the segments of eno-gastronomy, nautical tourism, culture, sport, entertainment, MICE and health tourism. In addition, tenders have been announced for regional tourist boards in underdeveloped areas and for projects of associated tourist boards.

“By announcing new tenders for 2027 through the HTZ funds, we are continuing with concrete measures by which we encourage more balanced development of Croatian tourism, while at the same time continuing cooperation with organisers of events and top events that contribute to the attractiveness of our destinations and the attraction of guests throughout the year,” said Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina. He emphasised that since 2021, 51.6 million euros have been secured from these funds for more than 2,000 projects.

“The results are also visible in tourist traffic, which in the continental counties has increased by 60 percent in arrivals and 58 percent in overnight stays over the past ten years, while according to the latest TOMAS research, the average daily expenditure of tourists in continental Croatia has increased by 21 percent compared to 2022.

These are indicators of the growing importance of continental tourism in the overall development of Croatian tourism, and our goal is to continue this positive trend, further strengthen the tourist offer and enable local communities across Croatia to feel the benefits of tourism even more strongly,” Glavina emphasised.

encouraging cooperation

HTZ director Kristjan Staničić stressed that with these calls they want to further encourage the development of quality events that have the potential to become a reason for the arrival of domestic and foreign guests.

“We place special emphasis on touristically underdeveloped areas and the mainland, where events can play an exceptionally important role in creating the recognisability of destinations, activating local potentials and a more even distribution of tourist traffic,” Staničić said, adding that their goal is to support events that, through quality, content and organisation, can position themselves at the national level, create additional value for the destination and encourage cooperation between tourist boards, local stakeholders and the economy.

World.title: Zagreb is Finally Getting A New Tram Line
World.content:
November the 14th, 2026 – The City of Zagreb will finally get a brand new tram line, after over six months of “combing through” all of the submitted bids.

The powers that be in the City of Zagreb have once again selected GIP Pionir as the winner of the tender issued back at the beginning of July. Over two whole years after it was announced, the tender for works on the tram line along Heinzelova and Radnička streets can now proceed. Poslovni reports that the State Commission for the Control of Public Procurement Procedures (DKOM) rejected the appeals of two companies that participated in the public procurement procedure estimated at 48 million euros, so the selection of the contractor can finally be completed and preparations for the start of works can begin soon.

This finally brings to an end the long-running complication surrounding one of the capital projects that the City of Zagreb announced back in 2023 and officially launched in November 2024. The first tender for the contractor of works on 3.7 kilometres of new tram track was announced at the end of 2024, but as the bids received significantly exceeded the estimated amount of 48 million euros (excluding VAT, as with other amounts in the text), the City cancelled the tender and announced a new one in May 2025. The value of the project remained the same, and by July four bids had been received.

After a two-month evaluation, the job was awarded to GIP Pionir, and then the problems began. A consortium of bidders led by the company Texo Molior, which also participated in the tender, decided to lodge an appeal, and the State Commission for the Control of Public Procurement Procedures (DKOM) upheld that appeal in January this year. The Commission ordered the City of Zagreb, as the contracting authority, to go through all the bids again and decide on the best one, which they did this summer. This brings us to the new problem.

As can be seen on the Electronic Public Procurement Noticeboard (EOJN), the company had to send several explanations and supplements to its bid over the past six months. A few days later, however, another appeal against the selection decision arrived at DKOM. The procedure was initiated by the same consortium of bidders as the previous time, namely the companies Texo Molior from Cavtat and Zagreb’s Tigra. The City waited three months for the Commission’s decision in the first appeal procedure, the re-selection of the contractor lasted more than six months, and it has now waited almost another four months for the new DKOM decision. The appeal was rejected and the procedure can now continue.

The project, incidentally, in addition to laying new kilometres of track, also includes the reconstruction and protection of 1.4 kilometres of water supply infrastructure along Heinzelova Street and Radnička Road, as well as the reconstruction of sewer collectors built between 1920 and 1950. Only after these works are completed will it be possible, as the City of Zagreb previously explained, to start work on the new line with a total of nine tram stops.

World.title: Croatia is Facing a Waste Crisis: Waste Could End Up in Forests
World.content:
November the 13th, 2026 – Croatia is currently facing a serious waste crisis, in which waste could end up in the streets and forests. In some cases, it often already is.

The Ekologija grada (City Ecology) association recently warned of the growing problem of waste acceptance at landfills in Croatia, assessing that due to insufficient capacities and the refusal to accept waste from other areas, regular waste collection could be interrupted in part of the country. Poslovni reports that because of what they describe as a crisis of trust in the waste management system after scandals involving illegally disposed waste, a number of landfills have limited or stopped accepting waste from other cities and municipalities. Among them are Karepovac, Ploče’s Lovornik, Bjelovar’s Doline, Diklo, and Sodol.

The consequences of the lack of available capacities, they emphasise, are particularly felt by Makarska and the municipalities of the Makarska Riviera, Omiš, Kaštela, Dugi Rat, Zadvarje and Šestanovac, which have been forced to look for alternative landfills, conclude temporary agreements or organise the transport of waste to more distant counties.

Similar difficulties, they note, have also been experienced by Varaždin, Samobor, Jastrebarsko, Josipdol and Plaški, while Otočac, after the closure of the Podum landfill, redirected its waste to the Babina Gora Waste Management Centre.

The association warns that the problem does not affect only municipal waste but also industrial waste, and that public service providers and authorised companies could be left without space for its disposal and treatment. “If public service providers and authorised companies are left without a place for disposal, the waste will not disappear,” they warn, noting that it could end up on the streets, in forests and by rivers, or in overcrowded warehouses where the risk of fire increases.

They are calling on the Ministry and the Environmental Protection and Energy Efficiency Fund to adopt a binding decision on the acceptance of municipal waste from municipalities that have been left without landfills, and to draw up an urgent plan for the disposal of non-hazardous industrial and hazardous waste.

They are also requesting a check of the contractual obligations of landfills that received Fund resources, with the application of contractual measures, including the return of funds, if it is established that they are refusing to accept waste contrary to the contracts.

They further demand the public disclosure of data on landfills that have free capacities, on the extent of those capacities, and on those that refuse to accept waste. “It is time for decisions, not for politics. Every week in which parties, ministries, counties and cities accuse each other is a week closer to waste on the streets,” said the association’s president, Josip Pavlović.

World.title: Split Port Opens Brand New International Passenger Terminal
World.content:
November the 13th, 2026 – Split Port opened its brand new international passenger terminal this week, concluding a 20+ million euro project.

Split Port officially opened its new international passenger terminal this week, formally marking the completion of a project worth over 20 million euros. Poslovni reports that the extensive project was co-financed with non-repayable EU funds from the National Recovery and Resilience Plan.

a ground floor passenger reception

The former ugly, totally dilapidated building has finally been renovated into a modern passenger terminal, the construction of which has upgraded the port infrastructure and reorganised domestic and international traffic. The terminal was built due to the increase in capacity of the city port, where passenger traffic is almost four times higher and vehicle traffic three times higher than 25 years ago, the Split Port Authority pointed out. The new terminal covers more than 12,000 square metres, while the building itself has almost 3,000 square metres. On the ground floor there is space for receiving passengers, while the upper floor houses operational services, including the police, customs, and the security and port authority departments.

Vice Mihanović, director of the Split Port Authority, announced that the roof of the building will be opened to citizens and will contain public amenities such as a children’s playroom, an outdoor gym and a telescope.

“The facility is intended for international traffic, while domestic liner traffic will remain at the previous locations. With the construction of the terminal, we are relocating international traffic to the port breakwater, and we have repurposed the entire St. Duje Quay for domestic liner traffic,” Mihanović stated. St. Duje Quay spans over 10,000 square metres and six berths, and the re-purposing will improve travel conditions for islanders and domestic passengers and bring them closer to the city after disembarking from the ferry. The old terminal building has also been put into use for domestic traffic only.

the viewpoint and lungomare

Mihanović also announced four major projects of the Port Authority with a total value of almost 60 million euros, including the expansion of St. Peter’s Quay by more than 5,000 square metres and the construction of two new berths. Split Mayor Tomislav Šuta said that the construction of the terminal is a major step forward for the city and passengers, and announced the arrangement of a lungomare and viewpoint in that area.

World.title: Croatia Introduces Tougher Rules and Surveillance for Short-Term Rentals
World.content:
November the 13th, 2026 – Croatia is set to introduce much stricter rules and heightened surveillance for short-term rentals, with around 60,000 units in particular being under the state’s magnifying glass.

Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina stated recently that the Hospitality Activity Act, which has been sent for a second reading in Parliament, is one of the most important for tourism and a major step forward in its development. “With this law we want to achieve three fundamental goals: a strong step forward in suppressing unregistered activity, the complete digitalisation of all administrative procedures in tourism, and the introduction of order, transparency and an increase in the quality of the offer, especially in the category of short-term rental accommodation,” Glavina said after the government session.

Poslovni reports that he further explained that the most important goal – suppressing unregistered activity – is achieved through the law in several ways, one of which is the transposition into Croatian legislation of the European Commission regulation and the introduction of a digital registration number whose aim is to prevent service providers who do not have it from appearing and advertising on online platforms.

He assessed these platforms as very important because the largest tourist traffic comes from them, so among the goals is the introduction of more order into the ways they operate, because until now short-term rental and accommodation could be advertised and sold through them without a decision in the member state.

“The penalties for platforms that would ignore this are draconian and they will certainly make an effort across Europe, including in Croatia, to ensure that this does not happen,” Glavina said. He recalled that the new law expands the powers for supervising providers of this accommodation, in addition to the State Inspectorate, to the Customs Administration, cities and municipalities through the activities of municipal wardens, and it has also been agreed that all eventual revenues from fines will go entirely to the budgets of local and regional self-government units.

The State Inspectorate has also been given the possibility of secret supervision of classifieds, groups on social networks and similar, so that it can react and control the facilities. “This year we have significantly strengthened the activities of inspectors against unregistered activity, and when it enters into force, the law will contribute to this even more,” Glavina said. He repeated that private landlords and family accommodation are very important and that they have been accommodated.

When asked whether he knows how many registered apartments for rent to tourists there are in buildings, he said that he does not have exact data because until now no records have been kept of the type of facilities in which the apartments are located, which will change with the new law and digitalisation.

According to our estimate, that is around 60,000 facilities-apartments, Glavina said, noting that other EU countries are also struggling in various ways with short-term rental to tourists because it reduces the available housing stock.

Regarding the objections and complaints of small landlords and entrepreneurs to the draft law, he said that from 2016 until about a year and a half ago, the number of newly registered beds in short-term accommodation for tourists grew by around 25,000 every year, which led to the fact that, despite the growth of overall tourism, growth in that accommodation was smaller. That is why the steps forward with the law and responsible tourism policy were important, and that is why in the last two years we have not had growth in the number of those beds but even a slight decrease, and those beds have gone into long-term rental, which is also the goal of housing policy, Glavina concluded.
