In July, India's Supreme Court set aside a tribunal's orders that relied on non-existent judgments. A US judge recently disqualified lawyers over the use of fabricated legal citations.

Last year, India's Supreme Court justices also warned against the fabrication of judicial documents, saying such acts "bearing forged signatures of Judges strikes at the very foundation of public trust" and "such grave criminal acts cannot be treated as ordinary or routine offences".

World.title: Congress vs Congress: How Mekedatu Dam has sparked war of words between Manickam Tagore and DK Shivakumar
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A proposed dam on the

has triggered a war of words between two Congress leaders from neighbouring states, with

Congress Committee president Manickam Tagore opposing the project and

chief minister DK Shivakumar defending his state's right to build it.

The disagreement has brought out the competing positions within the Congress over the Mekedatu dam, an inter-state water dispute that has long strained relations between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. While Tagore has urged the Tamil Nadu government to step up its legal opposition, Shivakumar has maintained that the project is within Karnataka's rights and would not affect Tamil Nadu's allocated share of Cauvery water.



How Congress face-off started

The latest exchange began with Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president Manickam Tagore condemning Karnataka's push for the proposed Mekedatu dam and urging Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay to strengthen the state's legal opposition to the project.

Tagore criticised Karnataka deputy chief minister DK Shivakumar for seeking final central clearance for the dam, arguing that his claim about the Supreme Court ruling in Karnataka's favour misrepresented the legal position.





He pointed out that Tamil Nadu had already approached the apex court challenging the project and that the matter remained sub judice.

"It is deeply condemnable that Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar, in the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Mysuru, said, 'No one can stop the construction of a dam at Mekedatu,' and that the central government must give its final approval for it. The Karnataka Chief Minister continues to adopt a stubborn stance that blatantly violates the Supreme Court ruling and the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal's final award.

This statement, which goes against the principle of federalism and seeks to destroy the livelihoods of Tamil Nadu's farmers, is utterly unacceptable," he said.

"Since Tamil Nadu is a lower-riparian state in the Cauvery river water sharing arrangement, Karnataka cannot unilaterally implement any project that affects our rights. The central government must not grant any permission to build the Mekedatu dam without the full consent of the lower-riparian states.

Approving the Mekedatu project without Tamil Nadu's consent is not only illegal but will also severely affect the lives of farmers in the delta districts," he added.

He also questioned the Centre's impartiality, alleging that its earlier approval of the project's Detailed Project Report (DPR) without Tamil Nadu's consent was an "outright act of discrimination". Tagore urged Vijay to pursue all necessary legal measures to prevent the dam's construction.

"It is the duty of the Modi-led central government to prevent Karnataka from laying even a single brick at Mekedatu. On behalf of the Tamil Nadu Congress, we will never allow this project; we will go to any lengths to fight to protect our state's rights," he said.

DK Shivakumar hits back

Responding to Tagore's criticism, Shivakumar asserted that Karnataka had the right to build the dam and said he was unconcerned about opposition from Tamil Nadu.

"Let anyone condemn; I am least bothered. It is my state, my right," he said.

He invited Tamil Nadu leaders to visit the proposed project site, offering to explain how the dam would benefit the region.

"Let them come with a delegation; I will show them and explain to them how it helps," he said.

Dismissing the criticism as political posturing, Shivakumar said opposition to the project would continue irrespective of which party raised the issue in Tamil Nadu.

"If Congress doesn't condemn, DMK will condemn. If DMK doesn't condemn, AIADMK will condemn. Then everyone may condemn," he said.

He also maintained that Karnataka would protect Tamil Nadu's allocated share of 177 TMC of Cauvery water while pursuing the project.

What is Mekedatu Dam project?

The proposed Mekedatu project is a balancing reservoir across the Cauvery river near Kanakapura in Karnataka. It is intended to meet Bengaluru's drinking water requirements and generate around 400 MW of electricity.

Karnataka has argued that the reservoir would help regulate the river's flow and store surplus water during periods of high inflow. The state maintains that the project would not reduce the quantity of water allocated to Tamil Nadu.

Tamil Nadu, however, has consistently opposed the proposal, arguing that an upstream reservoir could affect the flow of Cauvery water into the state, particularly during periods of shortage.

It has maintained that Karnataka cannot proceed without the consent of the other Cauvery basin states.

What is Cauvery water-sharing dispute?

The disagreement over Mekedatu is rooted in the decades-old Cauvery water-sharing dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, with both states having competing requirements for the river's water.

In its 2018 verdict, the Supreme Court modified the allocation made by the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal. Tamil Nadu was awarded 177.25 TMC of water, while Karnataka received 284.75 TMC.

Tagore referred to Tamil Nadu's entitlement of 177.25 TMC while arguing that Karnataka had historically failed to release the state's stipulated share on time.

According to Tagore, this allocation includes 60 TMC from the Kabini dam, 52 TMC from the Krishnaraja Sagar (KRS) dam and 80 TMC generated through rainfall in uncontrolled catchment areas of Karnataka along the 200-km stretch between the KRS dam and the Biligundulu water gauging station.

Tagore accused Karnataka politicians of using the Cauvery issue for political purposes.

"Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar's statement is very painful. The people of Tamil Nadu want to have cordial relations with Karnataka. But Karnataka politicians are doing politics over Cauvery. We want Cauvery water based on Supreme Court's order. The water has not been released as per Cauvery Tribunal order. Supreme Court's ruling has not been followed.

This is a very serious thing," news agency ANI quoted him as saying.

He also urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to intervene, saying, "We demand that the PM should not betray Tamil Nadu. If Modi betrays Tamil Nadu's interests, he will never be forgiven in Tamil Nadu."

What is political dimension

The dispute has placed two Congress leaders on opposing sides of an issue that cuts across state boundaries. Tagore has aligned his position with Tamil Nadu's longstanding opposition to the project, urging Vijay's government to pursue all necessary legal measures to prevent its construction.

World.title: Studying abroad, visiting India or working overseas? Who gets counted in Census 2027
World.content:
Sheetal Verma, director of census operations and chief principal census officer, Uttar Pradesh, explained that temporary absence from India was different from ordinarily residing overseas.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

LUCKNOW: Indian residents temporarily travelling abroad during Census 2027 will be counted at their usual place of residence if they return within 35 days, subject to enumeration rules.The clarification comes ahead of the 15-day online self-enumeration exercise beginning Nov 16, which will continue until Nov 30, followed by door-to-door population enumeration from Dec 1, 2026, to Jan 4, 2027.Sheetal Verma, director of census operations and chief principal census officer, Uttar Pradesh, explained that temporary absence from India was different from ordinarily residing overseas.Indian citizens studying, working or permanently residing abroad throughout the enumeration period would generally not be included in their family's household merely because they hold Indian passports.Parents completing online self-enumeration should therefore not include children ordinarily residing abroad.However, if a temporarily absent family member returns during the enumeration period and qualifies for inclusion, the enumerator can update the household details during the physical visit.Personnel posted at Indian diplomatic missions abroad will be covered through special arrangements coordinated centrally.Conversely, foreign nationals ordinarily residing in India, including students and workers, will be counted irrespective of citizenship. Short-term foreign visitors and diplomatic personnel enjoying immunity are subject to separate rules.Verma emphasised that the census records population, not citizenship, and inclusion does not confer Indian citizenship.Similarly, seasonal migrant workers residing in Uttar Pradesh during enumeration, including those employed at brick kilns, sugar mills and other establishments, will be counted in the state.They should inform enumerators at their places of origin to prevent duplication.The census reference time is midnight at the start of Jan 5, 2027. A revisional round from January 5 to 9 will account for births, deaths and omissions.Final census data is scheduled to be made public in April 2027.

World.title: Airlines warn of diplomatic fallout over slot cuts
World.content:

MUMBAI: Some foreign airlines facing relocation from Mumbai airport have threatened reciprocal measures under bilateral air services agreements if Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL) denies them historical slots for the summer 2027 schedule. Last week, MIAL decided to cut slots for airlines serving 14 destinations as part of a capacity-reduction plan linked to T1 redevelopment. The move has disproportionately affected West Asian carriers.Four airlines have written separately to MIAL and the ministry of civil aviation (MoCA), escalating the dispute to diplomatic channels, said sources. The carriers have sought MoCA intervention and warned of escalation to the govt, Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) and aviation authorities in their respective countries, including possible reciprocal measures under bilateral agreements.They have questioned why flights to 14 international destinations, mostly in West Asia, were selected for relocation from T2. One letter called the move "highly discriminatory and targeted towards" West Asia markets", while excluding Dubai and Abu Dhabi without justification. The 14 destinations are Bahrain, Dammam, Dhaka, Doha, Fujairah, Jakarta, Jeddah, Kathmandu, Kuwait City, Madinah, Muscat, Ras Al Khaimah, Riyadh and Sharjah.The airlines have also questioned the regulatory basis and methodology for the capacity cut, seeking a copy of any MoCA approval for the cited 5 million passengers per annum reduction and denial of historical slots. Arguing that redevelopment cannot override established historical slot entitlements, they asked: "On what authority does MIAL propose to decline summer 2027 historical slots?" They have demanded written confirmation that their S27 slots will be honoured without unilateral reduction or cancellation.MIAL's capacity-reduction plan is linked to the redevelopment of Terminal 1, which will eventually require passenger traffic to be redistributed between Mumbai and Navi Mumbai airports. tnn

World.title: KLE Society’s 111th Foundation Day celebrated by collecting 300 units of blood
World.content:
KLE Technological University celebrated the 111th Foundation Day of KLE Society in Hubballi on Friday (November 13, 2026), by paying tribute to its founders and organising a voluntary blood donation camp in which over 300 units of blood were collected.

Addressing the gathering, Vice-Chancellor Prakash G. Tewari recalled the founding of the society and lauded the vision and dedication of its founders in expanding access to education. He said their contribution to society continued to inspire generations.

The celebrations were attended by Registrar Basavaraj Anami, Executive Dean B.L. Desai deans Uma Mudengudi and Sanjay Kotabagi and Coordinator of the C&M Cell M.R. Patil, besides heads of departments, faculty members, administrators, staff and student representatives.

300 units collected

In the blood donation camp organised in association with Rashtrotthana Blood Bank and Karnataka Medical College and Research Institute (KMCRI), with the support of HDFC Bank, Hubballi, 300 units of blood were donated by faculty members and students.

Rashtrotthana Blood Bank administrator Dattamurthy Kulkarni, KMCRI Blood Bank Officer Anil Kumar and HDFC Bank Circle Head Madhusudhan Radhakrishna were present along with Sports Activities Coordinator Vijayakumar Nimbagal.

Medical teams from the partner institutions supervised the donation process, while student volunteers coordinated the arrangements.

World.title: Puri resigns from Uttar Pradesh Rajya Sabha seat after being re-elected from MP
World.content:
Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri resigned from his Rajya Sabha seat from Uttar Pradesh on Saturday, days after being re-elected to the House unopposed from Madhya Pradesh.

Rajya Sabha Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan accepted Mr. Puri’s resignation.

Mr. Puri’s term from Uttar Pradesh was due to end on November 25.

He was elected unopposed for the Madhya Pradesh seat on November 5, with his tenure ending on April 2, 2030.

Mr. Puri was nominated to the seat vacated by former Union Minister L. Murugan, who resigned last month to strengthen the BJP in Tamil Nadu ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.

Announcing the vacation of the Rajya Sabha seat, Secretary General P.C. Mody, in a notification, said, "Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, an elected Member of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha), representing the state of Uttar Pradesh, resigned his seat in the Rajya Sabha, and his resignation has been accepted by the Chairman, Rajya Sabha wef, 14th November, 2026."

World.title: Government is committed to supporting startups in Kalyana Karnataka: Priyank Kharge
World.content:
The Karnataka government will extend all necessary support to entrepreneurs in Kalyana Karnataka to establish and expand startups by facilitating access to investment, mentorship, technology and market linkages, Minister for Home, Information Technology and Biotechnology (IT-BT) and E-Governance and Kalaburagi District In-charge Priyank Kharge said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

Speaking at the ‘Kalyana Karnataka Startup Dialogue-2026’ in Kalaburagi, he urged young entrepreneurs to come forward with innovative ideas and pursue their business ventures with determination.

Referring to his government’s policies and schemes for encouraging start-ups, Mr. Kharge urged the young entrepreneurs to study the initiatives and identify the support available for their ventures. “If existing policies do not address their specific requirements, they should bring the gaps to the government’s notice. We are ready to formulate suitable new schemes and stand by young entrepreneurs,” he said.

ELEVATE programme

Pointing out that Bengaluru contributed around 41% to the State’s GDP, he said Kalaburagi’s contribution was estimated at 1.9%. “The government aimed to increase this to 3%, which would require concerted efforts across sectors, including education, agriculture and manufacturing. Startups would play a significant role in accelerating the economic growth of Kalyana Karnataka,” he added.

Mr. Kharge said the State government’s ELEVATE programme had supported the establishment of around 1,500 startups over the past 10 years. “Selected startups were eligible for financial assistance of up to ₹50 lakh. Startups based outside Bengaluru currently accounted for around 28% of the total, and the government was working to increase this proportion by encouraging entrepreneurship across the State,” he said and added that a scheme was also being planned to provide selected entrepreneurs working in the deep-tech sector with financial assistance of up to ₹1 crore over the next 10 years.

Local Economy Accelerator Programme

Emphasising that startups should not remain confined to Bengaluru but expand to tier-II and tier-III cities, Mr. Kharge said the government had introduced the Local Economy Accelerator Programme (LEAP) to strengthen local economies and encourage young people to become job creators rather than job seekers.

“Young entrepreneurs needed to understand market demand, business management, product positioning and customer outreach. Having an innovative idea alone was not be sufficient; they also needed the skills to turn it into a sustainable business. Interaction and mentoring programmes involving entrepreneurs and industry experts are being organised to help them acquire these skills,” Mr. Kharge said.

The minister said that the government was also taking up several initiatives to promote artificial intelligence (AI) in Kalyana Karnataka and incubation centres were being established to encourage startups.

Medical Education Minister Dr. Sharan Prakash Patil, Srikrishna Sridhar Murthy of Sattva Consulting and Prashanth Prakash, Founding Partner of Accel India, shared their views and experiences at the interaction. KrishiKalpa Foundation CEO C.M. Patil moderated the discussion.

Earlier, K. Ullas Kamath, founder of UK&Co, delivered a special address on the growth of local entrepreneurship and the skills required to build successful businesses.

World.title: Gaggan Anand’s rāga in Delhi: Inside his new restaurant with Chef Rydo Anton
World.content:
Gaggan is home. Or is he?

The flamboyant Kolkata-born drummer-turned-chef-turned-culinary rock star is finally bringing his irreverent spin on flavour to Delhi with rāga. His eponymous restaurant in Bangkok was recently named the second best in the world by the influential The 50 List, behind Asador Etxebarri in Spain. His India debut is in partnership with Zorawar Kalra, the founder and managing director of Massive Restaurants. Of course, expectations are sky-high.

Unsurprisingly, the restaurant oozes attitude. Set in swanky Janpath, it occupies what used to its heavy doors open into a cathedral-like foyer dominated by stained-glass windows. A list of ‘house rules’ are handed to guests as they enter: phones on silent, one smoke break (if you must), and remember, ‘this is not dinner and a dash’. It is peak Gaggan: his kitchen, his rules and lick the plate when you are told to.

The ₹23,333 you pay per couple (non-refundable and to be paid in full when you book) is not just for a meal, it is for theatre, the extravagance and, let us be honest, the novel experience of being guided firmly through an unpredictable menu in an age when we have become blasé about luxury.

Then, you meet Rydo Anton, the ‘Ra’ in the equation, and realise why the restaurant has a different, quieter energy from Gaggan in Bangkok. The young, calm chef is putting his own mark on the space, working alongside his mentor to create something fresh. “When Gaggan told me we would be opening in India, I said, ‘Okay. So who is going to come with me? And he said, ‘No one. It is just you’.“ Rydo chuckles and adds, “He knows I like challenges.”

Now 37-years-old, the Jakarta-born chef’s food is interesting because he is. He was sent to Kuala Lumpur with his brother when he was 11, in the wake of Indonesia’s monetary crisis. “I missed my mom’s food, so I started to cook,” he says. “It was survival for us.” He went on to get a diploma in culinary arts, then got his first internship at 18, cooking for members of a country club in Baltimore. The money he saved from this job enabled him to study at the Culinary Arts Academy in Switzerland, after which he worked with Gordon Ramsay’s restaurants in Doha.

“In 2012, I went to Gaggan in Bangkok and asked him for a job. I became his head chef in 2015,” says Rydo.

Gaggan explains why Rydo was chosen for India. “After 14 years, Rydo knows both my cooking and my madness. He has seen the good days, the disasters, the ideas that worked and the ones that should never have left my head... Our energies are different. I can get excited about an idea and want to change everything immediately. He has the patience and precision to work through it and make it happen consistently. And he can disagree with me. That is very important. A kitchen where everybody says yes becomes very boring.”

Gaggan adds, “People keep asking how much freedom I give him. Look at the name: the “Ra” comes before the “Ga”! He is my partner. rāga has to carry his identity too. If, after 14 years, all I have taught him is how to copy me, then I have failed as a mentor.”

As Bon Jovi’s ‘Livin‘ on a Prayer’plays in the background, we try Rydo’s spin on Gaggan’s popular Yoghurt Explosion, a version that brings together chilli-dusted guavas, a popular Indian roadside snack, and the popping candy of our childhood. I will not give away too many details from the menu – that ₹23,333 price tag is also for the joy of discovery. But I will warn you that you will enjoy some of it, be perplexed occasionally, and yes, not everything will work. Think of it like art: the exposure, the experience and your reaction to it is the point.

“I think time and attention are enormous luxuries,” says Gaggan. He adds, “Somebody gives us a few hours of their life. What do we do with that? Can we make them curious? Can we make them laugh? Can a flavour bring back something they had forgotten? Beautiful crockery and good ingredients matter, of course. But you cannot buy an emotional response by putting an expensive ingredient on a plate. At rāga, we also want you to enjoy the whole journey without feeling exhausted by the food.”

I sit facing the kitchen – always the best seats in the house in my opinion – while an army of chefs work with an easy rhythm, communicating constantly using eye contact and hand gestures, so all we hear is the sizzle of pans. While Sting’s ‘Every breath you take’ plays from powerful speakers, we clip through a 22-course menu inspired by some India’s street food, from Bengali walnut jhal muri to white chocolate pani puri, reimagined with sophisticated equipment, fancy culinary degrees and whimsy. There are nods to comfort food as well, including a serving of saffron ice cream with soft peaks.

Some flavours are sharper than they need to be, a consequence of the kitchen’s emphasis on concentrating flavour in every course. Rydo is gracious about the feedback, admitting that he is still developing his palate for Indian food. “After work I get kathi rolls for dinner, and I love the green chutney. It made me realise we need to make our food punchy.”

He adds that the food at rāga will evolve with the chefs and seasons. As it should.

After all, Gaggan sees food as a way to express himself. “When you are young, you carry a lot of anger and a lot of hunger. You want an opportunity, and when you don’t get it, you want to prove everybody wrong. That energy helped me. But you cannot spend your whole life cooking an argument,” Gaggan says. “Distance also makes you understand things differently. Food you took for granted becomes something you miss. You start examining your own memories more closely.”

He emphasises that he does not see rāga as a homecoming. “India never really left my cooking. I could be in Bangkok, listening to rock music, using Japanese ingredients and the flavour would still take you somewhere in India. I guess, that connection was always there.”

Now, he says, it is Rydo’s turn.

rāga by Gaggan is at 21 A, Janpath Road, Connaught Place. It costs ₹11,111 (plus taxes) per guest.

World.title: Masaharu Morimoto: 22 years of getting Japanese food right in Mumbai
World.content:
When Masaharu Morimoto opened Wasabi by Morimoto at Mumbai’s Taj Mahal Palace 22 years ago, he arrived with a menu he was confident would work. Within a month, he had to change half of it. “I was told this is a different culture. Most customers here are vegetarians. But I didn’t know how to make Japanese food vegetarian,” he says. He then turned to the temple cooking of Japan’s Buddhist monks and rebuilt the menu.

Recently, Morimoto was back in the city to mark the restaurant’s 22nd anniversary and he admits he almost did not come at all. “When the Taj asked me 22 years ago, I was hesitant. It was far away from the United States, and I was worried about how I would control the food quality,” he says. What changed his mind was the hotel itself: its reputation, its kitchen and the people running it. “That is Japanese culture. You match, you shake hands, it’s tight, and that’s it.”

Long before he became one of the world’s best-known Japanese chefs, Morimoto wanted to play professional baseball. A devoted fan of his hometown team, the Hiroshima Toyo Carp, he was a talented catcher at school and came close to turning professional before a broken shoulder ended his career. He remains a baseball fan to this day. Cooking began with an apprenticeship at a sushi restaurant, where the owner did not let him touch fish for the first year. Instead, he cleaned, served, chopped scallions and washed rice. He later spent five years at Nobu in New York before opening his first Morimoto restaurant in Philadelphia in 2001. Today, he runs 21 restaurants around the world and has helped create his own sake and beer.

Running a kitchen in Mumbai from thousands of miles away, he says, comes down to ingredients and communication. Sushi and sashimi fish are flown in from Japan every week, as Indian waters, though rich in seafood, do not yield fish suited to sushi. He personally approves every supplier the restaurant imports from, sets the menu, trains the staff and stays in regular contact with the Japanese chef who runs the kitchen. He visits once every two years. “Every country is different. In the US, the fish is good, but not the vegetables or fruit. In Europe, the fish is not so good, but the fruit and vegetables are fine. India is in between,” he says.

Being the city’s pioneer of Japanese dining is both a source of pride and pressure. “I am very proud, but it’s also a stress. We have to be the top,” he says. In the early years, many of Wasabi’s diners were Japanese expatriates working in the city, ordering sushi, sashimi, ramen and bento boxes. Today, the guests are largely well-travelled diners from India and abroad who know good sushi when they taste it. “I have to focus on real Japanese food,” he says, before offering a line that sums up his philosophy: “Fusion, for me, is confusion.”

Lunch began, fittingly, with the restaurant’s namesake — fresh wasabi root grated at the table. vThe shiro ebi nigiri, made with the delicate white shrimp of Japan’s Toyama Bay, and the flame-seared yellowtail maki with asparagus and ume plum were excellent, but the vegetarian dishes held their own. Edamame arrived smoked over cherry blossom wood chips and finished with furikake and soy butter, while Hakata eggplant took the place of fish in a nanbanzuke, the traditional sweet-and-sour pickled preparation. The shrimp tempura with spicy sauce, on the menu since opening day, and the black cod miso remain the restaurant’s best-known dishes.

His own eating habits are considerably simpler than the menus he creates. He eats one meal a day, usually between 3pm and 5pm, and stopped drinking alcohol five years ago. “Before, I used to drink a lot. Since I stopped, I don’t feel like going out. I stay at home,” he says. At home, he leaves the cooking to his wife, who keeps his diet largely vegetarian, with tofu, soya beans, yoghurt and occasional steamed salmon. He enjoys Indian food, especially the breads and dosa, though he now avoids anything too spicy.

For a chef who has battled on television, built 21 restaurants across the world and spent 22 years at the top of Mumbai’s Japanese dining scene, his favourite ingredient is still the one he washed as an apprentice. “Rice,” he says. Some lessons, it seems, are never forgotten.

World.title: Case registered against 100 Uvari villagers for holding bus passengers hostage
World.content:
Police have registered a case against 100 fishermen of the coastal village of Uvari on charges of holding passengers travelling in two Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (TNSTC) buses hostage on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night. They did so in a bid to compel officials of the Fisheries Department to release the vehicles loaded with fish they had harvested using banned purse seine nets.

After being alerted that a section of the Uvari fishermen had been using banned purse seine nets, the Fisheries Department officials conducted a surprise raid on Thursday evening and found 42 insulated vehicles loaded with tonnes of fish caught using the prohibited fishing gear. When the officials detained the 42 vehicles as they were about to leave for various markets, the Uvari fishermen sounded the church bell to mobilise a crowd and detained two TNSTC buses carrying passengers at around 9 p.m.

Only after the police pleaded with them were the passengers allowed to leave, after two hours of detention, the commuters said.

Based on the complaints received from the TNSTC bus crew, the Uvari police have registered a case against 100 persons under Sections 189(2) (unlawful assembly with the common illegal object), 126(2) (wrongful restraint), and 293 (public nuisance) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

“The sections invoked by the police are mere eyewash... The passengers of two TNSTC buses were held hostage by the mob, whose members made it clear that they would not release the buses until their demand was met...,” a woman teacher from Kanniyakumari district, who was one of the hostages, told The Hindu.

“They threatened to set the buses on fire even as we were sitting inside. When some of the passengers frantically called their families over the phone to tell them about their situation, they were threatened by the mob. Is that not tantamount to holding the passengers hostage? What prevents the police from invoking punitive sections against the mob? This kind of policing will only encourage unruly groups to take innocent members of the public hostage and make the police go down on their knees,” she said.

“We came to know about the BNS sections invoked in this case only today (Saturday). We will approach the High Court seeking a direction to alter the sections under which the case has been registered and also seek action against the police officer concerned for not discharging his duty of registering a case under the appropriate provisions of the BNS,” said the teacher.

World.title: Magnitude-4 moderate earthquake hits Assam
World.content:
An earthquake of magnitude 4 jolted parts of Assam on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

The National Centre for Seismology said the quake was recorded at 2.43 pm in Kamrup district at a depth of 10 km.

Several parts of the State, including its largest city Guwahati, felt the tremors.

However, no reports of damage to life or property have been reported so far.

Assam falls in a high seismic zone, making earthquakes frequent.

World.title: Will R&AW’s overseas operations affect ties? | Explained
World.content:
The story so far: India’s external intelligence agency R&AW (Research and Analysis Wing) was in the spotlight this week, as reports came in from the U.S., Canada, Australia and Pakistan of the alleged targeting and killing of Indian-origin Khalistani separatist operatives around the world, spearheaded by the agency.

The charges, that are yet to be proven in court, pertain to a number of investigations in different countries. This week, the U.S.-based Washington Post claimed that American officials believe that the R&AW’s previous chief Samant Goel had approved an assassination operation, that was foiled last year, against Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a Khalistani activist lawyer of U.S. and Canadian nationality on India’s most-wanted UAPA (Unlawful Activities Prevention Act) terror list. It also revealed the name of a security official, Vikash Yadav, believed to have been at R&AW at the time, and said U.S. officials had discussed whether to indict him for ordering Indian businessman Nikhil Gupta to hire a hitman for the job. In the indictment filed by the U.S. New York Southern District Attorney’s office last November, message transcripts indicated Mr. Gupta had also enquired about ordering a “hit” on a Khalistani activist in Canada, just days before the killing of Canadian Hardeep Singh Nijjar outside Toronto in June 2023.

World.title: FO says Climate Minister Musadik Malik nominated to represent Pakistan at SCO moot in New Delhi
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday that Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik had been nominated to represent Pakistan at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue in New Delhi from Nov 20-22.

In a statement, the FO said the gathering would bring representatives from SCO member states to discuss issues related to civilisational dialogue and cultural understanding.

“The government of Pakistan remains committed to promoting dialogue among civilisations and fostering people-to-people contacts within the SCO framework in a spirit of mutual respect,” the statement said.

According to Indian news outlet ANI, 10 SCO members — including Pakistan — have been invited to participate in the inaugural Civilisational Dialogue. It added that the gathering was proposed by New Delhi.

In a press briefing on Friday, Indian foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that India has invited several SCO member states to take part in the dialogue, adding that New Delhi looks forward to hosting the gathering.

Islamabad has a long history of engagement with the SCO through hosting meetings and chairing bodies within the group. It also holds the permanent chairmanship of an SCO working group on poverty alleviation, which focuses on improving living standards across the region.

In October 2024, Islamabad hosted the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting , which India’s Minister for External Affairs Dr S. Jaishan­kar attended on behalf of his prime minister.

Jaishankar’s trip, months before the May 2025 military conflict between the neighbours escalated tensions, marked the first such visit by an Indian foreign minister in nearly a decade.

Last month, India sent its SCO National Coordinator Alok Dimri to Islamabad for a preparatory meeting for the next SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) meeting in August 2027, which Pakistan is set to host.

“This is my first time on Pakistani soil; these SCO-related programmes will continue throughout the year and culminate in the Islamabad summit,” the Indian official had told PTV News.

Pakistan’s chairmanship of SCO CHS marks another step in the country’s growing engagement with the regional organisation, which has expanded its focus from security cooperation to economic development and regional connectivity.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar has noted that Pakistan’s membership has evolved from observer status to proactive full membership since 2017, reflecting its commitment to multilateralism and regional cooperation.

Earlier this month, Pakistan also assumed the chairmanship of the SCO Interbank Consortium (SCO-IBC) for 2026-27, the Ministry of Finance said, with HBL Chairman Sultan Ai Allana taking charge for the period.

“The development coincides with Pakistan’s chairmanship of the SCO for the same period, reflecting the country’s role in promoting regional trade, investment, financial connectivity and economic cooperation”, the ministry said.

World.title: 2 soldiers martyred, 16 terrorists killed in North Waziristan operations: ISPR
World.content:
Two soldiers were martyred and 16 terrorists were killed in North Waziristan district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the military’s media wing said on Saturday.

According to a statement issued by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), in continuation of a series of IBOs being conducted by security forces, multiple khwarij locations were engaged in the general areas of Mir Ali, Datta Khel and surrounding areas in North Waziristan.

“Following fierce fire exchanges, in last twelve hours, 12 khwarij, including two Afghan nationals belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khwarij were sent to hell in Ali Khel, while two khwarij each were neutralised in Mir Ali and Datta Khel, thereby causing a significant blow to the khwarijs’ network operating in the area,” ISPR said.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term used by the state for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

ISPR said that during the operations, 43-year-old Havildar Asmat Ali and 32-year-old Naik Aftab Ali embraced martyrdom.

“Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed Indian-sponsored khwarij, who remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities, including the killing of innocent civilians,” it said.

The statement said that sanitisation operations would continue to eliminate “remaining holed up khwarij from these areas”, adding that the counterterrorism campaign would continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored terrorism from the country.

President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the security forces for their successful operation and expressed condolences over the martyrdom of the two soldiers.

He said operations under the ongoing Azm-i-Istehkam campaign against foreign-sponsored terrorism would continue with full force until the elimination of the last terrorist.

The operations come a day after ISPR said 74 terrorists were killed in IBOs in KP and Balochistan.

On Friday, it said 43 terrorists were killed during operations conducted over 48 hours in KP, including 35 in Mir Ali, North Waziristan district, and eight in Orakzai district. Another 31 terrorists were killed in Balochistan during an operation launched on Nov 3.

Pakistan has seen a surge in terrorism, especially in KP and Balochistan since the banned TTP ended its ceasefire deal with the government in November 2022, vowing to increase attacks.

According to Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies , the country’s security environment continued to show considerable volatility from Oct 30 to Nov 5, 2026, with renewed terrorist activity in parts of KP and the former tribal districts, alongside intensified counterterrorism operations and changing patterns of militant violence.

Correction: An earlier version of this story said 14 terrorists were killed. The error is regretted.

World.title: KP Governor Kundi announces suspension of gold mining across province
World.content:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Saturday announced a ban on gold mining across the province and the revocation of all mining leases as part of measures to curb illegal mining.

Addressing a press conference in Peshawar, Governor Kundi condemned the attack in Kohat that claimed the lives of 10 police personnel returning from an operation against illegal mining in the region.

He said an exemplary operation would be launched against those responsible for the attack, as well as their facilitators, as part of the government’s future strategy.

“There will be zero tolerance for those involved in this,” he said.

The governor also directed mining leaseholders to remove heavy machinery from the relevant areas within a week, warning that they would be held responsible for any losses incurred otherwise.

“After one week, the machinery, if not removed, will be seized,” Governor Kundi said, adding that the fines imposed this time would not be limited to Rs25,000 or Rs30,000, as had been the case under magistrates, but could reach Rs2 million under the law.

“We are also investigating why fines were not being imposed in accordance with the law,” he said.

The governor added that any politicians or individuals from other institutions found to be involved in illegal mining would be punished in accordance with the law.

On the Kohat incident, Governor Kundi said that following the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule, the administration had launched an operation against illegal gold mining.

On October 11, 2026, the federal government imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in KP following the President’s approval of the federal cabinet’s recommendations. It cited KP government’s “deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism” and the deteriorating security situation in the province.

An 11-member technocratic KP Advisory Council was formed to assist the governor in running the province, and a new chief secretary was appointed.

He said police personnel were targeted by Fitna al-Khawarij while returning from a successful operation.

“Fitna al-Khawarij and illegal miners had a nexus. The miners used to pay extortion money to the terrorists and, in return, received protection from them,” the governor said, adding that this nexus was responsible for the martyrdom of the police personnel.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

He also shared a list of illegal mining equipment and machinery operating in Kohat. Mining was under way in two blocks — C and D — he said.

“Some 8,350 trucks, 3,660 excavators, 1,730 tractor trolleys with dynamos, 1,600 dumpers, 200 heavy loaders and between 49,000 and 51,000 labourers were involved in the mining activity,” Governor Kundi said, adding that illegal mining was worth Rs4.92 billion a month.

“Eighty per cent of the profits were being sent to Afghanistan and used for terrorist activities against Pakistan,” he said.

The governor further stated that during the tenure of the PTI government, a ‘Youth Committee’ was formed in February 2026 under the chairmanship of a Taliban leader, Naimatullah alias Commander.

“The purpose of this Youth Committee was to collect extortion money from locals and non-locals — Rs800,000 from locals and Rs110,000 from non-locals every week,” he said.

The money was being used by Fitna al-Khawarij against Pakistan, its security forces and police, he added.

The governor assured that there would be no political victimisation, adding that anyone found involved in the nexus would be held accountable.

“If there is no system of reward and punishment, neither this province nor this country will move forward. This country can no longer run under the doctrine of necessity,” he said.

He said anyone found guilty, whether a politician, bureaucrat or police officer, would have to face the consequences, regardless of how influential they were.

Governor Kundi also shared a list of people allegedly involved in illegal activities across KP, including 12 politicians: Aftab Alam of PTI, MNA Sheheryar Afridi of PTI, Senator Khurram Zeeshan of PTI, former Gambat town nazim Sajid Iqbal, former Lachi town nazim Ehsan, former MNA Amjad Afridi of PPP, former district mayor Seth Saifullah of JUI-F, Naseem Afridi, former JUI-F candidate Advocate Hammad Azam, Sohail Afridi’s brother Naveed, Azhar Bukhari and Nazir Afridi.

He also shared a list of local residents allegedly involved in the illegal activities.

The governor announced the establishment of a task force, named after martyred Deputy Superintendent of Police Haider Zaman, to formulate a “comprehensive and lasting” strategy for gold mining activities in KP within three weeks.

“We are bringing in a comprehensive system governing mining leases, related laws and security for mining workers under future leases,” he said.

Governor Kundi also announced that a judicial commission, headed by a retired Peshawar High Court (PHC) judge, would be formed by the following week to investigate the Kohat attack.

“We hope that the report will come soon so those responsible can be held accountable,” he said.

The governor also urged members of the KP Advisory Council to investigate all those involved in illegal gold mining and examine how large numbers of mining licences had been granted.

At the outset of his press conference, the KP governor said more than a month had passed since the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP. “We will try to move in the right direction,” he said.

He said action had been taken in certain areas and the administration had received positive feedback.

“However, our topmost priority is to restore peace in the province and protect the rights and lives of the people,” he said.

Governor Kundi said the provincial administration had also decided to protect KP’s resources and would not allow anyone to plunder them.

Referring to the recent two-day minerals conference, the governor said the province was keen to enter into joint ventures to utilise its resources. However, he added, protecting the people and their rights would come first.

“For the past 13 years, the resources of our province have been looted,” he said.

He said that whenever the provincial government invited international investors and national companies to invest in KP’s natural resources, some people opposed the move, claiming that the province’s resources were being sold off.

“We are not selling your resources. Above all, the interests of the people of the province will be protected,” he said.

Governor Kundi alleged that those raising objections to the initiative were themselves responsible for plundering KP’s resources.

Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman had alleged that the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in KP in October 2026 was linked to the federal government’s motive to take control of the province’s resources.

“We are fighting a war against terrorism and we have burnt our boats. Accepting defeat is not a choice for us,” Kundi said, reaffirming his commitment to winning the fight against terrorism and bringing peace and development to the province.

The governor reiterated his call for an effective system of reward and punishment, vowing that no one who had plundered the province’s resources would be spared, regardless of their position or status.

World.title: Achakzai, Abbas move FCC for release of Sohail Afridi, detained lawmakers
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The leaders of the opposition in both Houses of Parliament on Saturday approached the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), seeking the immediate release of Sohail Afridi, the non-functional Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister, along with eight other elected members of the provincial assembly and six members of the National Assembly.

Afridi has not been seen since the Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11. The very next day, a federal minister confirmed that he and some of his cabinet members were in preventive custody .

While the government has transferred powers to KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, the PTI has asserted that Afridi “remains and shall continue” to serve as the KP chief minister with the “confidence and support” of party founder and ex-premier Imran Khan.

National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas jointly filed a petition before the FCC.

The petition sought the enforcement of fundamental rights and constitutional protections against the alleged unlawful arrest, detention and confinement of Afridi, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, Fazal Shakoor Khan, Dr Amjad Ali, Sultan Room, Yameen Khan, Abdus Salam Afridi, Muhammad Azam Khan and Ikram Ghazi, as well as six members of the National Assembly — Junaid Akbar Khan, Dr Amjad Ali Khan, Iqbal Khan Afridi, Fazal Mohammad Khan, Zubair Wazir and Maulana Naseem Ali Shah.

The petition said it raised substantial questions of public importance concerning the supremacy of the Constitution, the sanctity of the democratic mandate, constitutional limits on executive authority under Articles 232, 234 and 245, and the protection of fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 4, 9, 10, 14, 17 and 19-A of the Constitution.

The petition also sought disclosure of the places of detention, production of the alleged detainees before the FCC, a declaration that their custody was unlawful and without lawful authority, and appropriate constitutional relief in the interest of justice and the rule of law.

The federal secretaries of interior and defence, the KP chief secretary, the secretary of the KP Home and Tribal Affairs Department, the provincial inspector general of police, the Peshawar capital city police officer, the Peshawar deputy commissioner and the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) director general were named as respondents.

The petition raised the question of whether the constitutional mandate conferred upon members of the National Assembly and provincial assemblies through the electoral process carried with it enforceable constitutional protection against arbitrary state action designed to obstruct, frustrate or undermine their participation in representative governance.

“Whether the arrest, intimidation, coercive restraint or other unlawful interference with elected legislators, in circumstances affecting their ability to represent their respective constituencies, amounts to an indirect disenfranchisement of the electorate and an impairment of the constitutional scheme of representative democracy?” it stated.

The petition questioned the selective or collective targeting of elected representatives on account of their political affiliation, parliamentary position or participation in opposition politics and contended that these constitute discriminatory treatment, political victimisation and an abuse of public authority contrary to Articles 4, 14, 17 and 25 of the Constitution.

It also prayed that the FCC declare that the Constitution was the supreme law of the land and that no proclamation of emergency, assumption of provincial executive authority, deployment of the armed forces or other extraordinary governmental measure could confer upon any state authority unfettered power to disregard fundamental rights, constitutional safeguards or the democratic mandate of the people.

The petition further requested the court to declare that the “liberty, dignity, political association and representative functions of elected members were constitutionally protected, and that any arrest, detention, confinement, restriction of movement or coercive action against them was unlawful, unconstitutional and without legal effect”.

“Moreover, the electoral mandate of the affected elected representatives cannot be defeated, neutralised or rendered ineffective through arbitrary executive action, political victimisation or the misuse of state machinery.

“The people of KP are constitutionally entitled to effective representation through their duly elected representatives.”

It also requested the FCC to order the production before the court of the members in custody. It further pleaded that Articles 232, 234 and 245 of the Constitution must be exercised strictly within their respective constitutional parameters and cannot be invoked to justify the suppression of political dissent, disabling of elected representatives, interference with parliamentary functions or circumvention of the fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution.

The petition argued that the exercise of executive and administrative authority under governor’s rule does not suspend the constitutional obligations of the state, displace the supremacy of fundamental rights or place the actions of public functionaries beyond the scrutiny of the FCC.

On Thursday, PTI lawmaker Shandana Gulzar also approached the FCC, seeking the immediate release of Afrid, the provincial assembly speaker and other party workers.

The petition requested the FCC to order the respondents to “immediately disclose before the court their whereabouts, the identity of the authority exercising custody, the legal instrument and statutory provisions invoked as well as the grounds of detention and the date and circumstances of their taking into custody”.

It further urged the court to order the production of the PTI’s provincial leadership in person so that their present condition, liberty and legal status be ascertained and the “legality of any such restraint upon their liberty be examined judicially”.

World.title: US air travel resumption will 'take time' after hours-long stop
World.content:
Flights in the United States were resuming on Saturday after being grounded for several hours due to a major communications outage, though authorities said returning to normal operations would take time.

The nationwide stop sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events.

Government officials said the incident was a major communications outage caused by decades old technology.

The incident marked only the second time such an alert had been issued in US airspace since the 9/11 attacks.

Federal Aviation Authority officials lifted the groundstop after around four hours, with President Donald Trump’s administration saying there was no evidence the outage was the result of foul play.

“This is a legacy system problem,” said Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy. “We have old, old switches, old routers.

“We use 1980s little copper lines. It’s an old system that went down, and went down everywhere. It got overloaded.”

Duffy on Thursday had formally asked Congress for $30.1 billion in funds to upgrade and modernise the US Air Traffic Control System.

As the groundstop was lifted he repeated his plea.

“I’m going to say it a million times: the Congress has to give the resources to the president so he can finish this bill,” he said.

6,000 flights canceled

With almost 6,000 flights canceled including some international routes according to FlightAware, the recovery from the stoppage was expected to take some time.

Footage from airports around the country showed gates full, with planes waiting on taxiways.

Passengers thronged concorses, desperate for information about an outage that had thrown their travel plans into chaos.

“We’re trying to debate whether or not we need to reschedule or drive or what, but if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too,” said Joseph Anderson, 72, who was trying to fly from Las Vegas to Oakland, California.

US airspace is among the busiest in the world, and is ramping up to its most frenetic as the Thanksgiving holiday moves into view.

A nationwide groundstop is highly unusual; there was one such stop in January 2023 when a pilot notification system failed, but the only other national stop happened in the wake of the 9/11 attacks, when no aircraft took to the skies for days.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin stressed there was no evidence of any hostile action on Friday.

“We’ve seen zero evidence that this was a cyber attack or (AI) attack,” he told a press conference.

He also ruled out any connection with the outage that affected Microsoft this week, knocking email systems offline for millions of users, public services and businesses worldwide.

Confusion and delays

The stop sparked chaos and misery at airports around the country.

At New York’s LaGuardia Airport, Tiara Johnson said she had been trying to get to Orlando for a concert with a friend.

“They just keep delaying it…So it started out at 7:55. Then it went to 8:30, 9:30. Now it’s at 10:30. So we don’t know when it’s gonna leave,” she told AFP.

“I feel very frustrated because you know, you come to the airport and then all of a sudden your whole plans have changed and you don’t know when you’re leaving. We’re kind of stuck.”

Travelers were left in the dark on the groundstop, with some saying they had been told their flight was delayed because of wind, while others were left to gather what information they could.

Boards at the airport continued to show departures leaving as normal, while mobile boarding passes held by those stuck on the ground appeared to show their flight was underway.

Stranded passengers were scrambling to find alternatives, with long lines forming at rental car counters at the airport in Las Vegas.

Susan Sardina said she had boarded her flight back to Orange County, California when staff told passengers there was a problem.

“We were already on our flight to leave and we were told to get off,” she told AFP as she stood in a lengthy queue for a rental car.

For those looking on the bright side, the delay was a chance to extend a break.

Kathy Sommers was on her way home from visiting friends in Las Vegas when her flight got canceled.

“We’re blessed that our friends are coming back to pick us up,” she said. “So one more night to play cards.”

World.title: Pakistan to host 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting on Nov 15-16
World.content:
The 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) Council of Ministers will be held in Islamabad on Nov 15 and 16, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday.

The meeting will be chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and attended by foreign ministers and heads of delegations from ECO member states, along with representatives of the organisation’s secretariat and subsidiary bodies, the FO said in a statement.

The ministerial meeting will be preceded by a meeting of senior officials of ECO member states, which will review the organisation’s activities and programmes, assess the work of its subsidiary bodies and finalise the agenda and draft outcome documents for consideration by the ministers.

Pakistan, which holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27, will seek to advance the organisation’s objectives under the theme “Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO”, the FO said.

It said Pakistan’s chairmanship would focus on strengthening regional connectivity and integration, deepening partnerships and promoting collective efforts for economic prosperity and sustainable development.

The chairmanship would also provide an opportunity to strengthen the ECO’s role as a platform for regional cooperation, dialogue and economic collaboration, it added.

According to the FO, Pakistan also aims to position itself as a regional connectivity hub, facilitate logistics supply chains and help shape the agenda for regional trade.

The efforts would help unlock the region’s economic potential and translate the benefits of regional cooperation into tangible improvements in the lives of people in ECO member states, the statement said.

In a post on X, Dar welcomed the delegates arriving for the meeting.

“I look forward to productive deliberations as we work together to strengthen regional cooperation and advance our shared priorities. Wishing all delegates a productive and memorable stay in Islamabad,” he said.

Meanwhile, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus Tahsin Ertuğruloğlu arrived in Islamabad to participate in the meeting. He was received at the airport by officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Last month DPM Dar directed relevant authorities to ensure flawless coordination and timely preparations for the ECO meeting, underscoring the deep importance Pakistan attaches to the regional bloc.

The 17th ECO Summit was held in Azerbaijan’s Khankendi on July 3-4, 2025, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif leading Pakistan’s delegation. The summit brought together heads of state and government from member countries to discuss regional cooperation and economic integration.

During the summit, Pakistan called for enhanced intra-regional trade, transport connectivity, energy cooperation and sustainable development, while reaffirming its commitment to the ECO Vision 2025.

World.title: Wasim Akram questions Cummins’ Sandpapergate denial, says bowlers would spot tampering
World.content:
Pakistan pace legend Wasim Akram has questioned Australia captain Pat Cummins’ claim that he was unaware of the use of sandpaper during the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa, arguing that any experienced bowler would immediately recognise the difference between natural wear and deliberate damage to the ball.

Speaking in a video posted on social media on Saturday from Melbourne, Wasim said the marks left by sandpaper were distinctly different from those caused by normal contact with the ground.

“As a bowler, I’ll have a look at the ball and know straight away something is not right,” Wasim said.

“He said he didn’t know (about the use of sandpaper). As a bowler, when the cricket ball comes into my hand, whether it’s the fifth over, the tenth over or the fiftieth over, you look after the ball, you shine one side of the ball. But the sandpaper scratch is totally different than the one-bounce scratch.”

Wasim suggested that the difference could easily be identified through a simple comparison, saying anyone could take a semi-new ball, rub sandpaper against it and observe the resulting marks.

The former Pakistan captain, widely regarded as one of the finest exponents of reverse swing, described Cummins as “a very close friend” and insisted he was not taking sides in the controversy, which has resurfaced following revelations by former Australia opener Usman Khawaja in his autobiography Sabr.

Khawaja alleged that knowledge of the ball-tampering plan was widespread within the Australian dressing room, including among the bowling group, during the 2018 tour of South Africa.

At the time, Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball during the third Test at Newlands in Cape Town. Then-captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and Bancroft subsequently received suspensions, while Cricket Australia undertook a wider cultural review.

Cummins, however, rejected Khawaja’s allegations during a lengthy press conference in Sydney on Friday, describing them as “100 per cent wrong” and “complete and utter nonsense”.

The Australia captain maintained that he had no knowledge of sandpaper being taken onto the field and denied being an architect of the ball-tampering scheme. He also said he was genuinely shocked to learn that Khawaja had warned Bancroft to be careful while using the sandpaper.

Wasim said the controversy had also raised wider questions about Australia’s reputation for honesty and sportsmanship.

“Australians are famous for their straightforwardness, their hardness on the field and off the field, and most importantly honesty. I think that’s why the whole nation has been under stress a bit,” he said.

“I hope things get sorted out, but this is my take.”

Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening its investigation into the 2018 scandal despite the fresh allegations.

Wasim’s intervention, however, has added further weight to a debate that continues to divide opinion over what players knew during one of the most damaging episodes in Australian cricket.

More than eight years after the Newlands incident, the renewed controversy has once again put the Australian team’s conduct and the credibility of its account of events under scrutiny.

World.title: Police foil attack on checkpost in KP's Bannu, eliminate four terrorists
World.content:
BANNU: Police foiled a terrorist attack on Kingar Pul Police Checkpost in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bannu district on Friday night, eliminating four terrorists in retaliation, a police spokesperson said.

According to the police spokesperson, heavily armed terrorists launched a sudden attack on the checkpost last night.

“However, police personnel deployed at the checkpost responded promptly and successfully repelled the assault,” he stated.

Following the incident, the Rapid Response Force (RRF) and additional police personnel were rushed from Police Lines to the scene. They cordoned off the area and launched a clearance and search operation, the spokesperson added.

“During the operation, the bodies of four terrorists were recovered,” he added.

The spokesperson said that police also seized four Kalashnikov rifles, several magazines, a substantial quantity of ammunition, hand grenades and bandoliers, adding that the identification of the slain terrorists was underway.

Meanwhile, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed commended Bannu Police for foiling the attack.

He said successfully repelling the assault under the cover of darkness reflected the high level of training, vigilance and bravery of police personnel.

The IG added that effective operations were underway under a comprehensive strategy to eliminate terrorism and rid the province of the menace.

“Protecting the lives and property of the public remains the top priority of the police,” IG Hameed said.

Yesterday, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that the security forces had killed 74 terrorists during intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in KP and Balochistan.

Two days ago, terrorists also attacked Bandkorai Police Station in Dera Ismail Khan by ramming an explosives-laden pickup into its main gate, triggering a powerful blast followed by intense gunfire.

However, prompt retaliatory fire by police personnel prevented the attackers from entering the police station, forcing them to flee.

On the same day, however, two policemen, including an assistant sub-inspector (ASI), were martyred in Swabi when three suspects opened fire on a patrolling party.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.

If Bangladesh had 30–40 percent of the grid powered by solar, along with solar-powered EVs, the country would be far less exposed to global fuel market shocks. Long fuel lines, online schooling, shorter office hours, and industrial disruption could be reduced. Solar, storage, and EVs should now be planned together.

Finance will decide how fast this transition happens. Renewable energy projects cannot grow at interest rates below 10–12 percent. Long-term financing should be available at an interest rate of 3.5–4.5 percent. A 10–15-year financing facility at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent should be introduced.
